statement: Independent research and development and bid and proposal project cost consists of all allocable costs except business unit general and administrative expense.
quote: The IR&D and B&P project costs shall consist of all allocable costs, except business unit general and administrative expenses.

statement: A home office's independent research and development and bid and proposal pools are allocated to segments on the basis of beneficial or causal relationship.
quote: The IR&D and B&P cost pools of a home office shall be allocated to segments on the basis of the beneficial or causal relationship between the IR&D and B&P costs and the segments reporting to that home office.

statement: A business unit's independent research and development and bid and proposal pools are allocated to that unit's final cost objectives on the basis of beneficial or causal relationship.
quote: allocated to the final cost objectives of that business unit on the basis of the beneficial or causal relationship between the IR&D and B&P costs and the final cost objectives

statement: Bid and proposal cost incurred in a cost accounting period is not assigned to any other cost accounting period.
quote: The B&P costs incurred in a cost accounting period shall not be assigned to any other cost accounting period.

statement: Independent research and development cost is not assigned to another period either, except as existing laws, regulations and other controlling factors permit.
quote: The IR&D costs incurred in a cost accounting period shall not be assigned to any other cost accounting period, except as may be permitted pursuant to provisions of existing laws, regulations, and other controlling factors.

statement: Records include books, documents, accounting procedures and practices, and other data, regardless of type or form.
quote: records includes books, documents, accounting procedures and practices, and other data, regardless of type and regardless of whether such items are in written form, in the form of computer data, or in any other form.

statement: The cost-examination provision covers cost-reimbursement, incentive, time-and-materials, labor-hour, and price redeterminable contracts, including combinations of those types.
quote: If this is a cost-reimbursement, incentive, time-and-materials, labor-hour, or price redeterminable contract, or any combination of these,

statement: For covered contracts, the contractor must maintain records and other evidence sufficient to reflect properly costs claimed to have been incurred, and the Contracting Officer or an authorized representative may examine and audit them.
quote: the Contractor shall maintain and the Contracting Officer, or an authorized representative of the Contracting Officer, shall have the right to examine and audit all records and other evidence sufficient to reflect properly all costs claimed to have been incurred

statement: The examination right includes inspection at all reasonable times of the contractor's plants, or parts of them, engaged in performing the contract.
quote: This right of examination shall include inspection at all reasonable times of the Contractor's plants, or parts of them, engaged in performing the contract.

statement: When certified cost or pricing data has been required, the examination and audit right covers related contractor records, including computations and projections, to evaluate accuracy, completeness, and currency.
quote: in order to evaluate the accuracy, completeness, and currency of the certified cost or pricing data, shall have the right to examine and audit all of the Contractor's records, including computations and projections

statement: Unless the contract is exempt under the cited CAS exemption provisions, the clause incorporates the CAS contract requirements by reference.
quote: Unless the contract is exempt under 48 CFR 9903.201-1 and 9903.201-2, the provisions of 48 CFR part 9903 are incorporated herein by reference

statement: Under the clause, a contractor on a CAS-covered contract discloses its cost accounting practices in a Disclosure Statement as required by 48 CFR 9903.202-1 through 9903.202-5, including methods of distinguishing direct costs from indirect costs and the basis used for allocating indirect costs.
quote: By submission of a Disclosure Statement, disclose in writing the Contractor's cost accounting practices as required by 48 CFR 9903.202-1 through 9903.202-5, including methods of distinguishing direct costs from indirect costs and the basis used for allocating indirect costs.

statement: The contractor must follow its cost accounting practices consistently in accumulating and reporting contract performance cost data for the contract.
quote: Follow consistently the Contractor's cost accounting practices in accumulating and reporting contract performance cost data concerning this contract.

statement: A change in cost accounting practices for a contract or subcontract subject to CAS requirements must be applied prospectively, and the Disclosure Statement must be amended accordingly.
quote: If any change in cost accounting practices is made for the purposes of any contract or subcontract subject to CAS requirements, the change must be applied prospectively to this contract and the Disclosure Statement must be amended accordingly.

statement: If the Contractor has notified the Contracting Officer that the Disclosure Statement contains trade secrets and commercial or financial information that is privileged and confidential, the Disclosure Statement must be protected and must not be released outside the Government.
quote: If the Contractor has notified the Contracting Officer that the Disclosure Statement contains trade secrets and commercial or financial information which is privileged and confidential, the Disclosure Statement shall be protected and shall not be released outside of the Government.

statement: For administering CAS requirements under the contract, the contractor must take the steps outlined in paragraphs (b) through (i) and (k) through (n) of the clause.
quote: For the purpose of administering the Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) requirements under this contract, the Contractor shall take the steps outlined in paragraphs (b) through (i) and (k) through (n) of this clause

statement: An affected CAS-covered contract or subcontract includes one where one practice was used to estimate costs and a changed practice was used to accumulate and report costs.
quote: Used one cost accounting practice to estimate costs and a changed cost accounting practice to accumulate and report costs under the contract or subcontract

statement: An affected CAS-covered contract or subcontract also includes one where a noncompliant practice was used for estimating or accumulating and reporting costs.
quote: Used a noncompliant practice for purposes of estimating or accumulating and reporting costs under the contract or subcontract

statement: The cognizant Federal agency official is the Contracting Officer assigned by the cognizant Federal agency to administer CAS.
quote: Cognizant Federal agency official (CFAO) means the Contracting Officer assigned by the cognizant Federal agency to administer the CAS.

statement: A desirable change is a compliant change to established or disclosed cost accounting practices that the cognizant Federal agency official finds desirable and not detrimental to the Government.
quote: Desirable change means a compliant change to a Contractor's established or disclosed cost accounting practices that the CFAO finds is desirable and not detrimental to the Government

statement: At any time during performance of a contract of a type referred to in 42.802, the cognizant contracting officer responsible for administering the contract may issue the contractor a written notice of intent to disallow specified costs incurred or planned for incurrence.
quote: (a) At any time during the performance of a contract of a type referred to in 42.802, the cognizant contracting officer responsible for administering the contract may issue the contractor a written notice of intent to disallow specified costs incurred or planned for incurrence.

statement: Before issuing the notice of intent to disallow costs, the contracting officer responsible for administering the contract must make every reasonable effort to reach a satisfactory settlement through discussions with the contractor.
quote: before issuing the notice, the contracting officer responsible for administering the contract shall make every reasonable effort to reach a satisfactory settlement through discussions with the contractor.

statement: A written response to a notice of intent to disallow costs is answered by withdrawal of the notice or by a written decision within 60 days.
quote: Any such response shall be answered by withdrawal of the notice or by making a written decision within 60 days.

statement: Cost-reimbursement contracts, the cost-reimbursement portion of fixed-price contracts, letter contracts that provide for reimbursement of costs, and time-and-material and labor-hour contracts provide for disallowing costs during performance after the costs have been incurred.
quote: Cost-reimbursement contracts, the cost-reimbursement portion of fixed-price contracts, letter contracts that provide for reimbursement of costs, and time-and-material and labor-hour contracts provide for disallowing costs during the course of performance after the costs have been incurred.

statement: If examination of a voucher raises a question about the allowability of a cost under the contract terms, the auditor, after informal discussion as appropriate and where authorized by agency regulations, may issue a notice of contract costs suspended and/or disapproved.
quote: (2) If the examination of a voucher raises a question regarding the allowability of a cost under the contract terms, the auditor, after informal discussion as appropriate, may, where authorized by agency regulations, issue a notice of contract costs suspended and/or disapproved

statement: If the contractor disagrees with the deduction from current payments, it may submit a written request to the cognizant contracting officer to consider whether the unreimbursed costs should be paid, or file a claim under the Disputes clause.
quote: (i) Submit a written request to the cognizant contracting officer to consider whether the unreimbursed costs should be paid and to discuss the findings with the contractor; (ii) File a claim under the Disputes clause

statement: A contractor must maintain an accounting system when it receives a cost-reimbursement, incentive type, time-and-materials or labor-hour contract, or a contract that provides for progress payments based on costs or on a percentage or stage of completion.
quote: Contractors receiving cost-reimbursement, incentive type, time-and-materials, or labor-hour contracts, or contracts which provide for progress payments based on costs or on a percentage or stage of completion, shall maintain an accounting system.

statement: When judging whether an accounting system is acceptable, the contracting officer, in consultation with the auditor or functional specialist, determines whether the system complies with the system criteria.
quote: the contracting officer, in consultation with the auditor or functional specialist, shall determine whether the contractor's accounting system complies with the system criteria

statement: The contracting officer requests that the contractor respond in writing to an initial determination within 30 days.
quote: Request the contractor to respond, in writing, to the initial determination within 30 days

statement: As one of the actions the contracting officer takes in the final determination notice where material weaknesses remain, the contracting officer requests that the contractor, within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate them.
quote: Request that the contractor, within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the weaknesses

statement: As another of the actions the contracting officer takes where material weaknesses remain after the final determination, the contracting officer withholds payments in accordance with the Contractor Business Systems clause at 252.242-7005 if that clause is included in the contract.
quote: Withhold payments in accordance with the clause at 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, if the clause is included in the contract

statement: The contracting officer promptly approves a previously disapproved accounting system and notifies the contractor once there are no remaining material weaknesses.
quote: The contracting officer shall promptly approve a previously disapproved accounting system and notify the contractor when the contracting officer determines that there are no remaining material weaknesses

statement: Under the cost principles subpart, a contingency is a possible future event or condition arising from presently known or unknown causes, whose outcome is indeterminable at the present time.
quote: Contingency, as used in this subpart, means a possible future event or condition arising from presently known or unknown causes, the outcome of which is indeterminable at the present time.

statement: Costs for contingencies are generally unallowable for historical costing purposes, because that costing deals with costs incurred and recorded on the contractor's books.
quote: Costs for contingencies are generally unallowable for historical costing purposes because such costing deals with costs incurred and recorded on the contractor's books.
note: Paragraph (b) also keeps a narrow past-period recognition, covered by CL-CMP-0753.

statement: In some cases, such as terminations, a contingency factor may be recognized when it applies to a past period, to give recognition to minor unsettled factors and expedite settlement.
quote: However, in some cases, as for example, terminations, a contingency factor may be recognized when it is applicable to a past period to give recognition to minor unsettled factors in the interest of expediting settlement.

statement: Contingencies of the first category described in FAR 31.205-7(c) are to be included in the estimates of future costs so as to provide the best estimate of performance cost.
quote: Contingencies of this category are to be included in the estimates of future costs so as to provide the best estimate of performance cost.

statement: Contingencies of the second category described in FAR 31.205-7(c) are to be excluded from cost estimates under the several items of cost, but should be disclosed separately, including the basis upon which the contingency is computed, to facilitate the negotiation of appropriate contractual coverage.
quote: Contingencies of this category are to be excluded from cost estimates under the several items of cost, but should be disclosed separately (including the basis upon which the contingency is computed) to facilitate the negotiation of appropriate contractual coverage.
note: The disclosure is meant to let appropriate contractual coverage be negotiated.

statement: Cost of money is an imputed cost and is not a form of interest on borrowings.
quote: an imputed cost that is not a form of interest on borrowings

statement: Cost of money counts as an incurred cost for cost-reimbursement purposes under applicable cost-reimbursement contracts and for progress payment purposes under fixed-price contracts.
quote: Is an “incurred cost” for cost-reimbursement purposes under applicable cost-reimbursement contracts and for progress payment purposes under fixed-price contracts

statement: Cost of money refers to facilities capital cost of money and to cost of money as an element of the cost of capital assets under construction, each under its own cost accounting standard.
quote: Refers to— (i) Facilities capital cost of money (48 CFR 9904.414); and (ii) Cost of money as an element of the cost of capital assets under construction (48 CFR 9904.417).

statement: Cost of money is allowable only where it is measured, assigned and allocated to contracts under the facilities capital standard, or measured and added to the cost of capital assets under construction under the capital asset standard.
quote: It is measured, assigned, and allocated to contracts in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.414 or measured and added to the cost of capital assets under construction in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.417, as applicable

statement: Cost of money is allowable only if the separate provision that limits the allowability of cost of money is followed.
quote: The requirements of 31.205-52, which limit the allowability of cost of money, are followed

statement: Cost of money is allowable only where the estimated facilities capital cost of money is specifically identified and proposed in the cost proposals for the contract under which it is claimed.
quote: The estimated facilities capital cost of money is specifically identified and proposed in cost proposals relating to the contract under which the cost is to be claimed

statement: Actual interest cost in lieu of the calculated imputed cost of money is unallowable.
quote: Actual interest cost in lieu of the calculated imputed cost of money is unallowable.

statement: Idle capacity is the unused capacity of partially used facilities.
quote: Idle capacity means the unused capacity of partially used facilities.

statement: The measurement of idle capacity starts from what a facility could achieve under 100 percent operating time on a one-shift basis.
quote: It is the difference between that which a facility could achieve under 100 percent operating time on a one-shift basis

statement: A multiple-shift basis may be used in the calculation instead of a one-shift basis if it can be shown that this amount of usage could normally be expected for the type of facility involved.
quote: A multiple-shift basis may be used in the calculation instead of a one-shift basis if it can be shown that this amount of usage could normally be expected for the type of facility involved.

statement: Idle facilities are completely unused facilities that are excess to the contractor's current needs.
quote: Idle facilities means completely unused facilities that are excess to the contractor's current needs.

statement: Costs of idle facilities are unallowable unless the facilities meet one of two listed conditions; the first is that they are necessary to meet fluctuations in workload.
quote: (b) The costs of idle facilities are unallowable unless the facilities— (1) Are necessary to meet fluctuations in workload; or (2)

statement: The second condition under which costs of idle facilities are not unallowable is that the facilities were necessary when acquired and are now idle because of changes in requirements, production economies, reorganization, termination, or other causes which could not have been reasonably foreseen.
quote: or (2) Were necessary when acquired and are now idle because of changes in requirements, production economies, reorganization, termination, or other causes which could not have been reasonably foreseen.

statement: A parenthetical that follows the two exceptions provides that costs of idle facilities are allowable for a reasonable period, ordinarily not to exceed 1 year, depending upon the initiative taken to use, lease, or dispose of the idle facilities.
quote: or other causes which could not have been reasonably foreseen. (Costs of idle facilities are allowable for a reasonable period, ordinarily not to exceed 1 year, depending upon the initiative taken to use, lease, or dispose of the idle facilities (but see 31.205-42)).

statement: Costs of idle capacity are allowable provided the capacity is necessary or was originally reasonable and is not subject to reduction or elimination by subletting, renting or sale, in accordance with sound business, economics or security practices.
quote: Such costs are allowable provided the capacity is necessary or was originally reasonable and is not subject to reduction or elimination by subletting, renting, or sale, in accordance with sound business, economics, or security practices.

statement: Widespread idle capacity throughout an entire plant, or among a group of assets having substantially the same function, may be idle facilities.
quote: Widespread idle capacity throughout an entire plant or among a group of assets having substantially the same function may be idle facilities.

statement: Costs to be paid directly by the Government for idle facilities or idle capacity reserved for defense mobilization production must be the subject of a separate agreement.
quote: Any costs to be paid directly by the Government for idle facilities or idle capacity reserved for defense mobilization production shall be the subject of a separate agreement.

statement: Selling is a generic term encompassing all efforts to market the contractor's products or services, some of which are covered specifically in other subsections of the cost principles.
quote: “Selling” is a generic term encompassing all efforts to market the contractor's products or services, some of which are covered specifically in other subsections of 31.205

statement: The costs of any selling efforts other than those addressed in the selling cost principle are unallowable.
quote: The costs of any selling efforts other than those addressed in this cost principle are unallowable.

statement: Direct selling efforts are acts or actions to induce particular customers to purchase particular products or services of the contractor, and are characterized by person-to-person contact.
quote: (5) Direct selling. Direct selling efforts are those acts or actions to induce particular customers to purchase particular products or services of the contractor. Direct selling is characterized by person-to-person contact

statement: The cost of direct selling efforts is allowable.
quote: for a particular customer's use. The cost of direct selling efforts is allowable.

statement: Long-range market planning costs are subject to a separate allowability provision, while other market planning costs are allowable.
quote: Long-range market planning costs are subject to the allowability provisions of 31.205-12. Other market planning costs are allowable.

statement: Whether or not contingent upon the award of contracts, the payments covered by FAR 31.205-38(c) are allowable only when paid to bona fide employees or established commercial or selling agencies maintained by the contractor for the purpose of securing business.
quote: whether or not contingent upon the award of contracts, are allowable only when paid to bona fide employees or established commercial or selling agencies maintained by the contractor for the purpose of securing business.

statement: Bid and proposal costs are defined in another subsection and are subject to the allowability provisions of that subsection.
quote: Bid and proposal costs are defined at 31.205-18 and are subject to the allowability provisions of that subsection.

statement: Federal, State and local taxes are allowable except as otherwise provided in the paragraph listing unallowable taxes, where they are required to be and are paid or accrued in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.
quote: (a) The following types of costs are allowable: (1) Federal, State, and local taxes (see part 29), except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) below that are required to be and are paid or accrued in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.

statement: Fines and penalties are not considered taxes.
quote: in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Fines and penalties are not considered taxes.

statement: Federal income and excess profits taxes are not allowable.
quote: The following types of costs are not allowable: (1) Federal income and excess profits taxes.

statement: Taxes in connection with financing, refinancing, refunding operations or reorganizations are not allowable.
quote: (b) The following types of costs are not allowable: (1) Federal income and excess profits taxes. (2) Taxes in connection with financing, refinancing, refunding operations, or reorganizations (see 31.205-20 and 31.205-27).

statement: Taxes from which exemptions are available to the contractor directly, or available to the contractor based on an exemption afforded the Government, are among the types of costs listed in paragraph (b) of the taxes principle.
quote: (3) Taxes from which exemptions are available to the contractor directly, or available to the contractor based on an exemption afforded the Government
note: The exclusion gives way under the contracting officer determination covered by CL-CMP-0788.

statement: The Environmental Tax found at section 59A of the Internal Revenue Code, also called the Superfund Tax, is among the types of costs listed in paragraph (a) of the taxes principle.
quote: (4) The Environmental Tax found at section 59A of the Internal Revenue Code, also called the “Superfund Tax.”

statement: Taxes, interest or penalties that were allowed as contract costs and are refunded to the contractor must be credited or paid to the Government in the manner it directs.
quote: Any taxes, interest, or penalties that were allowed as contract costs and are refunded to the contractor shall be credited or paid to the Government in the manner it directs.

statement: Taxes on property used in both Government and non-Government work are apportioned to all such work based on the use of the property on the respective final cost objectives.
quote: The cost of taxes incurred on property used in both Government and non-Government work shall be apportioned to all such work based upon the use of such property on the respective final cost objectives.

statement: The exemption-based exclusion does not apply when the contracting officer determines that the administrative burden of obtaining the exemption outweighs the corresponding benefits accruing to the Government.
quote: except when the contracting officer determines that the administrative burden incident to obtaining the exemption outweighs the corresponding benefits accruing to the Government

statement: Precontract costs are costs incurred before the effective date of the contract directly pursuant to negotiations and in anticipation of award when necessary to comply with the proposed delivery schedule.
quote: Precontract costs means costs incurred before the effective date of the contract directly pursuant to the negotiation and in anticipation of the contract award when such incurrence is necessary to comply with the proposed contract delivery schedule.

statement: Precontract costs are allowable to the extent that they would have been allowable if incurred after the date of the contract.
quote: These costs are allowable to the extent that they would have been allowable if incurred after the date of the contract (see 31.109).

statement: Subject to the limits on help-wanted advertising, costs of help-wanted advertising and costs of operating an employment office needed to secure and maintain an adequate labor force are allowable recruitment costs.
quote: Subject to paragraph (b) of this subsection, the following costs are allowable: (1) Costs of help-wanted advertising. (2) Costs of operating an employment office needed to secure and maintain an adequate labor force.

statement: The manual's table pairs a material weakness with a generally adverse opinion, a system deficiency with a generally qualified opinion, and a less than material noncompliance that warrants the attention of those charged with governance with a generally unqualified opinion.

statement: The deficiency reporting the manual requires includes both material weaknesses and internal control deficiencies that, while less than material, still warrant the attention of the contractor and the contracting officer.
quote: This includes reporting both material weaknesses and internal control deficiencies that, while less than material, still warrant the attention of the contractor and the contracting officer.

statement: Because a deficiency assignment is part of the primary engagement, auditors do not duplicate procedural documentation such as risk assessments in the deficiency working papers.
quote: Because it is part of the primary engagement, auditors do not need to duplicate procedural documentation, such as risk assessments, within the deficiency assignment working papers.

statement: To maintain a clear audit trail, both the primary examination report and the deficiency report must cross-reference each other and explicitly state that the deficiency report is a component of the original engagement.
quote: Finally, to maintain a clear audit trail, both the primary examination report and the deficiency report must cross-reference each other and explicitly state that the deficiency report is a component of the original engagement

statement: Reported issues found when examining contractors with covered contracts may result in payment withholding if the ACO makes a final determination to disapprove the business system under DFARS 252.242-7998.
quote: The reported issues found when examining contractors with “Covered contracts”, may be subject to withhold payments if the ACO makes a final determination to disapprove a contractor’s business system in accordance with the clause at DFARS 252.242-7998.

statement: The contracting officer has the sole discretion and authority to identify the covered contracts from which to withhold payments.
quote: The contracting officer has the sole discretion and authority to identify the covered contracts from which to withhold payments.

statement: The contracting officer has the sole authority to notify the contractor in writing of a determination to implement payment withholding under the Contractor Business Systems clause.
quote: The contracting officer has the sole authority to promptly notify the contractor, in writing, of the contracting officer’s determination to implement payment withholding in accordance with the clause at DFARS 252.242-7998, Contractor Business Systems.

statement: When the contractor notifies the contracting officer that deficiencies have been corrected, the contracting officer must request the auditor to review the corrections to determine whether the deficiencies have been resolved.
quote: When the contractor notifies the contracting officer that the contractor has corrected the deficiencies, the contracting officer shall request the auditor review the correction(s) to determine if the deficiencies have been resolved.

statement: Material weaknesses and system deficiencies are generally considered outstanding until the contractor corrects the deficiency and DCAA performs a follow-up audit finding the revised practices to be compliant.
quote: Material weaknesses and system deficiencies are generally considered outstanding until the contractor has corrected the deficiency and DCAA has performed a follow-up business system audit and found the revised business system practice(s) to be compliant

statement: The audit office should initiate a follow-up business system audit when the contractor notifies it, directly or through the contracting officer, that it has implemented the appropriate corrective actions and sufficient transactions or costs are readily available.
quote: FAOs should initiate a follow-up business system audit when the FAO is notified by the contractor (either directly or through the contracting officer) that it has implemented the appropriate corrective actions and sufficient transactions/costs are readily available

statement: The scope of the follow-up business system audit is limited to determining if the contractor corrected the previously reported deficiencies and the system complies with DFARS.
quote: The scope of the follow-up business system audit will be limited to determining if the contractor corrected the previously reported material weaknesses and/or system deficiencies and the system complies with DFARS.

statement: When the contractor has not changed its business system practices, a follow-up audit should not be performed.
quote: When the contractor has not changed its business system practices, a follow-up audit should not be performed.

statement: The audit office should notify the administrative contracting officer on a real-time basis of any revised business system practices determined to be noncompliant with DFARS requirements.
quote: The FAO should notify the ACO on a real-time basis of any revised business system practices that are determined to be noncompliant with the DFARS business system requirements.

statement: DCMA is cognizant over three of the six business systems defined by DFARS: Earned Value Management System, Contractor Purchasing System Administration, and Contractor Property Management System Administration.
quote: DCMA is cognizant over three of the six business systems as defined by DFARS 252.2427998: Earned Value Management System, Contractor Purchasing System Administration, and Contractor Property Management System Administration.

statement: The auditor's primary objective is to examine contractor cost representations, in whatever form they may be presented, and to express an opinion on those incurred costs.
quote: The auditor's primary objective is to examine contractor cost representations, in whatever form they may be presented (such as progress payments, incurred cost proposals, and termination claims), and to express an opinion as to whether such incurred costs are:

statement: The auditor expresses an opinion on whether incurred costs are allowable, reasonable, and allocable to the contract under FAR 31, and consistent with GAAP and applicable Cost Accounting Standards.
quote: Allowable, reasonable, and allocable to the contract under FAR 31; Consistent with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) applicable in the circumstances; and

statement: The auditor also evaluates whether incurred costs are not prohibited by the contract, by statute or regulation, or by previous agreement with or decision of the contracting officer.
quote: Not prohibited by the contract, by statute or regulation, or by previous agreement with, or decision of, the contracting officer.

statement: The discovery of fraud or other unlawful activity is not the primary audit objective, but audit work should be designed to provide reasonable assurance of detecting abuse or illegal acts that could significantly affect the audit objective.
quote: The discovery of fraud or other unlawful activity is not the primary audit objective; however, audit work should be designed to provide reasonable assurance of detecting abuse or illegal acts that could significantly affect the audit objective.

statement: If illegal activity is suspected during an incurred cost audit, the circumstances should be referred to investigative authorities.
quote: If illegal activity is suspected, the circumstances should be referred to investigative authorities.

statement: A single agency is responsible for establishing final indirect cost rates for each business unit under FAR 42.503-1.
quote: FAR 42.503-1 states that a single agency shall be responsible for establishing final indirect cost rates for each business unit.

statement: Incurred cost audits are usually performed on a contractor-wide basis by first evaluating management and financial systems and controls combined with transaction testing across all business activities.
quote: Incurred cost audits are usually performed on a contractor-wide basis. This approach recognizes the efficiency of first gaining an understanding of the adequacy of management and financial systems and controls combined with transaction testing across all business activities

statement: Periodic audits of relevant business systems establish an understanding of internal systems and controls to determine the nature and extent of transaction testing on incurred cost audits.
quote: Periodic audits of relevant business systems serve to develop an appropriate understanding of systems and controls necessary to determine the nature and extent of transaction testing needed on individual incurred cost audits.

statement: Separate audits of individual business systems may not be required for smaller contractors, whose internal controls may instead be evaluated during the final indirect cost audit or other contract audits.
quote: For smaller contractors, separate audits of individual contractor business systems may not be necessary. An understanding of the contractor's relevant internal controls may be gained at the time of the final indirect cost audit or during other contract audits.

statement: Auditing incurred costs at multi-segment contractors where a proposal covers multiple locations requires defining and coordinating audit responsibilities at each location to ensure appropriate coverage.
quote: Auditing incurred costs at multi-segment contractors where an incurred cost proposal covers more than one contractor location requires that audit responsibilities at each location be clearly defined and coordinated to ensure appropriate audit coverage

statement: If a non-DoW agency that granted significant awards is unwilling or unable to reimburse audit services, this situation may constitute a limitation on the audit scope.
quote: If the contractor has received a significant amount in Federal awards from a non-DoW agency, and the non-DoW agency is unwilling or unable to reimburse DCAA for its portion of DCAA’s incurred cost audit services, this may constitute a limitation on the scope of audit.

statement: Materiality refers to misstatements or omissions that could reasonably influence the decisions of users, encompassing qualitative and quantitative factors assessed through professional judgment.
quote: Materiality refers to misstatements or omissions, whether individually or combined, that could reasonably influence the decisions of intended users. It involves both qualitative and quantitative factors, and their significance in each engagement is determined by the auditor’s professional judgment.

statement: Auditors must design and perform procedures on all material balances to support the audit opinion, regardless of assessed risk.
quote: Auditors must design and perform procedures on all material balances to support their audit opinion, regardless of the assessed risk. However, risk assessment influences the nature, timing, and extent of these procedures.

statement: Qualitative risks may justify auditing amounts that fall below the quantitative materiality threshold.
quote: Additionally, qualitative risks may justify auditing amounts below the quantitative materiality threshold.

statement: Qualitative risk factors used to identify significant audit items must be supported by objective evidence, such as a history of questioned costs or documented concerns from the contracting officer.
quote: Qualitative or other risk factors used to identify significant items must be supported by objective evidence, such as a history of questioned costs or documented concerns from the contracting officer.

statement: Incurred cost proposals with a sampling auditable dollar volume of less than 100 million dollars are eligible for risk-based sampling unless an exception applies.
quote: Unless an exception applies, ICPs with the following Sampling ADV are eligible for sampling: a. Less than $100 million are eligible for sampling.

statement: Incurred cost proposals with a sampling auditable dollar volume of 1 billion dollars or greater are not eligible for sampling and are audited each year.
quote: e. $1 billion or greater are not eligible for sampling and will be audited each year.

statement: Incurred cost audits evaluate whether costs charged to Government contracts across major cost elements are necessary, comply with contract terms, and are allowable, allocable, and reasonable under FAR 31.
quote: Incurred cost audits encompass several major cost areas and cost elements, and include assessing and evaluating whether costs charged to Government contracts are necessary, comply with contract terms, and are allowable, allocable and reasonable and consistent with FAR 31

statement: Audit objectives for labor costs include verifying that costs are supported by proper timekeeping, payroll, and personnel records, and that internal controls over labor charging and allocation are adequate.
quote: (1) Labor Costs are supported by proper timekeeping, payroll, and personnel records, and internal controls over labor charging and allocation are adequate.

statement: Audit objectives for material costs include verifying that materials were received, used, and accounted for in accordance with contract terms and that related internal controls are adequate.
quote: (2) Materials were received, used, and accounted for in accordance with contract terms and internal controls over purchasing, receiving, inventory, and material issuance are adequate.

statement: Audit objectives for indirect costs include verifying that allocation methods and bases are acceptable, rate calculations are accurate and consistent, and internal controls are adequate.
quote: (3) Indirect cost methods and bases used to allocate indirect costs are acceptable, indirect cost rate calculations and the application of those rates are accurate and consistent, and internal controls over indirect cost charging and allocation are adequate.

statement: Audit objectives for other direct costs include verifying that costs are supported by adequate documentation and that internal controls over purchasing and cost charging are adequate.
quote: (4) Other Direct Costs are supported by adequate documentation and internal controls over purchasing and cost charging are adequate.

statement: Audit objectives for subcontract costs include verifying that costs are supported by appropriate documentation, comply with subcontract terms, and have adequate internal controls over subcontract administration.
quote: (5) Subcontract Costs are supported by appropriate documentation and comply with subcontract terms, internal controls over subcontract award, administration, and monitoring are adequate

statement: The administrative contracting officer determines whether to assess a penalty and issues a demand letter, while the auditor must communicate all unallowable costs potentially subject to penalties regardless of materiality.
quote: The Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO) determines whether a penalty should be assessed and issues a demand letter for the amount. The auditor is responsible for communicating all unallowable costs potentially subject to penalties to the ACO, regardless of materiality.

statement: The auditor has no authority to recommend or impose the penalty, recover it against subsequent public vouchers, or waive it; that authority rests with the administrative contracting officer.
quote: The auditor has no authority to recommend or impose the penalty, recover it against subsequent public vouchers, or waive the penalty. This authority rests with the ACO.

statement: A cost is expressly unallowable if the applicable cost principle states in direct terms that the cost is unallowable, leaving little room for interpretation.
quote: By definition, a cost is expressly unallowable if the applicable cost principle states in direct terms that the cost is unallowable, leaving little room for interpretation.

statement: The cognizant contracting officer is responsible for determining whether the penalties in 42.709-2(a) should be assessed and whether such penalties should be waived pursuant to 42.709-6.
quote: (a) The cognizant contracting officer is responsible for— (1) Determining whether the penalties in 42.709-2(a) should be assessed; (2) Determining whether such penalties should be waived pursuant to 42.709-6;

statement: The contract auditor is responsible for recommending to the contracting officer which costs may be unallowable and subject to penalties under FAR 42.709-2(a).
quote: The contract auditor, in the review and/or the determination of final indirect cost proposals for contracts subject to this section, is responsible for— (1) Recommending to the contracting officer which costs may be unallowable and subject to the penalties in 42.709-2(a);

statement: Under item (a) of FAR 42.709-4, the contracting officer assesses the penalty in 42.709-2(a)(1) when the submitted cost is expressly unallowable under a cost principle in the FAR or an executive agency supplement that defines the allowability of specific selected costs.
quote: (a) Assess the penalty in 42.709-2(a)(1), when the submitted cost is expressly unallowable under a cost principle in the FAR or an executive agency supplement that defines the allowability of specific selected costs;

statement: Under item (b) of FAR 42.709-4, the contracting officer assesses the penalty in 42.709-2(a)(2) when the submitted cost was determined to be unallowable for that contractor before the proposal was submitted.
quote: Assess the penalty in 42.709-2(a)(2), when the submitted cost was determined to be unallowable for that contractor prior to submission of the proposal.

statement: The contracting officer issues a final decision demanding payment of the assessed penalty and stating that the determination is a final decision under the Disputes clause.
quote: Issue a final decision (see 33.211) which includes a demand for payment of any penalty assessed under paragraph (a) or (b) of this section. The letter shall state that the determination is a final decision under the Disputes clause of the contract.

statement: Under FAR 42.709-5(a), the overpayment is considered to have occurred, and interest to have begun accumulating, from the midpoint of the contractor's fiscal year, and an alternate equitable method is used if the cost was not paid evenly over the fiscal year.
quote: (a) Consider the overpayment to have occurred, and interest to have begun accumulating, from the midpoint of the contractor's fiscal year. Use an alternate equitable method if the cost was not paid evenly over the fiscal year.

statement: Under FAR 42.709-5(c), interest is computed from the date of overpayment to the date of the demand letter for payment of the penalty.
quote: (c) Compute interest from the date of overpayment to the date of the demand letter for payment of the penalty.

statement: The contracting officer must waive penalties if the contractor withdraws the proposal before an audit is formally initiated and submits a revised proposal.
quote: The cognizant contracting officer shall waive the penalties at 42.709-2(a) when— (a) The contractor withdraws the proposal before the Government formally initiates an audit of the proposal and the contractor submits a revised proposal

statement: The contracting officer must waive penalties if the amount of unallowable costs under the proposal subject to penalty allocated to covered contracts is 10,000 dollars or less.
quote: (b) The amount of the unallowable costs under the proposal which are subject to the penalty is $10,000 or less (i.e., if the amount of expressly or previously determined unallowable costs which would be allocated to the contracts specified in 42.709-1(b) is $10,000 or less);

statement: The second showing under FAR 42.709-6(c), in addition to the first, is that the unallowable costs subject to the penalty were inadvertently incorporated into the proposal, meaning their inclusion resulted from an unintentional error notwithstanding the exercise of due care.
quote: and (2) The unallowable costs subject to the penalty were inadvertently incorporated into the proposal; i.e., their inclusion resulted from an unintentional error, notwithstanding the exercise of due care.

statement: Several types of DCAA audits and advisory services focus on testing for compliance with CAS requirements.
quote: several types of DCAA audits and advisory services focus on testing for compliance with CAS requirements
note: The printed source is a page of the DCAA Contract Audit Manual, agency audit guidance rather than a codified regulation.

statement: A Disclosure Statement compliance audit tests whether the cost accounting practices as described comply with CAS and FAR Part 31, and the manual places it after the CFAO has determined the Disclosure Statement is adequate.
quote: Initial and Revised CASB Disclosure Statement Compliance Audits (activity code 19100). After the CFAO has determined the Disclosure Statement is adequate, test whether the cost accounting practices, as described, comply with CAS and FAR Part 31.

statement: On the CFAO's request, technical assistance evaluates the adequacy of a contractor's cost accounting practice descriptions in its revised Disclosure Statement and the materiality of any related cost accounting practice changes.
quote: Technical Assistance to the CFAO (activity code 19190). Upon CFAO request, evaluate the adequacy of a contractor’s cost accounting practice descriptions in its revised CASB Disclosure Statement and materiality of any related cost accounting practice changes.

statement: In a CAS-specific compliance audit, the auditor reviews a contractor's estimating, accumulating and reporting cost accounting practices to see whether they match the descriptions of its disclosed practices and comply with a specific applicable standard.
quote: review a contractor’s estimating, accumulating, and reporting cost accounting practices to see if they match the descriptions of its disclosed practices and comply with a specific applicable Standard.

statement: Where a non-CAS audit finds a material CAS noncompliance, the details of the noncompliance are reported in a separate audit report.
quote: Upon finding a material CAS noncompliance in non-CAS audits, report the details of the noncompliance in a separate audit report.

statement: A cost impact proposal audit tests the contractor's proposed estimate of the cost impact to Government contracts of a practice change or a material noncompliance, expressed as a general dollar magnitude or a detailed cost impact.
quote: Audit the contractor’s proposed estimate (including a general dollar magnitude (GDM) or detailed cost impact (DCI)) of cost impact to Government contracts due to a contractor’s change to a cost accounting practice or material noncompliance with CAS.

statement: Contractors with fully CAS-covered contracts must complete, submit and maintain a Disclosure Statement.
quote: Contractors with fully CAS-covered contracts must complete, submit, and maintain a Disclosure Statement.

statement: The CAS and related CAS contract clauses require contractors with applicable CAS-covered contracts and subcontracts to comply with each applicable standard.
quote: The CAS, and related CAS contract clauses, require contractors with applicable CAScovered contracts and subcontracts to: • comply with each applicable Standard

statement: The head of an executive agency may waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards for a contract or subcontract with a value of less than $100 million if that official determines, in writing, certain facts about the business unit of the contractor or subcontractor that will perform the work; the facts are listed in the next paragraph of the section.
quote: The head of an executive agency may waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards for a contract or subcontract with a value of less than $100 million, if that official determines, in writing, that the business unit of the contractor or subcontractor that will perform the work—

statement: The written determination must be that the business unit that will perform the work is primarily engaged in the sale of commercial items and would not otherwise be subject to the Cost Accounting Standards under that chapter.
quote: that the business unit of the contractor or subcontractor that will perform the work— (1) Is primarily engaged in the sale of commercial items; and (2) Would not otherwise be subject to the Cost Accounting Standards under this Chapter.

statement: The head of an executive agency may waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards for a contract or subcontract under exceptional circumstances when necessary to meet the needs of the agency.
quote: The head of an executive agency may waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards for a contract or subcontract under exceptional circumstances when necessary to meet the needs of the agency.

statement: A determination to waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards by the agency head must be set forth in writing and must include a statement of the circumstances justifying the waiver.
quote: A determination to waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards by the agency head shall be set forth in writing, and shall include a statement of the circumstances justifying the waiver.

statement: The head of an executive agency may not delegate the waiver authority under paragraphs (a) and (b) of the section to any official below the senior policymaking level in the agency.
quote: The head of an executive agency may not delegate the authority under paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, to any official below the senior policymaking level in the agency.

statement: The head of each executive agency must report the waivers granted under paragraphs (a) and (b) to the Cost Accounting Standards Board on an annual basis, not later than 90 days after the close of the Government's fiscal year.
quote: The head of each executive agency shall report the waivers granted under paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, for that agency, to the Cost Accounting Standards Board, on an annual basis, not later than 90 days after the close of the Government's fiscal year.

statement: Upon request of an agency head or his designee, the Cost Accounting Standards Board may waive all or any part of the Cost Accounting Standards clause requirements, or of the disclosure and consistency of cost accounting practices requirements.
quote: Upon request of an agency head or his designee, the Cost Accounting Standards Board may waive all or any part of the requirements of 9903.201-4(a), Cost Accounting Standards, or 9903.201-4(c), Disclosure and Consistency of Cost Accounting Practices

statement: The requirements of part 9903 shall, to the maximum extent practicable, be administered by the cognizant Federal agency responsible for a particular contractor organization or location, usually the Federal agency responsible for negotiating indirect cost rates on behalf of the Government.
quote: The requirements of part 9903 shall, to the maximum extent practicable, be administered by the cognizant Federal agency responsible for a particular contractor organization or location, usually the Federal agency responsible for negotiating indirect cost rates on behalf of the Government.

statement: The cognizant Federal agency should take the lead role in administering the requirements of part 9903 and in coordinating CAS administrative actions with all affected Federal agencies.
quote: The cognizant Federal agency should take the lead role in administering the requirements of part 9903 and coordinating CAS administrative actions with all affected Federal agencies.

statement: When multiple CAS-covered contracts or more than one Federal agency are involved, agencies should discourage Contracting Officers from individually administering CAS on a contract-by-contract basis.
quote: When multiple CAS-covered contracts or more than one Federal agency are involved, agencies should discourage Contracting Officers from individually administering CAS on a contract-by-contract basis.

statement: Federal agencies shall prescribe regulations and establish internal policies and procedures governing how they will administer the requirements of CAS-covered contracts, with particular emphasis on inter-agency coordination activities.
quote: Federal agencies shall prescribe regulations and establish internal policies and procedures governing how agencies will administer the requirements of CAS-covered contracts, with particular emphasis on inter-agency coordination activities.

statement: Internal agency policies and procedures must provide for the designation of the agency office or officials responsible for administering CAS at each contractor business unit and for the delegation of the necessary contracting authority.
quote: Internal agency policies and procedures shall provide for the designation of the agency office(s) or officials responsible for administering CAS under the agency's CAS-covered contracts at each contractor business unit and the delegation of necessary contracting authority

statement: A cost accounting practice is any disclosed or established accounting method or technique used for allocation of cost to cost objectives, assignment of cost to cost accounting periods, or measurement of cost.
quote: Cost accounting practice, as used in this part, means any disclosed or established accounting method or technique which is used for allocation of cost to cost objectives, assignment of cost to cost accounting periods, or measurement of cost.

statement: The determination of the amount paid, or of a change in the amount paid, for a unit of goods and services is not a cost accounting practice.
quote: The determination of the amount paid or a change in the amount paid for a unit of goods and services is not a cost accounting practice.

statement: Allocation of cost to cost objectives includes both direct and indirect allocation of cost.
quote: Allocation of cost to cost objectives, as used in this part, includes both direct and indirect allocation of cost.

statement: A change to a cost accounting practice is any alteration in a cost accounting practice, whether or not the practices are covered by a Disclosure Statement, apart from the exclusions that follow in the section.
quote: any alteration in a cost accounting practice, as defined in 9903.302-1, whether or not such practices are covered by a Disclosure Statement, except for the following

statement: The initial adoption of a cost accounting practice for the first time a cost is incurred, or a function is created, is not a change in cost accounting practice.
quote: The initial adoption of a cost accounting practice for the first time a cost is incurred, or a function is created, is not a change in cost accounting practice.

statement: The partial or total elimination of a cost, or of the cost of a function, is not a change in cost accounting practice.
quote: The partial or total elimination of a cost or the cost of a function is not a change in cost accounting practice.

statement: The revision of a cost accounting practice for a cost which previously had been immaterial is not a change in cost accounting practice.
quote: The revision of a cost accounting practice for a cost which previously had been immaterial is not a change in cost accounting practice.

statement: In determining whether amounts of cost are material or immaterial, the listed criteria shall be considered where appropriate, and no one criterion is necessarily determinative.
quote: In determining whether amounts of cost are material or immaterial, the following criteria shall be considered where appropriate; no one criterion is necessarily determinative

statement: The absolute dollar amount involved is a materiality criterion: the larger the dollar amount, the more likely it is that the amount is material.
quote: (a) The absolute dollar amount involved. The larger the dollar amount, the more likely that it will be material.

statement: The amount of contract cost compared with the amount under consideration is a materiality criterion: the larger the proportion of the amount under consideration to contract cost, the more likely it is to be material.
quote: (b) The amount of contract cost compared with the amount under consideration. The larger the proportion of the amount under consideration to contract cost, the more likely it is to be material.

statement: Direct cost items, especially where the amounts are themselves part of a base for allocation of indirect costs, normally have more impact on materiality than the same amount of indirect costs.
quote: (c) The relationship between a cost item and a cost objective. Direct cost items, especially if the amounts are themselves part of a base for allocation of indirect costs, will normally have more impact than the same amount of indirect costs.

statement: In judging cumulative impact, it is appropriate to consider whether individually immaterial items tend to offset one another or tend to be in the same direction and so accumulate into a material amount.
quote: (e) The cumulative impact of individually immaterial items. It is appropriate to consider whether such impacts: (1) Tend to offset one another, or (2) Tend to be in the same direction and hence to accumulate into a material amount.

statement: The cost of administrative processing of the price adjustment modification is a materiality criterion; if the cost to process exceeds the amount to be recovered, the amount is less likely to be material.
quote: (f) The cost of administrative processing of the price adjustment modification shall be considered. If the cost to process exceeds the amount to be recovered, it is less likely the amount will be material.

statement: The amount of insurance cost to be assigned to a cost accounting period is the projected average loss for that period plus insurance administration expenses in that period.
quote: The amount of insurance cost to be assigned to a cost accounting period is the projected average loss for that period plus insurance administration expenses in that period.

statement: The allocation of insurance costs to cost objectives shall be based on the beneficial or causal relationship between the insurance costs and the benefiting or causing cost objectives.
quote: The allocation of insurance costs to cost objectives shall be based on the beneficial or casual relationship between the insurance costs and the benefiting or causing cost objectives.
note: The printed text reads "casual" where "causal" is evidently meant; the statement uses the intended word.

statement: The premium cost applicable to a given policy term shall be assigned pro rata among the cost accounting periods covered by the policy term, except as provided in the listed subdivisions.
quote: The premium cost applicable to a given policy term shall be assigned pro rata among the cost accounting periods covered by the policy term, except as provided in subdivisions (a)(1) (ii) through (vi) of this subsection.

statement: Where insurance is purchased specifically for, and directly allocated to, a single final cost objective, the premium need not be prorated among cost accounting periods.
quote: Where insurance is purchased specifically for, and directly allocated to, a single final cost objective, the premium need not be prorated among cost accounting periods.

statement: Except as provided in the two listed subdivisions, actual losses shall not become a part of insurance costs.
quote: Except as provided in subdivisions (a)(2)(ii) and (iii) of this subsection, actual losses shall not become a part of insurance costs.

statement: The self-insurance charge that the contractor makes for each period for each type of self-insured risk shall represent the projected average loss for that period.
quote: the contractor shall make a self-insurance charge for each period for each type of self-insured risk which shall represent the projected average loss for that period

statement: Insurance costs shall be allocated on the basis of the factors used to determine the premium, assessment, refund, dividend or self-insurance charge, subject to an exception stated in the same sentence.
quote: Insurance costs shall be allocated on the basis of the factors used to determine the premium, assessment, refund, dividend, or self-insurance charge

statement: Insurance administration expenses which are material in relation to total insurance costs shall be allocated on the same basis as the related premium costs or self-insurance charge.
quote: Insurance administration expenses which are material in relation to total insurance costs shall be allocated on the same basis as the related premium costs or self-insurance charge.

statement: The contractor shall maintain records necessary to substantiate the amounts of premiums, refunds, dividends, losses and self-insurance charges paid or accrued, and the measurement and allocation of insurance costs.
quote: The contractor shall maintain such records as may be necessary to substantiate the amounts of premiums, refunds, dividends, losses, and self-insurance charges, paid or accrued, and the measurement and allocation of insurance costs.

statement: The cost of money applicable to the investment in tangible and intangible capital assets being constructed, fabricated or developed for a contractor's own use shall be included in the capitalized acquisition cost of such assets.
quote: The cost of money applicable to the investment in tangible and intangible capital assets being constructed, fabricated, or developed for a contractor's own use shall be included in the capitalized acquisition cost of such assets.

statement: The cost of money rate used shall be based on interest rates determined by the Secretary of the Treasury pursuant to Public Law 92-41.
quote: The cost of money rate used shall be based on interest rates determined by the Secretary of the Treasury pursuant to Public Law 92-41 (85 stat. 97).

statement: A representative investment amount shall be determined each cost accounting period for each capital asset being constructed, fabricated or developed, giving appropriate consideration to the rate at which costs of construction are incurred.
quote: A representative investment amount shall be determined each cost accounting period for each capital asset being constructed, fabricated, or developed giving appropriate consideration to the rate at which costs of construction are incurred.

statement: Other methods for calculating the cost of money to be capitalized may be used, provided the resulting amount does not differ materially from the amount calculated by use of the prescribed rate and investment amount paragraphs.
quote: Other methods for calculating the cost of money to be capitalized, such as the method used for financial accounting and reporting, may be used, provided the resulting amount does not differ materially from the amount calculated by use of paragraphs (a) (1) and (2) of this subsection.

statement: If substantially all the activities necessary to get the asset ready for its intended use are discontinued, cost of money shall not be capitalized for the period of discontinuance.
quote: If substantially all the activities necessary to get the asset ready for its intended use are discontinued, cost of money shall not be capitalized for the period of discontinuance.

statement: Cessation of cost of money capitalization is not required where the discontinuance arises out of causes beyond the control and without the fault or negligence of the contractor.
quote: However, if such discontinuance arises out of causes beyond the control and without the fault or negligence of the contractor, cessation of cost of money capitalization is not required.

statement: Audit objectives for subcontract costs also include verifying that the Government is not paying excessive pass-through costs if the contracting officer determines the contractor does not provide added value to subcontracted work.
quote: and the Government is not paying excessive pass-through costs if the contracting officer determines the contractor does not provide “added value” to subcontracted work pursuant to FAR 52.215-22, 52.215-23, and 31.203(i).

statement: The manual section on incurred cost audit objectives gives general guidance on audit objectives and approach, including general considerations applicable to all types of contracts and cost categories.
quote: This section provides general guidance on the audit objectives and approach for incurred costs, including general considerations applicable to all types of contracts and cost categories.

statement: Incurred cost audit objectives and guidance for institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations and federally funded research and development centers are addressed in Chapter 13 of the manual, not in the chapter on general incurred cost audit objectives.

statement: Store requisitions for materials, supplies, equipment, and services are to be retained 2 years.

statement: Work orders for maintenance and other services are to be retained 4 years.

statement: Equipment records, consisting of equipment usage and status reports and equipment repair orders, are to be retained 4 years.

statement: Property records are to be retained 4 years.

statement: At the outset of administrative closeout, the contract administration office must review the contract funds status and notify the contracting office of any excess funds the contract administration office might deobligate.
quote: At the outset of this process, the contract administration office must review the contract funds status and notify the contracting office of any excess funds the contract administration office might deobligate.

quote: (c) An agency that requires a shorter retention period than those identified in Table 4-1 shall request approval from NARA through the agency's records officer.

statement: FAR 3.900 through 3.906 do not apply to DoD, NASA, the Coast Guard, or any element of the intelligence community.
quote: These sections do not apply to— (1) DoD, NASA, and the Coast Guard; or (2) Any element of the intelligence community,

quote: This subpart does not implement 10 U.S.C. 4701, which is applicable only to DoD, NASA, and the Coast Guard.

statement: Those sections also do not apply to a disclosure by an employee of a contractor or subcontractor of an element of the intelligence community if the disclosure relates to an activity of such an element.
quote: Sections 3.900 through 3.906 do not apply to any disclosure made by an employee of a contractor or subcontractor of an element of the intelligence community if such disclosure— (i) Relates to an activity of an element of the intelligence community;

statement: The second listed alternative is a disclosure that was discovered during contract or subcontract services provided to an element of the intelligence community.
quote: or (ii) Was discovered during contract or subcontract services provided to an element of the intelligence community.

statement: Agencies shall avoid duplicate audits, reviews, inspections and examinations of contractors or subcontractors by more than one agency through the use of interagency agreements.
quote: Agencies shall avoid duplicate audits, reviews, inspections, and examinations of contractors or subcontractors, by more than one agency, through the use of interagency agreements.

statement: Subject to the fiscal regulations of the agencies and applicable interagency agreements, the requesting agency shall reimburse the servicing agency for rendered services in accordance with the Economy Act.
quote: Subject to the fiscal regulations of the agencies and applicable interagency agreements, the requesting agency shall reimburse the servicing agency for rendered services in accordance with the Economy Act (31 U.S.C. 1535).

statement: DoD requires reimbursement from non-DoD organizations at a rate set by the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller/Chief Financial Officer), except for listed cases.
quote: DoD requires reimbursement, at a rate set by the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller/Chief Financial Officer), from non-DoD organizations, except for—

quote: (A) Quality assurance, contract administration, and audit services provided under a no-charge reciprocal agreement; (B) Services performed under subcontracts awarded by the Small Business Administration under FAR subpart 19.8;
