quote: (C) Quality assurance requests performed for the Canadian Department of National Defence and pricing services performed for Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC), operating as Public Services and Procurment Canada (PSPC).
note: The quote keeps the source spelling.

statement: Departments and agencies may request an exception from the DoD reimbursement policy from the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller/Chief Financial Officer), and the request must show that an exception is in the best interest of the Government.
quote: Departments and agencies may request an exception from the reimbursement policy in paragraph (b)(i) of this section from the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller/Chief Financial Officer). A request must show that an exception is in the best interest of the Government.

statement: Departments and agencies must pay for services performed by non-DoD activities, foreign governments or international organizations, unless reciprocal agreements provide otherwise.
quote: Departments and agencies must pay for services performed by non-DoD activities, foreign governments, or international organizations, unless otherwise provided by reciprocal agreements.

statement: Foreign governments and international organizations may request contract administration services on their direct purchases from U.S. producers.
quote: Foreign governments and international organizations may request contract administration services on their direct purchases from U.S. producers.

statement: Other foreign governments, including Canadian government organizations other than PSPC, and international organizations send their requests for contract administration services to the DoD Central Control Point at the Headquarters, Defense Contract Management Agency.
quote: Other foreign governments (including Canadian government organizations other than PSPC) and international organizations send their requests for contract administration services to the DoD Central Control Point (CCP) at the Headquarters, Defense Contract Management Agency
note: The preceding printed paragraph lets PWGSC, operating as PSPC, submit its requests directly to the cognizant contract administration office.

statement: As provided in agency procedures, contracting officers may delegate contract administration or specialized support services, either through interagency agreements or by direct request to the cognizant CAO listed in the Federal Directory of Contract Administration Services Components.
quote: As provided in agency procedures, contracting officers may delegate contract administration or specialized support services, either through interagency agreements or by direct request to the cognizant CAO listed in the Federal Directory of Contract Administration Services Components.

statement: The delegation should include, among other items, the name and address of the CAO designated to perform the administration, which also shall be entered in the contract, and any special instructions, including any functions withheld or any specific authorization to perform functions listed in 42.302(b).
quote: The delegation should include— (1) The name and address of the CAO designated to perform the administration (this information also shall be entered in the contract); (2) Any special instructions, including any functions withheld or any specific authorization to perform functions listed in 42.302(b);
note: The delegation list continues with further items that this claim does not cover.

statement: For individual contracts or groups of contracts, the contracting office may delegate to the CAO functions not listed in 42.302, provided that listed conditions are met, one being prior coordination with the CAO to ensure the availability of required resources.
quote: For individual contracts or groups of contracts, the contracting office may delegate to the CAO functions not listed in 42.302: Provided that— (1) Prior coordination with the CAO ensures the availability of required resources;

statement: The contracting officer at the requesting agency may rescind or recall a delegation to administer a contract or perform a contract administration function, except for functions pertaining to cost accounting standards and negotiation of forward pricing rates and indirect cost rates.
quote: The contracting officer at the requesting agency may rescind or recall a delegation to administer a contract or perform a contract administration function, except for functions pertaining to cost accounting standards and negotiation of forward pricing rates and indirect cost rates

statement: The requesting agency must coordinate with the CAO to establish a reasonable transition period before rescinding or recalling a delegation.
quote: The requesting agency must coordinate with the CAO to establish a reasonable transition period prior to rescinding or recalling the delegation.

statement: Supporting contract administration shall not be used for subcontracts unless the Government otherwise would incur undue cost, successful completion of the prime contract is threatened, or it is authorized under paragraph (f) of the section or elsewhere in the regulation.
quote: supporting contract administration shall not be used for subcontracts unless— (i) The Government otherwise would incur undue cost; (ii) Successful completion of the prime contract is threatened; or (iii) It is authorized under paragraph (f) of this section or elsewhere in this regulation.

statement: An agency may decline a request for contract administration services on a case-by-case basis if its resources are inadequate to accomplish the tasks, and a declination shall be in writing.
quote: An agency may decline a request for contract administration services on a case-by-case basis if resources of the agency are inadequate to accomplish the tasks. Declinations shall be in writing.

statement: The Defense Contract Management Agency maintains the Federal Directory of Contract Administration Services Components.
quote: The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) maintains the Federal Directory of Contract Administration Services Components.

statement: DoD activities shall not retain for administration any contract that requires performance of any contract administration function at or near contractor facilities, except listed categories of contract, which include contracts for the National Security Agency and research and development with universities.
quote: DoD activities shall not retain any contract for administration that requires performance of any contract administration function at or near contractor facilities, except contracts for— (A) The National Security Agency; (B) Research and development with universities;
note: The printed exception list continues with further categories.

statement: Contract administration functions for base, post, camp and station contracts on a military installation are normally the responsibility of the installation or tenant commander.
quote: Contract administration functions for base, post, camp, and station contracts on a military installation are normally the responsibility of the installation or tenant commander.

statement: Production surveillance is a function of contract administration used to determine contractor progress and to identify any factors that may delay performance.
quote: Production surveillance is a function of contract administration used to determine contractor progress and to identify any factors that may delay performance.

quote: Production surveillance involves Government review and analysis of (a) contractor performance plans, schedules, controls, and industrial processes and (b) the contractor's actual performance under them.

statement: The production surveillance and reporting subpart applies to all contracts for supplies or services other than construction contracts, and Federal Supply Schedule contracts.
quote: This subpart applies to all contracts for supplies or services other than construction contracts, and Federal Supply Schedule contracts.

quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.242-2, Production Progress Reports, in solicitations and contracts when production progress reporting is required; unless a construction contract, or a Federal Supply Schedule contract is contemplated.

statement: When the Production Progress Reports clause is used, the contracting officer shall specify appropriate reporting instructions in the Schedule.
quote: When the clause at 52.242-2 is used, the contracting officer shall specify appropriate reporting instructions in the Schedule (see 42.1106(a)).

quote: In the event of disagreement, the contractor may submit to the contracting officer a written response. Any such response shall be answered by withdrawal of the notice or by making a written decision within 60 days.

statement: As a minimum, the notice shall, among other listed items, refer to the contract's Notice of Intent to Disallow Costs clause and state the contractor's name and list the numbers of the affected contracts.
quote: As a minimum, the notice shall— (1) Refer to the contract's Notice of Intent to Disallow Costs clause; (2) State the contractor's name and list the numbers of the affected contracts;

statement: A notice that involves elements of indirect cost shall not be issued without coordination with the contracting officer or auditor having authority for final indirect cost settlement.
quote: If the notice involves elements of indirect cost, it shall not be issued without coordination with the contracting officer or auditor having authority for final indirect cost settlement (see 42.705).

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Notice of Intent to Disallow Costs clause in solicitations and contracts when a cost-reimbursement contract, a fixed-price incentive contract, or a contract providing for price redetermination is contemplated.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.242-1, Notice of Intent to Disallow Costs, in solicitations and contracts when a cost-reimbursement contract, a fixed-price incentive contract, or a contract providing for price redetermination is contemplated.

statement: The contract auditor is the authorized representative of the contracting officer for, among listed duties, receiving vouchers from contractors electronically or by other delivery methods as directed by the terms of the contract.
quote: The contract auditor is the authorized representative of the contracting officer for— (A) Receiving vouchers from contractors electronically or by other delivery methods as directed by the terms of the contract;

quote: (D) Issuing DCAA Forms 1, Notice of Contract Costs Suspended and/or Disapproved, to deduct costs where allowability is questionable.

quote: The administrative contracting officer— (A) Approves all completion/final vouchers and sends them to the disbursing officer; and (B) May issue or direct the issuance of DCAA Form 1 on any cost when there is reason to believe it should be suspended or disallowed.

quote: (2) Determine the amount of the Government's potential claim against the contractor (in assessing this impact, identify and review any contracts that have not been closed out, including those physically completed or terminated);

statement: Two further listed minimum actions on notice of bankruptcy are to take actions necessary to protect the Government's financial interests and safeguard Government property, and to furnish pertinent contract information to the legal counsel representing the Government.
quote: (3) Take actions necessary to protect the Government's financial interests and safeguard Government property; and (4) Furnish pertinent contract information to the legal counsel representing the Government.

statement: The contracting officer shall consult the legal counsel, whenever possible, before taking any action regarding the contractor's bankruptcy proceedings.
quote: The contracting officer shall consult the legal counsel, whenever possible, prior to taking any action regarding the contractor's bankruptcy proceedings.

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Bankruptcy clause in all solicitations and contracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.242-13, Bankruptcy, in all solicitations and contracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold.

quote: A suspension of work under a construction or architect-engineer contract may be ordered by the contracting officer for a reasonable period of time. If the suspension is unreasonable, the contractor may submit a written claim for increases in the cost of performance, excluding profit.

statement: The Government Delay of Work clause provides for the administrative settlement of contractor claims that arise from delays and interruptions in the contract work caused by the acts, or failures to act, of the contracting officer.
quote: The clause at 52.242-17, Government Delay of Work, provides for the administrative settlement of contractor claims that arise from delays and interruptions in the contract work caused by the acts, or failures to act, of the contracting officer.

note: The quote begins with the words this clause, which refer to the clause named in the preceding printed sentence.

statement: The Government Delay of Work clause does not authorize the contracting officer to order a suspension, delay or interruption of the contract work and shall not be used as the basis or justification of such an order.
quote: The clause does not authorize the contracting officer to order a suspension, delay, or interruption of the contract work and it shall not be used as the basis or justification of such an order.

statement: If the contracting officer has notice of an unordered delay or interruption covered by the clause, the contracting officer shall act to end the delay or take other appropriate action as soon as practicable.
quote: If the contracting officer has notice of an unordered delay or interruption covered by the clause, the contracting officer shall act to end the delay or take other appropriate action as soon as practicable.

quote: The contracting officer shall retain in the file a record of all negotiations leading to any adjustment made under the clause, and related certified cost or pricing data, or data other than certified cost or pricing data.

quote: Past performance information (including the ratings and supporting narratives) is relevant information, for future source selection purposes, regarding a contractor's actions under previously awarded contracts or orders.

note: The printed list continues with further items.

quote: Agencies shall monitor their compliance with the past performance evaluation requirements (see 42.1502), and use the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS) metric tools to measure the quality and timely reporting of past performance information.

statement: The Payments to Small Business Subcontractors clause is inserted in all solicitations and contracts containing the Small Business Subcontracting Plan clause.
quote: Insert the clause at 52.242-5, Payments to Small Business Subcontractors, in all solicitations and contracts containing the clause at 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan.

statement: The Certificate of Independent Price Determination provision is to be inserted as prescribed in FAR 3.103-1.
quote: As prescribed in 3.103-1, insert the following provision.

quote: (a) The offeror certifies that—

statement: One listed certification in the provision is that the prices in the offer were arrived at independently, without, for the purpose of restricting competition, any consultation, communication, or agreement with any other offeror or competitor relating to those prices, the intention to submit an offer, or the methods or factors used to calculate the prices offered.

quote: (a) The Contractor warrants that no person or agency has been employed or retained to solicit or obtain this contract upon an agreement or understanding for a contingent fee, except a bona fide employee or agency.

statement: For breach or violation of the covenant warranty, the Government shall have the right to annul the contract without liability or to deduct from the contract price or consideration, or otherwise recover, the full amount of the contingent fee.
quote: For breach or violation of this warranty, the Government shall have the right to annul this contract without liability or to deduct from the contract price or consideration, or otherwise recover, the full amount of the contingent fee.

statement: The Anti-Kickback Procedures clause is to be inserted as prescribed in FAR 3.502-3.
quote: As prescribed in 3.502-3, insert the following clause:

quote: (b) 41 U.S.C. chapter 87, Kickbacks, prohibits any person from— (1) Providing or attempting to provide or offering to provide any kickback; (2) Soliciting, accepting, or attempting to accept any kickback; or

quote: (3) Including, directly or indirectly, the amount of any kickback in the contract price charged by a prime Contractor to the United States or in the contract price charged by a subcontractor to a prime Contractor or higher tier subcontractor.

statement: The Contractor shall have in place and follow reasonable procedures designed to prevent and detect possible violations of the listed prohibitions in its own operations and direct business relationships.
quote: The Contractor shall have in place and follow reasonable procedures designed to prevent and detect possible violations described in paragraph (b) of this clause in its own operations and direct business relationships.

statement: If, after notification, additional funds are not allotted by the end of the period specified in the Schedule or another agreed-upon date, then upon the contractor's written request the contracting officer will terminate the contract on that date.
quote: If, after notification, additional funds are not allotted by the end of the period specified in the Schedule or another agreed-upon date, upon the Contractor's written request the Contracting Officer will terminate this contract on that date

statement: The clause prescription permits the 60-day period to be varied from 30 to 90 days and the 75 percent figure from 75 to 85 percent.
quote: The 60-day period may be varied from 30 to 90 days and the 75 percent from 75 to 85 percent.

statement: Except as required by other provisions of the contract that specifically cite and are stated to be an exception to this clause, the Government is not obligated to reimburse the contractor for costs incurred above the total amount allotted to the contract.
quote: Except as required by other provisions of this contract, specifically citing and stated to be an exception to this clause— (1) The Government is not obligated to reimburse the Contractor for costs incurred in excess of the total amount allotted by the Government to this contract

statement: The contracting officer, cognizant Federal agency official, or auditor responsible for establishing the final indirect cost rates is also responsible for determining the billing rates.
quote: The contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) or auditor responsible under 42.705 for establishing the final indirect cost rates also shall be responsible for determining the billing rates.

statement: Billing rates should be as close as possible to the final indirect cost rates anticipated for the contractor's fiscal period, as adjusted for any unallowable costs.
quote: the billing rates are as close as possible to the final indirect cost rates anticipated for the contractor's fiscal period, as adjusted for any unallowable costs

statement: Once established, billing rates may be revised prospectively or retroactively by mutual agreement of the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) or auditor and the contractor at either party's request, to prevent substantial overpayment or underpayment.
quote: billing rates may be prospectively or retroactively revised by mutual agreement of the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) or auditor and the contractor at either party's request, to prevent substantial overpayment or underpayment

statement: The indirect cost elements and bases used in computing billing rates are not determinative of the indirect costs to be distributed or of the bases of distribution used in the final settlement.
quote: shall not be construed as determinative of the indirect costs to be distributed or of the bases of distribution to be used in the final settlement.

statement: Until final annual indirect cost rates are established for a period, the Government reimburses the contractor at billing rates established by the contracting officer or the cognizant auditor, subject to adjustment when the final rates are established.
quote: the Government shall reimburse the Contractor at billing rates established by the Contracting Officer or by an authorized representative (the cognizant auditor), subject to adjustment when the final rates are established

statement: Under the basic allowable cost and payment clause, the Government makes payments when requested as work progresses but, except for small business concerns, not more often than once every two weeks.
quote: The Government will make payments to the Contractor when requested as work progresses, but (except for small business concerns) not more often than once every 2 weeks

statement: The Prompt Payment clause is inserted in contracts as prescribed in FAR 32.908(c).
quote: As prescribed in 32.908(c), insert the following clause: Prompt Payment (JAN 2017)

statement: Except as indicated in paragraphs (a)(2) and (c) of the Prompt Payment clause, the due date for invoice payments is the later of the 30th day after the designated billing office receives a proper invoice and the 30th day after Government acceptance of supplies delivered or services performed.
quote: Except as indicated in paragraphs (a)(2) and (c) of this clause, the due date for making invoice payments by the designated payment office is the later of the following two events: (A) The 30th day after the designated billing office receives a proper invoice from the Contractor

statement: The designated payment office pays an interest penalty automatically, without a request from the contractor, if payment is not made by the due date and the conditions listed in the clause are met, if applicable.
quote: The designated payment office will pay an interest penalty automatically, without request from the Contractor, if payment is not made by the due date and the conditions listed in paragraphs (a)(4)(i) through (a)(4)(iii) of this clause are met, if applicable.

statement: If an invoice does not comply with the content requirements, the designated billing office returns it within 7 days after receipt; the next claim covers the shorter periods for certain products and the statement of reasons.
quote: If the invoice does not comply with these requirements, the designated billing office will return it within 7 days after receipt

statement: All days referred to in the Prompt Payment clause are calendar days unless otherwise specified.
quote: All days referred to in this clause are calendar days, unless otherwise specified.

statement: An additional penalty requires an unpaid interest penalty of $1 or more, failure to pay that interest penalty within 10 days after the invoice amount is paid, and a written demand to the payment office postmarked not later than 40 days after the invoice amount is paid.
quote: The Contractor makes a written demand to the designated payment office for additional penalty payment, in accordance with paragraph (a)(7)(ii) of this clause, postmarked not later than 40 days after the invoice amount is paid.

statement: Where the contract contains the fast payment procedure clause, payments are made within 15 days after the date the invoice is received.
quote: If this contract contains the clause at 52.213-1, Fast Payment Procedure, payments will be made within 15 days after the date of receipt of the invoice.

statement: Contract financing payments are not subject to the interest penalty provisions of the Prompt Payment Act.
quote: Contract financing payments are not subject to the interest penalty provisions of the Prompt Payment Act.

statement: Subject to the other limitations and conditions in the contract and clause, the contract's description of the basis for payment specifies payment amounts and limitations.
quote: Subject to such other limitations and conditions as are specified in this contract and this clause, the amount of payments and limitations on payments shall be specified in the contract's description of the basis for payment.

statement: The contractor may submit performance-based payment requests no more often than monthly, in a form and manner acceptable to the Contracting Officer.
quote: The Contractor may submit requests for payment of performance-based payments not more frequently than monthly, in a form and manner acceptable to the Contracting Officer.

statement: Unless the Contracting Officer otherwise authorizes, all performance-based payments for a period must be included in a single, appropriately itemized and totaled request.
quote: Unless otherwise authorized by the Contracting Officer, all performance-based payments in any period for which payment is being requested shall be included in a single request, appropriately itemized and totaled.

statement: The contractor is not entitled to a requested performance-based payment before successful accomplishment of the event or performance criterion for which payment is requested.
quote: The Contractor shall not be entitled to payment of a request for performance-based payment prior to successful accomplishment of the event or performance criterion for which payment is requested.

statement: The Contracting Officer determines whether the event or performance criterion has been successfully accomplished in accordance with the contract terms.
quote: The Contracting Officer shall determine whether the event or performance criterion for which payment is requested has been successfully accomplished in accordance with the terms of the contract.

statement: The Progress Payments clause provides a Government right to reduce or suspend progress payments, or to increase the liquidation rate, under specified conditions.
quote: The Progress Payments clause provides a Government right to reduce or suspend progress payments, or to increase the liquidation rate, under specified conditions.

statement: If the system or controls are deemed inadequate, progress payments (or the portion associated with the unacceptable portion of the contractor's accounting system) must be suspended until the necessary changes have been made.
quote: If the system or controls are deemed inadequate, progress payments shall be suspended (or the portion of progress payments associated with the unacceptable portion of the contractor's accounting system shall be suspended) until the necessary changes have been made.

statement: The contracting officer must adjust progress payments when necessary to ensure that the fair value of undelivered work equals or exceeds the amount of unliquidated progress payments.
quote: The contracting officer must adjust progress payments when necessary to ensure that the fair value of undelivered work equals or exceeds the amount of unliquidated progress payments.

statement: If the contracting officer concludes that further progress payments would increase the probable loss to the Government, the contracting officer must suspend progress payments and all other payments until the unliquidated balance of progress payments is eliminated.
quote: If the contracting officer concludes that further progress payments would increase the probable loss to the Government, the contracting officer shall suspend progress payments and all other payments until the unliquidated balance of progress payments is eliminated.

statement: Advance payments may be provided on any type of contract, but the agency must authorize advance payments sparingly.
quote: Advance payments may be provided on any type of contract; however, the agency shall authorize advance payments sparingly.

statement: Except for the contracts described in 32.403(a) and (b), advance payment is the least preferred method of contract financing and generally should not be authorized if other types of financing are reasonably available to the contractor in adequate amounts.
quote: Except for the contracts described in 32.403(a) and (b), advance payment is the least preferred method of contract financing (see 32.106) and generally they should not be authorized if other types of financing are reasonably available to the contractor in adequate amounts.

statement: The statutory requirements for advance payments include that the contractor gives adequate security and that the advance payments will not exceed the unpaid contract price.
quote: The statutory requirements are that— (i) The contractor gives adequate security; (ii) The advance payments will not exceed the unpaid contract price

statement: If necessary, the agency may authorize advance payments in addition to progress or partial payments on the same contract.
quote: If necessary, the agency may authorize advance payments in addition to progress or partial payments on the same contract (see 32.501-1(c)).

statement: For purchases of commercial products or commercial services, financing of the contract is normally the contractor's responsibility.
quote: Thus, for purchases of commercial products or commercial services, financing of the contract is normally the contractor's responsibility.

statement: Commercial interim payments and commercial advance payments may be made under the circumstances listed in paragraph (b), which include that the contract item financed is a commercial supply or service and that the contract price exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold, among other listed circumstances.
quote: Commercial interim payments and commercial advance payments may be made under the following circumstances— (1) The contract item financed is a commercial supply or service; (2) The contract price exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold;

statement: Prior to any performance of work under the contract, the aggregate of commercial advance payments shall not exceed 15 percent of the contract price.
quote: Prior to any performance of work under the contract, the aggregate of commercial advance payments shall not exceed 15 percent of the contract price;

statement: Statutes do not allow contract financing by the Government for commercial purchases unless it is in the best interest of the United States.
quote: The statutes cited in 32.201 do not allow contract financing by the Government unless it is in the best interest of the United States.

statement: The Fixed Fee clause is inserted in solicitations and contracts when a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract, other than a facilities contract or a construction contract, is contemplated.
quote: insert the following clause in solicitations and contracts when a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract (other than a facilities contract or a construction contract) is contemplated.

statement: Payment of fixed fee is made as specified in the Schedule, provided the Contracting Officer withholds a reserve not to exceed 15 percent of the total fixed fee or $100,000, whichever is less, to protect the Government's interest.
quote: Payment of the fixed fee shall be made as specified in the Schedule; provided that the Contracting Officer withholds a reserve not to exceed 15 percent of the total fixed fee or $100,000, whichever is less, to protect the Government's interest.

statement: The Contracting Officer must release 75 percent of all fee withholds under the contract after receipt of an adequate certified final indirect cost rate proposal covering the year of physical completion, on the proviso stated in the next claim.
quote: The Contracting Officer shall release 75 percent of all fee withholds under this contract after receipt of an adequate certified final indirect cost rate proposal covering the year of physical completion of this contract,

statement: The Contracting Officer may release up to 90 percent of fee withholds under the contract based on the contractor's past performance related to the submission and settlement of final indirect cost rate proposals.
quote: The Contracting Officer may release up to 90 percent of the fee withholds under this contract based on the Contractor's past performance related to the submission and settlement of final indirect cost rate proposals.

statement: The Incentive Fee clause is inserted in solicitations and contracts when a cost-plus-incentive-fee contract, other than a facilities contract, is contemplated.
quote: insert the following clause in solicitations and contracts when a cost-plus-incentive-fee contract (other than a facilities contract) is contemplated:

statement: When the Contracting Officer considers that performance or cost indicates the contractor will not achieve target, the Government pays fee on the basis of an appropriate lesser fee.
quote: However, when the Contracting Officer considers that performance or cost indicates that the Contractor will not achieve target, the Government shall pay on the basis of an appropriate lesser fee.

statement: Payment of the incentive fee is made as specified in the Schedule, provided the Contracting Officer withholds a reserve not to exceed 15 percent of the total incentive fee or $100,000, whichever is less, to protect the Government's interest.
quote: Payment of the incentive fee shall be made as specified in the Schedule; provided that the Contracting Officer withholds a reserve not to exceed 15 percent of the total incentive fee or $100,000, whichever is less, to protect the Government's interest.

statement: The total allowable cost and the adjusted incentive fee determined under the clause must be evidenced by a contract modification signed by the contractor and the Contracting Officer.
quote: The total allowable cost and the adjusted fee determined as provided in this clause shall be evidenced by a modification to this contract signed by the Contractor and Contracting Officer.

statement: The computation adds financing payments to subcontractors (see paragraph (j) of the clause) and subtracts the sum of all previous progress payments made by the Government under the contract.
quote: , plus financing payments to subcontractors (see paragraph (j) of this clause), less the sum of all previous progress payments made by the Government under this contract.

statement: The conditions include failure to comply with any material requirement of the contract (which includes paragraphs (f) and (g) of the clause), and endangered performance because of the Contractor's failure to make progress or unsatisfactory financial condition.
quote: (1) The Contractor failed to comply with any material requirement of this contract (which includes paragraphs (f) and (g) below). (2) Performance of this contract is endangered by the Contractor's (i) failure to make progress or (ii) unsatisfactory financial condition.

quote: (5) The fair value of the undelivered work is less than the amount of unliquidated progress payments for that work.

quote: , if any, required to continue timely performance under the contract or for any further period specified in the Schedule or otherwise agreed upon, and when the funds will be required.

statement: The release is conditioned on the Contractor having satisfied all other contract terms and conditions, including the submission of the final patent and royalty reports, and not being delinquent in submitting final vouchers on prior years' settlements.
quote: provided the Contractor has satisfied all other contract terms and conditions, including the submission of the final patent and royalty reports, and is not delinquent in submitting final vouchers on prior years' settlements.

statement: The Economic Price Adjustment—Labor and Material clause appears at FAR 52.216-4 and is inserted as prescribed in FAR 16.203-4(c).

note: The packet's topic label 'Standard Supplies' maps to FAR 52.216-4, which the printed text titles 'Economic Price Adjustment—Labor and Material'.

quote: The Contractor shall furnish this notice within 60 days after the increase or decrease, or within any additional period that the Contracting Officer may approve in writing, but not later than the date of final payment under this contract.

quote: Any payment may be (1) reduced by any amounts found by the Contracting Officer not to constitute allowable costs or (2) adjusted for overpayments or underpayments made on preceding invoices or vouchers.

statement: FAR 52.249-2 is the clause titled Termination for Convenience of the Government (Fixed-Price) (APR 2012), which is inserted as prescribed in FAR 49.502(b)(1)(i).
quote: As prescribed in 49.502(b)(1)(i), insert the following clause: Termination for Convenience of the Government (Fixed-Price) (APR 2012)

quote: The Government may terminate performance of work under this contract in whole or, from time to time, in part if the Contracting Officer determines that a termination is in the Government's interest.

statement: Any proposal by the contractor for an equitable adjustment of the continued portion in a partial termination must be requested within 90 days from the effective date of termination unless extended in writing.

quote: (a) Contract debts are amounts that— (1) Have been paid to a contractor to which the contractor is not currently entitled under the terms and conditions of the contract; or (2) Are otherwise due from the contractor under the terms and conditions of the contract.

statement: FAR 32.1103 says the Government shall provide all contract payments through EFT except in the listed cases, one of which is that the office making payment under a contract that requires payment by EFT loses the ability to release payment by EFT.
quote: The Government shall provide all contract payments through EFT except if— (a) The office making payment under a contract that requires payment by EFT, loses the ability to release payment by EFT.

statement: Two further listed exceptions in FAR 32.1103 are a payment to be received by or on behalf of the contractor outside the United States and Puerto Rico and a contract paid in other than United States currency, each marked in the text with a cross-reference to 32.1106(b).
quote: (b) The payment is to be received by or on behalf of the contractor outside the United States and Puerto Rico (but see 32.1106(b)); (c) A contract is paid in other than United States currency (but see 32.1106(b));

statement: A further listed exception in FAR 32.1103 is payment by EFT under a classified contract that could compromise the safeguarding of classified information or national security, or for which arrangements for appropriate EFT payments would be impractical due to security considerations.
quote: (d) Payment by EFT under a classified contract could compromise the safeguarding of classified information or national security, or arrangements for appropriate EFT payments would be impractical due to security considerations;

statement: One situation named in the exception for deployed and emergency operations in FAR 32.1103 is a contract awarded by a deployed contracting officer in the course of military operations, including, but not limited to, contingency operations as defined in 2.101.
quote: A contract is awarded by a deployed contracting officer in the course of military operations, including, but not limited to, contingency operations as defined in 2.101,
note: The paragraph attaches the conditions on EFT possibility and operation objectives after both situations; they are stated in the next claim.

statement: The other situation named in that exception is a contract awarded by any contracting officer in the conduct of emergency operations, such as responses to natural disasters or national or civil emergencies, if EFT is not known to be possible or EFT payment would not support the objectives of the operation.
quote: or a contract is awarded by any contracting officer in the conduct of emergency operations, such as responses to natural disasters or national or civil emergencies, if— (1) EFT is not known to be possible; or (2) EFT payment would not support the objectives of the operation;

statement: Two further listed exceptions in FAR 32.1103 are that the agency does not expect to make more than one payment to the same recipient within a one-year period, and that the agency's need for supplies and services is of such unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured unless payment is made by a method other than EFT.
quote: (f) The agency does not expect to make more than one payment to the same recipient within a one-year period; (g) An agency's need for supplies and services is of such unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured unless payment is made by a method other than EFT;

statement: The last two listed exceptions in FAR 32.1103 are that there is only one source for supplies and services and the Government would be seriously injured unless payment is made by a method other than EFT, and that EFT is otherwise not required where authorized by Department of the Treasury Regulations at 31 CFR part 208.
quote: (h) There is only one source for supplies and services and the Government would be seriously injured unless payment is made by a method other than EFT; or (i) Otherwise authorized by Department of the Treasury Regulations at 31 CFR part 208.

statement: FAR 32.1108 says a Governmentwide commercial purchase card charge authorizes the third party that issued the card to make immediate payment to the contractor, and that the Government reimburses the third party at a later date.
quote: A Governmentwide commercial purchase card charge authorizes the third party (e.g., financial institution) that issued the purchase card to make immediate payment to the contractor. The Government reimburses the third party at a later date for the third party's payment to the contractor.

statement: FAR 32.1108 says the contracting officer shall not authorize the Governmentwide commercial purchase card as a method of payment during any period the SAM indicates that the contractor has delinquent debt subject to collection under the TOP.
quote: (ii) The contracting officer shall not authorize the Governmentwide commercial purchase card as a method of payment during any period the SAM indicates that the contractor has delinquent debt subject to collection under the TOP.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—System for Award Management, in solicitations and contracts that include the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management.
quote: (a) The contracting officer shall insert the clause at— (1) 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—System for Award Management, in solicitations and contracts that include the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management,
note: The same paragraph continues with an alternative trigger and exceptions, which are stated in the next claim.

statement: The same paragraph also names an agency clause that requires a contractor to be registered in SAM and maintain registration until final payment as a trigger, and closes with two exceptions, which are payment through a third party arrangement and an exception listed in 32.1103(a) through (i).
quote: or an agency clause that requires a contractor to be registered in SAM and maintain registration until final payment, unless— (i) Payment will be made through a third party arrangement (see 13.301 and paragraph (d) of this section); or (ii) An exception listed in 32.1103(a) through (i) applies.

statement: FAR 32.1110(a)(2)(i) lists the clause at 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other than System for Award Management, for solicitations and contracts that require EFT as the method for payment.
quote: (2) (i) 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other than System for Award Management, in solicitations and contracts that require EFT as the method for payment

statement: FAR 32.1110(a)(2)(i) describes the solicitations and contracts that require EFT as the method for payment as ones that do not include the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management, or a similar agency clause that requires the contractor to be registered in SAM.
quote: but do not include the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management, or a similar agency clause that requires the contractor to be registered in SAM.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that if EFT information is to be submitted to other than the payment office in accordance with agency procedures, the contracting officer shall insert in solicitations and contracts the clause at 52.232-35, Designation of Office for Government Receipt of Electronic Funds Transfer Information.
quote: (c) If EFT information is to be submitted to other than the payment office in accordance with agency procedures, the contracting officer shall insert in solicitations and contracts the clause at 52.232-35, Designation of Office for Government Receipt of Electronic Funds Transfer Information,
note: The printed paragraph continues with an alternative clause substantially the same as 52.232-35, which a later claim states.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that if payment under a written contract will be made by a charge to a Government account with a third party such as a Governmentwide commercial purchase card, the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.232-36, Payment by Third Party, in solicitations and contracts.
quote: (d) If payment under a written contract will be made by a charge to a Government account with a third party such as a Governmentwide commercial purchase card, then the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.232-36, Payment by Third Party, in solicitations and contracts.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that if the contract or agreement provides for the use of delivery orders and provides that the ordering office designate the method of payment for individual orders, the contracting officer shall insert in the solicitation and contract or agreement the clause at 52.232-37.
quote: (e) If the contract or agreement provides for the use of delivery orders, and provides that the ordering office designate the method of payment for individual orders, the contracting officer shall insert, in the solicitation and contract or agreement, the clause at 52.232-37,
note: The printed paragraph continues with the applicable EFT and third party clauses to be inserted as well.

statement: FAR 32.1110(g) applies if the solicitation contains the clause at 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other Than System for Award Management, and an offeror is required to submit EFT information prior to award.
quote: (g) If the solicitation contains the clause at 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other than System for Award Management, and an offeror is required to submit EFT information prior to award—

statement: One listed action under FAR 32.1110(g) is that the contracting officer shall insert in the solicitation the provision at 52.232-38, Submission of Electronic Funds Transfer Information with Offer, or a provision substantially the same.
quote: (1) The contracting officer shall insert in the solicitation the provision at 52.232-38, Submission of Electronic Funds Transfer Information with Offer, or a provision substantially the same;

statement: FAR 32.001 defines a delivery payment as a payment for accepted supplies or services, including accepted partial deliveries, says commercial financing payments are liquidated by deduction from delivery payments, and says delivery payments are invoice payments for prompt payment purposes.
quote: Delivery payment means a payment for accepted supplies or services, including payments for accepted partial deliveries. Commercial financing payments are liquidated by deduction from these payments. Delivery payments are invoice payments for prompt payment purposes.

statement: FAR 32.001 defines an invoice payment as a Government disbursement of monies to a contractor under a contract or other authorization for supplies or services accepted by the Government.
quote: Invoice payment means a Government disbursement of monies to a contractor under a contract or other authorization for supplies or services accepted by the Government.

statement: FAR 32.001 lists payments for accepted partial deliveries and final cost or fee payments where amounts owed have been settled among the invoice payments.
quote: (1) Invoice payments include— (i) Payments for partial deliveries that have been accepted by the Government; (ii) Final cost or fee payments where amounts owed have been settled between the Government and the contractor;

statement: FAR 32.001 lists, for purposes of subpart 32.9 only, all payments made under the Payments Under Fixed-Price Construction Contracts clause and the Payments Under Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts clause among the invoice payments.
quote: (iii) For purposes of subpart 32.9 only, all payments made under the clause at 52.232-5, Payments Under Fixed-Price Construction Contracts, and the clause at 52.232-10, Payments Under Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts;

statement: FAR 32.001 lists interim payments under a cost-reimbursement contract for services, when Alternate I of the Prompt Payment clause is used, among the invoice payments, and says invoice payments do not include contract financing payments.
quote: (iv) Interim payments under a cost-reimbursement contract for services when Alternate I of the clause at 52.232-25, Prompt Payment, is used. (2) Invoice payments do not include contract financing payments.

statement: FAR 32.001 lists progress payments based on a percentage or stage of completion among the contract financing payments, except those made under the Fixed-Price Construction Contracts clause or the Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts clause.
quote: (v) Progress payments based on a percentage or stage of completion (see 32.102(e)), except those made under the clause at 52.232-5, Payments Under Fixed-Price Construction Contracts, or the clause at 52.232-10, Payments Under Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts;

statement: FAR 32.001 lists interim payments under a cost reimbursement contract among the contract financing payments, except for a cost reimbursement contract for services when Alternate I of the Prompt Payment clause is used.
quote: (vi) Interim payments under a cost reimbursement contract, except for a cost reimbursement contract for services when Alternate I of the clause at 52.232-25, Prompt Payment, is used.

statement: FAR 32.001 defines a commercial interim payment as any payment that is not a commercial advance payment or a delivery payment, and says these payments are contract financing payments for prompt payment purposes.
quote: Commercial interim payment means any payment that is not a commercial advance payment or a delivery payment. These payments are contract financing payments for prompt payment purposes

statement: FAR 32.001 defines the designated billing office as the office or person, governmental or nongovernmental, designated in the contract where the contractor first submits invoices and contract financing requests.
quote: Designated billing office means the office or person (governmental or nongovernmental) designated in the contract where the contractor first submits invoices and contract financing requests.

statement: FAR 32.007 says agency heads may prescribe shorter periods for payment of contract financing based on contract pricing or administrative considerations.
quote: (3) Agency heads may prescribe shorter periods for payment based on contract pricing or administrative considerations.

statement: FAR 32.007 says a proper contract financing request must comply with the terms and conditions specified by the contract, and that the contractor must correct any defects in requests submitted in the manner specified in the contract or as directed by the contracting officer.
quote: (c) A proper contract financing request must comply with the terms and conditions specified by the contract. The contractor must correct any defects in requests submitted in the manner specified in the contract or as directed by the contracting officer.

statement: FAR 32.007 says the designated billing office and designated payment office must annotate each contract financing request with the date their respective offices received the request.
quote: (d) The designated billing office and designated payment office must annotate each contract financing request with the date their respective offices received the request.

statement: FAR 32.111(b) says the contracting officer shall insert the clauses listed in that paragraph, appropriately modified with respect to payment due dates in accordance with agency regulations.
quote: (b) The contracting officer shall insert the following clauses, appropriately modified with respect to payment due dates in accordance with agency regulations:

statement: FAR 32.111(b) lists the clause at 52.232-8, Discounts for Prompt Payment, for solicitations and contracts when a fixed-price supply contract or fixed-price service contract is contemplated.
quote: (1) The clause at 52.232-8, Discounts for Prompt Payment, in solicitations and contracts when a fixed-price supply contract or fixed-price service contract is contemplated.

statement: FAR 32.111(b) lists a clause substantially the same as the clause at 52.232-9, Limitation on Withholding of Payments, for solicitations and contracts when a supply, research and development, service, time-and-materials, or labor-hour contract is contemplated.
quote: (2) A clause, substantially the same as the clause at 52.232-9, Limitation on Withholding of Payments, in solicitations and contracts when a supply contract, research and development contract, service contract, time-and-materials contract, or labor-hour contract is contemplated

statement: FAR 32.111(b)(2) describes the contract contemplated as one that includes two or more terms authorizing the temporary withholding of amounts otherwise payable to the contractor for supplies delivered or services performed.
quote: or labor-hour contract is contemplated that includes two or more terms authorizing the temporary withholding of amounts otherwise payable to the contractor for supplies delivered or services performed.

statement: FAR 32.111(a) says that, if the contracting officer determines it is necessary to withhold payment to protect the Government interests, paragraph (a)(7) of the clause permits the contracting officer to unilaterally issue a modification requiring the contractor to withhold 5 percent of amounts due.
quote: If the contracting officer determines that it is necessary to withhold payment to protect the Government's interests, paragraph (a)(7) of the clause permits the contracting officer to unilaterally issue a modification requiring the contractor to withhold 5 percent of amounts due

statement: FAR 32.111(a) says the withholding of 5 percent of amounts due that the modification requires is up to a maximum of $50,000 under the contract.
quote: requiring the contractor to withhold 5 percent of amounts due, up to a maximum of $50,000 under the contract.

statement: FAR 32.502-4 says that, if advance agency approval has been given in accordance with 32.501-1, the contracting officer may substitute a different customary rate for other than small business concerns for the progress payment and liquidation rate indicated.
quote: (2) If advance agency approval has been given in accordance with 32.501-1, the contracting officer may substitute a different customary rate for other than small business concerns for the progress payment and liquidation rate indicated.

statement: FAR 32.502-4 says that, if an unusual progress payment rate is approved for the prime contractor, the approved rate is substituted for the customary rate in paragraphs (a)(1), (a)(6), and (b) of the clause.
quote: (3) If an unusual progress payment rate is approved for the prime contractor (see 32.501-2), substitute the approved rate for the customary rate in paragraphs (a)(1), (a)(6), and (b) of the clause.

statement: FAR 32.502-4 says that, if the liquidation rate is changed from the customary progress payment rate, the new rate is substituted for the rate in paragraphs (a)(1), (a)(6), and (b) of the clause.
quote: (4) If the liquidation rate is changed from the customary progress payment rate (see 32.503-8 and 32.503-9), substitute the new rate for the rate in paragraphs (a)(1), (a)(6), and (b) of the clause.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that, when the clause at 52.232-36 is included in a solicitation or contract, the contracting officer shall also insert the clause at 52.232-33 or the clause at 52.232-34.
quote: When the clause at 52.232-36 is included in a solicitation or contract, the contracting officer shall also insert the clause at 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—System for Award Management, or 52.232-34

statement: FAR 32.1110(d) leaves the choice between the clause at 52.232-33 and the clause at 52.232-34 to be made as appropriate.
quote: or 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other Than System for Award Management, as appropriate.

statement: FAR 32.1110(c) allows, in place of the clause at 52.232-35, a clause substantially the same as 52.232-35 that clearly informs the contractor where to send the EFT information.
quote: or a clause substantially the same as 52.232-35 that clearly informs the contractor where to send the EFT information.

statement: FAR 32.304-5 says the contractor shall also execute an assignment of claims if requested to do so by the guarantor or the financing institution.
quote: (b) The contractor shall also execute an assignment of claims if requested to do so by the guarantor or the financing institution.

statement: Under the codified FAR, certified cost or pricing data are required above $2.5 million for prime contracts awarded on or after July 1, 2018, unless an exception applies.
quote: The threshold for obtaining certified cost or pricing data is $950,000 for prime contracts awarded before July 1, 2018, and $2.5 million for prime contracts awarded on or after July 1, 2018.
note: Not the DoD rule after June 30, 2026: see CL-EST-0002. RFO 15.403-3(a) says meets or exceeds; the codified text says expected to exceed.

statement: For DoD prime contracts awarded after June 30, 2026, certified cost or pricing data are required when the contract is expected to exceed $10 million, unless an exception at FAR 15.403-2 or DFARS 215.403-71 applies.
quote: obtain certified cost or pricing data when a prime contract is expected to exceed $10 million and is awarded after June 30, 2026
note: Replaces FAR 15.403-3(a) for DoD. Subcontracts under primes entered on or before June 30, 2026 keep $2.5 million when the prime and each higher tier must submit certified data; a DoD prime awarded on or before that date stays at $2.5 million unless the contract states otherwise (pp. 23-24). Effective date is the memo's signature date; it says effective immediately.

statement: Before agreement on price, a contracting officer who learns that certified cost or pricing data are inaccurate, incomplete or noncurrent must immediately bring the matter to the prospective contractor's attention, whether the defective data increase or decrease the price.
quote: the contracting officer shall immediately bring the matter to the attention of the prospective contractor, whether the defective data increase or decrease the contract price

statement: After award, if certified cost or pricing data are found inaccurate, incomplete or noncurrent as of the date of final agreement on price or an earlier date agreed by the parties on the Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data, the Government is entitled to a price adjustment, including profit or fee, of any significant amount by which the price was increased because of the defective data.
quote: the Government is entitled to a price adjustment, including profit or fee, of any significant amount by which the price was increased because of the defective data

statement: Subject to the conditions in (b)(5) and (b)(6), the contracting officer allows an offset for understated certified cost or pricing data submitted in support of price negotiations, up to the amount of the Government's claim for overstated data arising out of the same pricing action.
quote: the contracting officer shall allow an offset for any understated certified cost or pricing data submitted in support of price negotiations, up to the amount of the Government's claim for overstated pricing data

statement: The Government's right to a price adjustment is not affected by the contractor or subcontractor having been a sole source supplier or otherwise being in a superior bargaining position.
quote: The contractor or subcontractor was a sole source supplier or otherwise was in a superior bargaining position

statement: An overpayment for defective pricing purposes occurs only when payment is made for supplies or services accepted by the Government, and amounts paid as contract financing do not create an overpayment.
quote: Overpayment occurs only when payment is made for supplies or services accepted by the Government. Overpayments do not result from amounts paid for contract financing

statement: Where the submission of defective certified cost or pricing data was a knowing submission, the contracting officer obtains a penalty equal to the amount of the overpayment, and must obtain the advice of counsel before taking contractual action concerning penalties.
quote: the contracting officer shall obtain an amount equal to the amount of overpayment made. Before taking any contractual actions concerning penalties, the contracting officer shall obtain the advice of counsel

statement: The contracting officer may not reprice a contract solely because the profit was greater than forecast or because a contingency specified in the submission failed to materialize.
quote: The contracting officer shall not reprice the contract solely because the profit was greater than forecast or because a contingency specified in the submission failed to materialize.

statement: For each advisory audit received based on a postaward review that indicates defective pricing, the contracting officer determines whether the data submitted were defective and relied upon, and should first give the contractor an opportunity to support the accuracy, completeness and currency of the data.
quote: the contracting officer shall make a determination as to whether or not the data submitted were defective and relied upon

statement: When a prime contractor priced its proposal with defective subcontract data but later awards the subcontract at a lower price or does not subcontract the work, the prime contract price adjustment is limited to the difference, plus applicable indirect cost and profit markups, between the subcontract price used for pricing the prime contract and the amount stated in the next claim.
quote: any adjustment in the prime contract price due to defective subcontract data is limited to the difference (plus applicable indirect cost and profit markups) between the subcontract price used for pricing the prime contract

statement: The objective of proposal analysis is to ensure that the final agreed-to price is fair and reasonable.
quote: The objective of proposal analysis is to ensure that the final agreed-to price is fair and reasonable.

statement: Price analysis is used when certified cost or pricing data are not required.
quote: Price analysis shall be used when certified cost or pricing data are not required

statement: Cost analysis is used to evaluate the reasonableness of individual cost elements when certified cost or pricing data are required.
quote: Cost analysis shall be used to evaluate the reasonableness of individual cost elements when certified cost or pricing data are required.

statement: Cost analysis may also be used on data other than certified cost or pricing data to determine cost reasonableness or cost realism when a fair and reasonable price cannot be determined through price analysis alone.
quote: Cost analysis may also be used to evaluate data other than certified cost or pricing data to determine cost reasonableness or cost realism when a fair and reasonable price cannot be determined through price analysis alone.

statement: The first two price analysis techniques are the preferred techniques, but if information on competitive proposed prices or previous contract prices is unavailable or insufficient to establish a fair and reasonable price, the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques.
quote: information on competitive proposed prices or previous contract prices is not available or is insufficient to determine that the price is fair and reasonable, the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques as appropriate to the circumstances applicable to the acquisition.

statement: Cost realism analyses are performed on cost-reimbursement contracts to determine the probable cost of performance for each offeror.
quote: Cost realism analyses shall be performed on cost-reimbursement contracts to determine the probable cost of performance for each offeror.

statement: The probable cost produced by cost realism analysis is used for purposes of evaluation to determine the best value.
quote: The probable cost shall be used for purposes of evaluation to determine the best value.

statement: Where cost realism analysis is used on competitive fixed-price incentive contracts or on other competitive fixed-price-type contracts, the proposals are still evaluated using the criteria in the solicitation and the offered prices are not adjusted as a result of the analysis.
quote: proposals shall be evaluated using the criteria in the solicitation, and the offered prices shall not be adjusted as a result of the analysis

statement: Recommendations or conclusions about the Government's review of a proposal are not disclosed to the offeror or contractor without the concurrence of the contracting officer.
quote: Recommendations or conclusions regarding the Government's review or analysis of an offeror's or contractor's proposal shall not be disclosed to the offeror or contractor without the concurrence of the contracting officer

statement: Normally, adequate price competition establishes a fair and reasonable price.
quote: Normally, adequate price competition establishes a fair and reasonable price

statement: An offer may be rejected if the contracting officer determines that the lack of price balance poses an unacceptable risk to the Government.
quote: An offer may be rejected if the contracting officer determines that the lack of balance poses an unacceptable risk to the Government.

statement: An acceptable estimating system must produce verifiable, supportable, documented and timely cost estimates that are an acceptable basis for negotiation of fair and reasonable prices, in addition to being maintained, reliable and consistently applied.
quote: (1) Is maintained, reliable, and consistently applied; (2) Produces verifiable, supportable, documented, and timely cost estimates that are an acceptable basis for negotiation of fair and reasonable prices

statement: An estimating system is the contractor's policies, procedures and practices for budgeting and planning controls and for generating estimates of costs and other data included in proposals submitted in the expectation of receiving contract awards.
quote: the Contractor's policies, procedures, and practices for budgeting and planning controls, and generating estimates of costs and other data included in proposals submitted to customers in the expectation of receiving contract awards.

statement: The contractor must establish, maintain and comply with an acceptable estimating system.
quote: The Contractor shall establish, maintain, and comply with an acceptable estimating system.

statement: One condition under which paragraphs (d) and (e) apply to a large business is that, in its fiscal year preceding award, it received Department of Defense prime contracts or subcontracts totaling $50 million or more for which certified cost or pricing data were required.
quote: In its fiscal year preceding award of this contract, received Department of Defense (DoD) prime contracts or subcontracts, totaling $50 million or more for which certified cost or pricing data were required

statement: For a large business that, in its fiscal year before award, received DoD prime contracts or subcontracts totaling $10 million or more but less than $50 million for which certified cost or pricing data were required, paragraphs (d) and (e) apply only if the contracting officer has also notified it in writing that they apply.
quote: Was notified, in writing, by the Contracting Officer that paragraphs (d) and (e) of this clause apply

statement: The contractor discloses its estimating system to the administrative contracting officer in writing.
quote: The Contractor shall disclose its estimating system to the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO), in writing

statement: An estimating system disclosure is acceptable when the documentation both accurately describes the policies, procedures and practices the contractor currently uses in preparing cost proposals and provides sufficient detail for the Government to reasonably make an informed judgment on the acceptability of its estimating practices.
quote: Accurately describes those policies, procedures, and practices that the Contractor currently uses in preparing cost proposals

statement: The contractor must disclose significant changes to its cost estimating system to the administrative contracting officer on a timely basis.
quote: Disclose significant changes to the cost estimating system to the ACO on a timely basis

statement: An acceptable estimating system establishes clear responsibility for preparation, review and approval of cost estimates and budgets.
quote: Establish clear responsibility for preparation, review, and approval of cost estimates and budgets

statement: The system must identify and document the sources of data and the estimating methods and rationale used in developing cost estimates and budgets.
quote: Identify and document the sources of data and the estimating methods and rationale used in developing cost estimates and budgets

statement: The system must provide for internal review of, and accountability for, the acceptability of the estimating system, including the budgetary data supporting indirect cost estimates and comparisons of projected results to actual results.
quote: Provide for internal review of, and accountability for, the acceptability of the estimating system, including the budgetary data supporting indirect cost estimates and comparisons of projected results to actual results

statement: The contractor must respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the contracting officer that identifies material weaknesses in its estimating system.
quote: The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor's estimating system.

statement: After a final determination of material weaknesses, the contractor must within 45 days of receipt either correct the weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate them.
quote: within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material weaknesses

statement: If the contracting officer makes a final determination to disapprove the contractor's estimating system and the contract includes the Contractor Business Systems clause, the contracting officer withholds payments in accordance with that clause.
quote: the Contracting Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause

statement: Certified cost or pricing data shall not be obtained for acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold.
quote: Certified cost or pricing data shall not be obtained for acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold.

statement: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data to support any action, including contracts, subcontracts, or modifications, when one of the listed circumstances applies.
quote: contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data to support any action (contracts, subcontracts, or modifications) (but may require data other than certified cost or pricing data as defined in FAR 2.101 to support a determination of a fair and reasonable price or cost realism)—

statement: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data when the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on adequate price competition.
quote: When the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on adequate price competition

statement: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data when the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on prices set by law or regulation.
quote: When the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on prices set by law or regulation

statement: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data when a commercial product or commercial service is being acquired.
quote: When a commercial product or commercial serviceis being acquired

statement: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data when a waiver has been granted.
quote: When a waiver has been granted (see standards in paragraph (c)(4) of this subsection)

statement: A price is based on adequate price competition when two or more responsible offerors, competing independently, submit priced offers that satisfy the Government's expressed requirement, together with the further conditions stated in the next claim.
quote: Two or more responsible offerors, competing independently, submit priced offers that satisfy the Government's expressed requirement

statement: The head of the contracting activity may, without power of delegation, waive the requirement for submission of certified cost or pricing data in exceptional cases.
quote: The head of the contracting activity (HCA) may, without power of delegation, waive the requirement for submission of certified cost or pricing data in exceptional cases.

statement: This subsection prescribes policies for establishing the profit or fee portion of the Government prenegotiation objective in price negotiations based on cost analysis.
quote: This subsection prescribes policies for establishing the profit or fee portion of the Government prenegotiation objective in price negotiations based on cost analysis.

statement: Profit or fee prenegotiation objectives do not necessarily represent net income to contractors; they represent that element of the potential total remuneration that contractors may receive for contract performance over and above allowable costs.
quote: Profit or fee prenegotiation objectives do not necessarily represent net income to contractors. Rather, they represent that element of the potential total remuneration that contractors may receive for contract performance over and above allowable costs.

statement: For experimental, developmental, or research work performed under a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract, the fee shall not exceed 15 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.
quote: For experimental, developmental, or research work performed under a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract, the fee shall not exceed 15 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.

statement: For architect-engineer services for public works or utilities, the contract price or the estimated cost and fee for production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings, and specifications shall not exceed 6 percent of the estimated cost of construction of the public work or utility, excluding fees.
quote: For architect-engineer services for public works or utilities, the contract price or the estimated cost and fee for production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings, and specifications shall not exceed 6 percent of the estimated cost of construction of the public work or utility, excluding fees.

statement: For other cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts, the fee shall not exceed 10 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.
quote: For other cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts, the fee shall not exceed 10 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.

statement: When the price negotiation is not based on cost analysis, contracting officers are not required to analyze profit.
