statement: The suitability sentence in FAR 16.202-2 first names commercial products or commercial services, and other supplies or services bought on reasonably definite functional or detailed specifications, as the things a firm-fixed-price contract is suitable for acquiring.
quote: A firm-fixed-price contract is suitable for acquiring commercial products or commercial services (see parts 2 and 12) or for acquiring other supplies or services on the basis of reasonably definite functional or detailed specifications (see part 11)
note: The condition that follows in the same sentence, that the contracting officer can establish fair and reasonable prices at the outset, is carried by CL-EST-1152.

statement: The suitability sentence applies when the contracting officer can establish fair and reasonable prices at the outset, such as when there is adequate price competition.
quote: when the contracting officer can establish fair and reasonable prices at the outset, such as when— (a) There is adequate price competition;

statement: Two further listed examples are reasonable price comparisons with prior purchases of the same or similar supplies or services made on a competitive basis or supported by valid certified cost or pricing data, and available cost or pricing information that permits realistic estimates of the probable costs of performance.
quote: (b) There are reasonable price comparisons with prior purchases of the same or similar supplies or services made on a competitive basis or supported by valid certified cost or pricing data; (c) Available cost or pricing information permits realistic estimates of the probable costs of performance; or

statement: One listed example is that performance uncertainties can be identified and reasonable estimates of their cost impact can be made, and the contractor is willing to accept a firm fixed price representing assumption of the risks involved.
quote: (d) Performance uncertainties can be identified and reasonable estimates of their cost impact can be made, and the contractor is willing to accept a firm fixed price representing assumption of the risks involved.

statement: A fixed-price contract with economic price adjustment provides for upward and downward revision of the stated contract price upon the occurrence of specified contingencies.
quote: A fixed-price contract with economic price adjustment provides for upward and downward revision of the stated contract price upon the occurrence of specified contingencies.

statement: Economic price adjustments are of three general types, the first being adjustments based on established prices, which are based on increases or decreases from an agreed-upon level in published or otherwise established prices of specific items or the contract end items.
quote: Economic price adjustments are of three general types: (1) Adjustments based on established prices. These price adjustments are based on increases or decreases from an agreed-upon level in published or otherwise established prices of specific items or the contract end items.

statement: One listed type is adjustments based on actual costs of labor or material, which are based on increases or decreases in specified costs of labor or material that the contractor actually experiences during contract performance.
quote: (2) Adjustments based on actual costs of labor or material. These price adjustments are based on increases or decreases in specified costs of labor or material that the contractor actually experiences during contract performance.
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in that names the three general types is in the claim for the first type.

statement: One listed type is adjustments based on cost indexes of labor or material, which are based on increases or decreases in labor or material cost standards or indexes that are specifically identified in the contract.
quote: (3) Adjustments based on cost indexes of labor or material. These price adjustments are based on increases or decreases in labor or material cost standards or indexes that are specifically identified in the contract.
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in that names the three general types is in the claim for the first type.

statement: A fixed-price contract with economic price adjustment may be used when there is serious doubt concerning the stability of market or labor conditions during an extended period of contract performance and contingencies that would otherwise be included in the contract price can be identified and covered separately in the contract.
quote: may be used when (i) there is serious doubt concerning the stability of market or labor conditions that will exist during an extended period of contract performance, and (ii) contingencies that would otherwise be included in the contract price can be identified and covered separately in the contract
note: The quote starts after the subject of the sentence, which is a fixed-price contract with economic price adjustment, and stops before the final full stop to stay within 300 characters.

statement: In establishing the base level from which adjustment will be made, the contracting officer shall ensure that contingency allowances are not duplicated by inclusion in both the base price and the adjustment the contractor requests under the economic price adjustment clause.
quote: In establishing the base level from which adjustment will be made, the contracting officer shall ensure that contingency allowances are not duplicated by inclusion in both the base price and the adjustment requested by the contractor under economic price adjustment clause.

statement: In contracts that do not require submission of certified cost or pricing data, the contracting officer shall obtain adequate data to establish the base level from which adjustment will be made and may require verification of the data submitted.
quote: In contracts that do not require submission of certified cost or pricing data, the contracting officer shall obtain adequate data to establish the base level from which adjustment will be made and may require verification of data submitted.

statement: A fixed-price contract with economic price adjustment shall not be used unless the contracting officer determines that it is necessary either to protect the contractor and the Government against significant fluctuations in labor or material costs or to provide for contract price adjustment in the event of changes in the contractor's established prices.
quote: shall not be used unless the contracting officer determines that it is necessary either to protect the contractor and the Government against significant fluctuations in labor or material costs or to provide for contract price adjustment in the event of changes in the contractor's established prices.
note: The quote starts after the subject of the sentence, which is a fixed-price contract with economic price adjustment.

statement: FAR 16.204 says fixed-price incentive contracts are covered in subpart 16.4, Incentive Contracts, and points to 16.403 for more complete descriptions, application and limitations and to 16.406 for the prescribed clauses.
quote: Fixed-price incentive contracts are covered in subpart 16.4, Incentive Contracts. See 16.403 for more complete descriptions, application, and limitations for these contracts. Prescribed clauses are found at 16.406.

statement: The contracting officer shall, when contracting by negotiation, insert the clause at FAR 52.216-2 or an agency-prescribed clause as authorized in paragraph (a)(2) in solicitations and contracts when all of the listed conditions apply.
quote: The contracting officer shall, when contracting by negotiation, insert the clause at 52.216-2, Economic Price Adjustment—Standard Supplies, or an agency-prescribed clause as authorized in subparagraph (2) below, in solicitations and contracts when all of the following conditions apply:

quote: (i) A fixed-price contract is contemplated. (ii) The requirement is for standard supplies that have an established catalog or market price. (iii) The contracting officer has made the determination specified in 16.203-3.
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in is in the claim for paragraph (a)(1).

statement: The contracting officer may modify the clause at FAR 52.216-2 by increasing the 10 percent limit on aggregate increases specified in its paragraph (c)(1), upon approval by the chief of the contracting office.
quote: (4) The contracting officer may modify the clause by increasing the 10 percent limit on aggregate increases specified in 52.216-2(c)(1), upon approval by the chief of the contracting office.

statement: The contracting officer shall, when contracting by negotiation, insert the clause at FAR 52.216-3 or an agency-prescribed clause as authorized in paragraph (b)(2) in solicitations and contracts when all of the listed conditions apply.

statement: One listed condition for the clause at FAR 52.216-3 is that a fixed price contract is contemplated.
quote: (i) A fixed price contract is contemplated.
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in is in the claim for paragraph (b)(1). The text without a hyphen in fixed price is the printed wording of paragraph (b)(1)(i).

statement: Two further listed conditions for the clause at FAR 52.216-3 are that the requirement is for semistandard supplies whose prices can be reasonably related to the prices of nearly equivalent standard supplies that have an established catalog or market price, and that the contracting officer has made the determination specified in 16.203-3.
quote: (ii) The requirement is for semistandard supplies for which the prices can be reasonably related to the prices of nearly equivalent standard supplies that have an established catalog or market price. (iii) The contracting officer has made the determination specified in 16.203-3.
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in is in the claim for paragraph (b)(1).

statement: The contracting officer may modify the clause at FAR 52.216-3 by increasing the 10 percent limit on aggregate increases specified in its paragraph (c)(1), upon approval by the chief of the contracting office.
quote: (6) The contracting officer may modify the clause by increasing the 10 percent limit on aggregate increases specified in 52.216-3(c)(1), upon approval by the chief of the contracting office.

statement: The contracting officer shall, when contracting by negotiation, insert a clause substantially the same as the clause at FAR 52.216-4 or an agency-prescribed clause as authorized in paragraph (c)(2).
quote: The contracting officer shall, when contracting by negotiation, insert a clause that is substantially the same as the clause at 52.216-4, Economic Price Adjustment—Labor and Material, or an agency-prescribed clause as authorized in subparagraph (2) below

statement: The insertion in paragraph (c)(1) applies in solicitations and contracts when all of the listed conditions apply, the first two being that a fixed-price contract is contemplated and that no major element of design engineering or development work is involved.
quote: in solicitation and contracts when all of the following conditions apply: (i) A fixed-price contract is contemplated. (ii) There is no major element of design engineering or development work involved.

statement: Two further listed conditions are that one or more identifiable labor or material cost factors are subject to change and that the contracting officer has made the determination specified in 16.203-3.
quote: (iii) One or more identifiable labor or material cost factors are subject to change. (iv) The contracting officer has made the determination specified in 16.203-3.
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in is in the claim for the conditions on paragraph (c)(1).

statement: The contracting officer may modify the clause at FAR 52.216-4 by increasing the 10 percent limit on aggregate increases specified in its paragraph (c)(4), upon approval by the chief of the contracting office.
quote: (5) The contracting officer may modify the clause by increasing the 10 percent limit on aggregate increases specified in 52.216-4(c)(4), upon approval by the chief of the contracting office.

statement: DFARS says to use the clauses at FAR 52.216-2, 52.216-3 and 52.216-4 generally only when the conditions that follow are met.
quote: (1) Generally, use the clauses at FAR 52.216-2, Economic Price Adjustment—Standard Supplies, FAR 52.216-3, Economic Price Adjustment—Semistandard Supplies, and FAR 52.216-4, Economic Price Adjustment—Labor and Material, only when—
note: Instrument is the DFARS; the quote names the three FAR clauses. The two listed conditions are in the next claim.

statement: The two listed conditions are that the total contract price exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and that delivery or performance will not be completed within 6 months after contract award.
quote: (i) The total contract price exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold; and (ii) Delivery or performance will not be completed within 6 months after contract award.
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in is in the claim for the opening of paragraph (1). The simplified acquisition threshold amount is not printed in this section.

statement: Under DFARS 216.203-4-70(a)(1)(i), the price adjustment clause for basic steel, aluminum, brass, bronze, or copper mill products may be used in fixed-price supply solicitations and contracts for those products when an established catalog or market price exists for the particular product being acquired.
quote: may be used in fixed-price supply solicitations and contracts for basic steel, aluminum, brass, bronze, or copper mill products, such as sheets, plates, and bars, when an established catalog or market price exists for the particular product being acquired.

quote: (ii) The 10 percent figure in paragraph (d)(1) of the clause shall not be exceeded unless approval is obtained at a level above the contracting officer.
note: The section says a level above the contracting officer and does not name an office.

statement: The price adjustment clause at 252.216-7001, Economic Price Adjustment, Nonstandard Steel Items, may be used in fixed-price supply contracts when the conditions that follow are met.
quote: (1) The price adjustment clause at 252.216-7001, Economic Price Adjustment—Nonstandard Steel Items, may be used in fixed-price supply contracts when—

statement: The two listed conditions are that the contractor is a steel producer and actually manufactures the standard steel mill item referred to in the base steel index definition of the clause, and that the items being acquired are nonstandard steel items made wholly or in part of standard steel mill items.
quote: (i) The contractor is a steel producer and actually manufacture the standard steel mill item referred to in the “base steel index” definition of the clause; and (ii) The items being acquired are nonstandard steel items made wholly or in part of standard steel mill items.
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in is in the claim for paragraph (b)(1). The printed source reads "actually manufacture".

statement: One listed requirement is that the ten percent figure in paragraph (e)(4) of the clause at 252.216-7001 shall not be exceeded unless approval is obtained at a level above the contracting officer.
quote: (5) The ten percent figure in paragraph (e)(4) of the clause shall not be exceeded unless approval is obtained at a level above the contracting officer.
note: The section says a level above the contracting officer and does not name an office.

statement: The price adjustment clause at 252.216-7003, Economic Price Adjustment, Wage Rates or Material Prices Controlled by a Foreign Government, may be used in fixed-price supply and service solicitations and contracts when the conditions that follow are met.
quote: The price adjustment clause at 252.216-7003, Economic Price Adjustment—Wage Rates or Material Prices Controlled by a Foreign Government, may be used in fixed-price supply and service solicitations and contracts when—

statement: The two listed conditions are that the contract is to be performed wholly or in part in a foreign country, and that a foreign government controls wage rates or material prices and may impose a mandatory change in wages or prices of material during contract performance.
quote: (A) The contract is to be performed wholly or in part in a foreign country; and (B) A foreign government controls wage rates or material prices and may, during contract performance, impose a mandatory change in wages or prices of material.
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in is in the claim for paragraph (c)(1)(i).

statement: The offeror represents that the unit price stated in its offer for the identified item is not in excess of its established price in effect on the date set for opening of bids, or on the contract date if the contract is to be negotiated, for like quantities of the same item.
quote: represents that the unit price stated in this offer for ________________ (Identify the item) is not in excess of the offeror's established price in effect on the date set for opening of bids (or the contract date if this is to be a negotiated contract) for like quantities of the same item.
note: The quote starts after the words that say the representation is made by submission of the offer.

statement: The contractor shall promptly notify the Contracting Officer of the amount and effective date of each decrease in any established price, and each corresponding contract unit price shall be decreased by the same percentage that the established price is decreased.
quote: The Contractor shall promptly notify the Contracting Officer of the amount and effective date of each decrease in any established price. (1) Each corresponding contract unit price shall be decreased by the same percentage that the established price is decreased.

statement: If the contractor's established price is increased after the date set for opening of bids, or after the contract date for a negotiated contract, the corresponding contract unit price is to be increased by the same percentage upon the contractor's written request to the Contracting Officer.
quote: after the date set for opening of bids (or the contract date if this is a negotiated contract), upon the Contractor's written request to the Contracting Officer, the corresponding contract unit price shall be increased by the same percentage that the established price is increased
note: The quote starts after the opening words of the sentence and stops before the words 'and this contract shall be modified accordingly, provided', which are carried by CL-EST-1200 together with the conditions listed after them.

statement: One listed condition on an increase is that the aggregate of the increases in any contract unit price shall not exceed 10 percent of the original contract unit price.
quote: (1) The aggregate of the increases in any contract unit price under this contract shall not exceed 10 percent of the original contract unit price;
note: The quote carries no lead-in; the lead-in with the word "provided" is in the claim for the increase.

statement: One listed condition is that the increased contract unit price takes the effective date of the increase in the established price if the Contracting Officer receives the contractor's written request within ten days of the change, and otherwise the date the Contracting Officer receives the request.
quote: the effective date of the increase in the applicable established price if the Contractor's written request is received by the Contracting Officer within ten days of the change. If it is not, the effective date of the increased unit price shall be the date of receipt of the request
note: The quote starts after the words "shall be effective on" and carries no lead-in; the lead-in with the word "provided" is in the claim for the increase.

statement: One listed condition is that the Contracting Officer shall not execute a modification incorporating an increase in a contract unit price under the clause until the increase is verified.
quote: (4) The Contracting Officer shall not execute a modification incorporating an increase in a contract unit price under this clause until the increase is verified.

statement: Within 30 days after receipt of the contractor's written request, the Contracting Officer may cancel, without liability to either party, any portion of the contract affected by the requested increase and not delivered at the time of cancellation, subject to listed exceptions.
quote: (e) Within 30 days after receipt of the Contractor's written request, the Contracting Officer may cancel, without liability to either party, any portion of the contract affected by the requested increase and not delivered at the time of such cancellation, except as follows—

statement: The clause defines the base steel index as the contractor's established price including all applicable extras for the identified item on the date set for bid opening or the date of submission of the offer.
quote: Base steel index means the Contractor's established price (see note 6) including all applicable extras of $________ per __________ (see note 1) for __________ (see note 2) on the date set for bid opening (or the date of submission of the offer).

statement: The clause defines the current steel index as the contractor's established price for that item, including all applicable extras, in effect a stated number of days before the first day of the month in which delivery is required.
quote: Current steel index means the Contractor's established price (see note 6) for that item, including all applicable extras in effect ________ days (see note 3) prior to the first day of the month in which delivery is required.
note: The number of days is a blank the offeror fills in under a note to the clause.

statement: One listed provision of the clause says the aggregate of the increases in any contract unit price shall not exceed ten percent of the original contract unit price.
quote: (4) The aggregate of the increases in any contract unit price under this contract shall not exceed ten percent of the original contract unit price.

statement: Within 30 days after final delivery, or such other period as the Contracting Officer authorizes, the contractor shall furnish a statement identifying the correctness of the items listed in the paragraph.
quote: Within 30 days after final delivery (or such other period as may be authorized by the Contracting Officer), the Contractor shall furnish a statement identifying the correctness of—
note: The quote stops at the lead-in of the two items; they are quoted in CL-EST-1201 and CL-EST-1202.

statement: No modification will be made under the clause until the Contracting Officer has verified the revised established price.
quote: No modification to this contract will be made pursuant to this clause until the Contracting Officer has verified the revised established price

statement: One listed rule is that an increase in contract unit prices is effective on the same date the foreign government increased the wage rate or material price, but only if the Contracting Officer receives the contractor's written request within 10 days of the change.
quote: shall be effective on the same date that the government named in paragraph (a) of this clause increased the applicable wage rate(s) or material price(s), but only if the Contracting Officer receives the Contractor's written request for contract adjustment within 10 days of the change.
note: The quote starts after the words 'For increases in established wage rates or material prices, the increase in contract unit price(s)'. The adjustment these rules sit under is carried by CL-EST-1204.

statement: If the contractor's written request for an increase is received later than the ten days stated in the preceding sentence of the clause, the effective date is the date the Contracting Officer received the request.
quote: If the Contractor's request is received later, the effective date shall be the date that the Contracting Officer received the Contractor's request.
note: "Later" refers to the 10 days stated in the sentence before it, which is quoted in the claim for increases.

statement: Another listed rule is that for decreases in established wage rates or material prices, the decrease in contract unit prices shall be effective on the same date that the foreign government decreased the applicable wage rate or material price.
quote: (2) For decreases in established wage rates or material prices, the decrease in contract unit price(s) shall be effective on the same date that the government named in paragraph (a) of this clause decreased the applicable wage rate(s) or material price(s).

statement: No modification changing the contract unit prices shall be executed until the Contracting Officer has verified the applicable change in the rates or prices set by the foreign government.
quote: (c) No modification changing the contract unit price(s) shall be executed until the Contracting Officer has verified the applicable change in the rates or prices set by the government named in paragraph (a) of this clause.

statement: The increase in the corresponding contract unit price and the resulting modification of the contract are made provided that the conditions listed after the word provided in paragraph (d) are met.
quote: the corresponding contract unit price shall be increased by the same percentage that the established price is increased, and this contract shall be modified accordingly, provided—

statement: One item whose correctness the contractor's statement identifies is the average straight time hourly earnings of its employees in the identified shop that are relevant to the computations of the base labor index and the current labor index.
quote: (i) The average straight time hourly earnings of the Contractor's employees in the shop identified in paragraph (a) that are relevant to the computations of the base labor index and the current labor index;
note: The lead-in to this item is in CL-EST-1194.

statement: The other item whose correctness the contractor's statement identifies is its established prices, including all applicable extras for like quantities of the item, that are relevant to the computation of the base steel index and the current steel index.
quote: (ii) The Contractor's established prices (see note 6), including all applicable extras for like quantities of the item that are relevant to the computation of the base steel index and the current steel index.
note: The lead-in to this item is in CL-EST-1194.

quote: 3 Offeror insert best estimate of the number of days required for processing the standard steel mill item in the shop identified under the labor index definition.
note: This note explains the blank for days in the current steel index definition quoted in CL-EST-1192.

statement: Under the clause, the Contracting Officer shall make an equitable adjustment in the contract price and modify the contract to the extent that the contractor's actual costs of performing the contract are increased or decreased as a direct result of a revision, subject to the listed rules.
quote: the Contracting Officer shall make an equitable adjustment in the contract price and shall modify the contract to the extent that the Contractor's actual costs of performing this contract are increased or decreased, as a direct result of the revision, subject to the following:

statement: Price adjustments based on established prices should normally be restricted to industry-wide contingencies, and price adjustments based on labor and material costs should be limited to contingencies beyond the contractor's control.
quote: Price adjustments based on established prices should normally be restricted to industry-wide contingencies. Price adjustments based on labor and material costs should be limited to contingencies beyond the contractor's control.
note: These are the two sentences that follow the sentence quoted in CL-EST-1159.

statement: The clause at FAR 52.216-4, Economic Price Adjustment, Labor and Material, is prescribed in the paragraph headed adjustments based on actual cost of labor or material.

statement: The clause at FAR 52.216-3, Economic Price Adjustment, Semistandard Supplies, is prescribed in the paragraph headed adjustment based on established prices for semistandard supplies.
quote: (b) Adjustment based on established prices—semistandard supplies. (1) The contracting officer shall, when contracting by negotiation, insert the clause at 52.216-3, Economic Price Adjustment—Semistandard Supplies,
note: The rest of the sentence and its conditions are in CL-EST-1167, CL-EST-1168 and CL-EST-1169.

statement: A fixed-price incentive contract is a fixed-price contract that provides for adjusting profit and establishing the final contract price by a formula based on the relationship of final negotiated total cost to total target cost.
quote: A fixed-price incentive contract is a fixed-price contract that provides for adjusting profit and establishing the final contract price by a formula based on the relationship of final negotiated total cost to total target cost.

statement: Contracting officers shall purchase supplies and services from responsible sources at fair and reasonable prices.
quote: 15.402 Pricing policy. Contracting officers shall— (a) Purchase supplies and services from responsible sources at fair and reasonable prices.

statement: In establishing the reasonableness of offered prices, the contracting officer shall obtain certified cost or pricing data when required by the cross-referenced section, along with data other than certified cost or pricing data as necessary to establish a fair and reasonable price.
quote: In establishing the reasonableness of the offered prices, the contracting officer— (1) Shall obtain certified cost or pricing data when required by 15.403-4, along with data other than certified cost or pricing data as necessary to establish a fair and reasonable price; or

statement: When certified cost or pricing data are not required, the contracting officer shall obtain data other than certified cost or pricing data as necessary to establish a fair and reasonable price, generally using a listed order of preference in determining the type of data required.
quote: (2) When certified cost or pricing data are not required by 15.403-4, shall obtain data other than certified cost or pricing data as necessary to establish a fair and reasonable price, generally using the following order of preference in determining the type of data required:

statement: One listed item in the order of preference is no additional data from the offeror if the price is based on adequate price competition, except as provided by a cross-referenced paragraph.
quote: (i) No additional data from the offeror, if the price is based on adequate price competition, except as provided by 15.403-3(b).

statement: For data related to prices, the contracting officer relies first on data available within the Government, second on data obtained from sources other than the offeror, and, if necessary, on data obtained from the offeror.
quote: (A) Data related to prices (e.g., established catalog or market prices, sales to non-governmental and governmental entities), relying first on data available within the Government; second, on data obtained from sources other than the offeror; and, if necessary, on data obtained from the offeror.

statement: When obtaining data from the offeror is necessary, then unless an exception under the cross-referenced paragraphs applies, the price data the offeror submits shall include, at a minimum, appropriate data on the prices at which the same or similar items have been sold previously.
quote: When obtaining data from the offeror is necessary, unless an exception under 15.403-1(b)(1) or (2) applies, such data submitted by the offeror shall include, at a minimum, appropriate data on the prices at which the same or similar items have been sold previously

statement: One listed duty of the contracting officer is to obtain the type and quantity of data necessary to establish a fair and reasonable price, but not more data than is necessary.
quote: (3) Obtain the type and quantity of data necessary to establish a fair and reasonable price, but not more data than is necessary.

statement: If the contracting officer cannot establish a fair and reasonable price from the analyses of the data obtained or submitted to date, the contracting officer shall require the submission of additional data sufficient for the contracting officer to support the determination.
quote: If a fair and reasonable price cannot be established by the contracting officer from the analyses of the data obtained or submitted to date, the contracting officer shall require the submission of additional data sufficient for the contracting officer to support the determination

statement: The purpose of performing cost or price analysis is to develop a negotiation position that permits the contracting officer and the offeror an opportunity to reach agreement on a fair and reasonable price.
quote: (a) The purpose of performing cost or price analysis is to develop a negotiation position that permits the contracting officer and the offeror an opportunity to reach agreement on a fair and reasonable price.

statement: The contracting officer shall document in the contract file the principal elements of the negotiated agreement, and the documentation, for example a price negotiation memorandum, shall include listed items.
quote: (a) The contracting officer shall document in the contract file the principal elements of the negotiated agreement. The documentation (e.g., price negotiation memorandum (PNM)) shall include the following:

statement: One listed item of the documentation is the current status of any contractor systems, such as purchasing, estimating, accounting and compensation, to the extent they affected and were considered in the negotiation.
quote: (4) The current status of any contractor systems (e.g., purchasing, estimating, accounting, and compensation) to the extent they affected and were considered in the negotiation.

quote: (7) A summary of the contractor's proposal, any field pricing assistance recommendations, including the reasons for any pertinent variances from them, the Government's negotiation objective, and the negotiated position.

statement: Where the determination of a fair and reasonable price is based on cost analysis the summary shall address each major cost element, and where it is based on price analysis the summary shall include the source and type of data used to support the determination.
quote: Where the determination of a fair and reasonable price is based on cost analysis, the summary shall address each major cost element. When determination of a fair and reasonable price is based on price analysis, the summary shall include the source and type of data used to support the determination.

statement: One listed item of the documentation is the basis for the profit or fee prenegotiation objective and the profit or fee negotiated.
quote: (10) The basis for the profit or fee prenegotiation objective and the profit or fee negotiated.

statement: Taking into consideration the pricing policy, the contracting officer shall specify in the solicitation, among listed items, whether certified cost or pricing data are required.
quote: (a) Taking into consideration the policy at 15.402, the contracting officer shall specify in the solicitation (see 15.408 (l) and (m))— (1) Whether certified cost or pricing data are required;

statement: Government personnel shall not reveal an offeror's price without that offeror's permission, but the contracting officer may inform an offeror that its price is too high or too low and reveal the results of the analysis supporting that conclusion.
quote: (3) Reveals an offeror's price without that offeror's permission. However, the contracting officer may inform an offeror that its price is considered by the Government to be too high, or too low, and reveal the results of the analysis supporting that conclusion.

statement: One listed limit is that Government personnel shall not reveal the names of individuals providing reference information about an offeror's past performance.
quote: (4) Reveals the names of individuals providing reference information about an offeror's past performance;

statement: The agency may publish a presolicitation notice that invites potential offerors to submit information that allows the Government to advise them about their potential to be viable competitors.
quote: (a) The agency may publish a presolicitation notice (see 5.204) that provides a general description of the scope or purpose of the acquisition and invites potential offerors to submit information that allows the Government to advise the offerors about their potential to be viable competitors.

statement: The agency shall inform all respondents that, notwithstanding the advice the Government gave in response to their submissions, they may participate in the resultant acquisition.
quote: The agency shall inform all respondents that, notwithstanding the advice provided by the Government in response to their submissions, they may participate in the resultant acquisition.

statement: When contracting by negotiation, the contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.215-1 in all competitive solicitations where the Government intends to award a contract without discussions.
quote: When contracting by negotiation— (a) The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.215-1, Instructions to Offerors—Competitive Acquisition, in all competitive solicitations where the Government intends to award a contract without discussions.

statement: One listed rule is that where the Government intends award after discussions with offerors within the competitive range, the contracting officer shall use the basic provision with its Alternate I.
quote: (1) If the Government intends to make award after discussions with offerors within the competitive range, the contracting officer shall use the basic provision with its Alternate I.

statement: Except as provided in a cross-referenced paragraph, the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.215-2, Audit and Records-Negotiation.
quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.215-2, Audit and Records-Negotiation

statement: When issuing a solicitation for information or planning purposes, the contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.215-3 and clearly mark the face of the solicitation as for information or planning purposes.
quote: (c) When issuing a solicitation for information or planning purposes, the contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.215-3, Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes, and clearly mark on the face of the solicitation that it is for information or planning purposes.

statement: The audit clause is inserted in solicitations and contracts except those for listed acquisitions, one of which is an acquisition not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold.
quote: in solicitations and contracts except those for— (i) Acquisitions not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold;

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.215-6, Place of Performance, in solicitations unless the place of performance is specified by the Government.
quote: (f) The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.215-6, Place of Performance, in solicitations unless the place of performance is specified by the Government.

statement: The contracting officer shall promptly notify offerors in writing when their proposals are excluded from the competitive range or otherwise eliminated from the competition, and the notice shall state the basis for the determination and that a proposal revision will not be considered.
quote: The contracting officer shall notify offerors promptly in writing when their proposals are excluded from the competitive range or otherwise eliminated from the competition. The notice shall state the basis for the determination and that a proposal revision will not be considered.

statement: In addition to the exclusion notice, the contracting officer shall notify each offeror in writing before award and upon completion of negotiations and responsibility determinations when using a small business set-aside.
quote: (i) In addition to the notice in paragraph (a)(1) of this section, the contracting officer shall notify each offeror in writing prior to award and upon completion of negotiations and determinations of responsibility— (A) When using a small business set-aside (see subpart 19.5);

statement: Three further listed occasions for the preaward small business program notice are use of the HUBZone procedures, use of the service-disabled veteran-owned small business procedures, and use of the Women-Owned Small Business Program procedures.
quote: (B) When using the HUBZone procedures in 19.1305 or 19.1307; (C) When using the service-disabled veteran-owned small business procedures in 19.1405; or (D) When using the Women-Owned Small Business Program procedures in 19.1505.

statement: The small business program notice shall state, among its listed contents, the name and address of the apparently successful offeror and that the Government will not consider subsequent revisions of the offeror's proposal.
quote: (ii) The notice shall state— (A) The name and address of the apparently successful offeror; (B) That the Government will not consider subsequent revisions of the offeror's proposal; and

statement: One listed content of the small business program notice is that no response is required unless a basis exists to challenge the size status or small business status of the apparently successful offeror.
quote: (C) That no response is required unless a basis exists to challenge the size status or small business status of the apparently successful offeror

statement: The preaward small business program notice is not required when the contracting officer determines in writing that the urgency of the requirement necessitates award without delay or when the contract is entered into under the 8(a) program.
quote: (iii) The notice is not required when the contracting officer determines in writing that the urgency of the requirement necessitates award without delay or when the contract is entered into under the 8(a) program (see 19.805-2).

statement: Within 3 days after the date of contract award, the contracting officer shall provide written notification to each offeror whose proposal was in the competitive range but was not selected for award or had not been previously notified under paragraph (a).
quote: Within 3 days after the date of contract award, the contracting officer shall provide written notification to each offeror whose proposal was in the competitive range but was not selected for award (10 U.S.C. 3304 and 41 U.S.C. 3704) or had not been previously notified under paragraph (a)

statement: The postaward notice shall include, among its listed contents, the number of offerors solicited, the number of proposals received, and the name and address of each offeror receiving an award.
quote: The notice shall include— (i) The number of offerors solicited; (ii) The number of proposals received; (iii) The name and address of each offeror receiving an award;

statement: One listed content of the postaward notice is the items, quantities, and any stated unit prices of each award, but only the total contract price need be furnished in the notice if the number of items or other factors makes listing unit prices impracticable at that time.
quote: (iv) The items, quantities, and any stated unit prices of each award. If the number of items or other factors makes listing any stated unit prices impracticable at that time, only the total contract price need be furnished in the notice.

statement: One listed content of the postaward notice is, in general terms, the reason the offeror's proposal was not accepted, unless the price information in the notice readily reveals the reason.
quote: (v) In general terms, the reason(s) the offeror's proposal was not accepted, unless the price information in paragraph (b)(1)(iv) of this section readily reveals the reason.

statement: Upon request, the contracting officer shall provide the postaward notice information to unsuccessful offerors that received a preaward notice of exclusion from the competitive range.
quote: (3) Upon request, the contracting officer shall provide the information in paragraph (b)(1) of this section to unsuccessful offerors that received a preaward notice of exclusion from the competitive range.

statement: Offerors excluded from the competitive range or otherwise excluded from the competition before award may request a debriefing before award.
quote: Offerors excluded from the competitive range or otherwise excluded from the competition before award may request a debriefing before award (10 U.S.C. 3305 and 41 U.S.C. 3705).

statement: The offeror may request a preaward debriefing by submitting a written request to the contracting officer within 3 days after receipt of the notice of exclusion from the competition.
quote: (1) The offeror may request a preaward debriefing by submitting a written request for debriefing to the contracting officer within 3 days after receipt of the notice of exclusion from the competition.

statement: At the offeror's request a preaward debriefing may be delayed until after award, and a debriefing delayed in that way shall include all information normally provided in a postaward debriefing.
quote: (2) At the offeror's request, this debriefing may be delayed until after award. If the debriefing is delayed until after award, it shall include all information normally provided in a postaward debriefing (see 15.506(d)).

statement: If the offeror does not submit a timely request it need not be given either a preaward or a postaward debriefing, and offerors are entitled to no more than one debriefing for each proposal.
quote: (3) If the offeror does not submit a timely request, the offeror need not be given either a preaward or a postaward debriefing. Offerors are entitled to no more than one debriefing for each proposal.

statement: Preaward debriefings shall include at a minimum, among their listed items, the agency's evaluation of significant elements in the offeror's proposal and a summary of the rationale for eliminating the offeror from the competition.
quote: At a minimum, preaward debriefings shall include— (1) The agency's evaluation of significant elements in the offeror's proposal; (2) A summary of the rationale for eliminating the offeror from the competition; and

statement: Preaward debriefings shall not disclose the number of offerors, the identity of other offerors, the content of other offerors' proposals, the ranking of other offerors, the evaluation of other offerors, or any information prohibited in the postaward debriefing paragraph on disclosure.
quote: (f) Preaward debriefings shall not disclose— (1) The number of offerors; (2) The identity of other offerors; (3) The content of other offerors proposals; (4) The ranking of other offerors; (5) The evaluation of other offerors; or (6) Any of the information prohibited in 15.506(e).

statement: An offeror whose written request is received by the agency within 3 days after the date on which it received notification of contract award shall be debriefed and furnished the basis for the selection decision and contract award.
quote: An offeror, upon its written request received by the agency within 3 days after the date on which that offeror has received notification of contract award in accordance with 15.503(b), shall be debriefed and furnished the basis for the selection decision and contract award.

statement: To the maximum extent practicable, the postaward debriefing should occur within 5 days after receipt of the written request.
quote: To the maximum extent practicable, the debriefing should occur within 5 days after receipt of the written request.

statement: The debriefing information shall include at a minimum, among its listed items, the Government's evaluation of the significant weaknesses or deficiencies in the offeror's proposal, if applicable.
quote: At a minimum, the debriefing information shall include— (1) The Government's evaluation of the significant weaknesses or deficiencies in the offeror's proposal, if applicable;

statement: One listed minimum item of the debriefing information is the overall evaluated cost or price (including unit prices) and technical rating, if applicable, of the successful offeror and the debriefed offeror, and past performance information on the debriefed offeror.
quote: (2) The overall evaluated cost or price (including unit prices), and technical rating, if applicable, of the successful offeror and the debriefed offeror, and past performance information on the debriefed offeror;

statement: Two further listed minimum items are the overall ranking of all offerors, when any ranking was developed by the agency during the source selection, and a summary of the rationale for award.
quote: (3) The overall ranking of all offerors, when any ranking was developed by the agency during the source selection; (4) A summary of the rationale for award;

statement: One listed minimum item is, for acquisitions of commercial products, the make and model of the product to be delivered by the successful offeror.
quote: (5) For acquisitions of commercial products, the make and model of the product to be delivered by the successful offeror; and

statement: The debriefing shall not include point-by-point comparisons of the debriefed offeror's proposal with those of other offerors.
quote: The debriefing shall not include point-by-point comparisons of the debriefed offeror's proposal with those of other offerors.

statement: The debriefing shall not reveal any information prohibited from disclosure by the cited disclosure rule or exempt from release under the Freedom of Information Act, including trade secrets.
quote: Moreover, the debriefing shall not reveal any information prohibited from disclosure by 24.202 or exempt from release under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552) including— (1) Trade secrets;

statement: Two further listed items the debriefing shall not reveal are privileged or confidential commercial and financial information such as cost breakdowns, profit and indirect cost rates, and the names of individuals providing reference information about an offeror's past performance.
quote: (3) Commercial and financial information that is privileged or confidential, including cost breakdowns, profit, indirect cost rates, and similar information; and (4) The names of individuals providing reference information about an offeror's past performance.

statement: A valid unsolicited proposal must, among its listed requirements, be innovative and unique, be independently originated and developed by the offeror, and be prepared without Government supervision, endorsement, direction, or direct Government involvement.
quote: A valid unsolicited proposal must— (1) Be innovative and unique; (2) Be independently originated and developed by the offeror; (3) Be prepared without Government supervision, endorsement, direction, or direct Government involvement;

statement: One listed requirement for a valid unsolicited proposal is sufficient detail to permit a determination that Government support could be worthwhile and the proposed work could benefit the agency's research and development or other mission responsibilities.
quote: (4) Include sufficient detail to permit a determination that Government support could be worthwhile and the proposed work could benefit the agency's research and development or other mission responsibilities;

statement: Two further listed requirements are that a valid unsolicited proposal not be an advance proposal for a known agency requirement that can be acquired by competitive methods and not address a previously published agency requirement.
quote: (5) Not be an advance proposal for a known agency requirement that can be acquired by competitive methods; and (6) Not address a previously published agency requirement.

statement: Advertising material, commercial product or commercial service offers, contributions as defined in the same subpart, and routine correspondence on technical issues are not unsolicited proposals.
quote: Advertising material, commercial product or commercial service offers, or contributions, as defined in 15.601, or routine correspondence on technical issues, are not unsolicited proposals.

statement: Agencies must make available to potential offerors of unsolicited proposals at least a listed set of information, one item being the definition and content of an unsolicited proposal acceptable for formal evaluation.
quote: Agencies must make available to potential offerors of unsolicited proposals at least the following information: (1) Definition (see 2.101) and content (see 15.605) of an unsolicited proposal acceptable for formal evaluation.

statement: Only the cognizant contracting officer has the authority to bind the Government regarding unsolicited proposals.
quote: Only the cognizant contracting officer has the authority to bind the Government regarding unsolicited proposals.

statement: Unsolicited proposals should contain listed information to permit consideration in an objective and timely manner, beginning with basic information that includes the offeror's name, address and type of organization.
quote: Unsolicited proposals should contain the following information to permit consideration in an objective and timely manner: (a) Basic information including— (1) Offeror's name and address and type of organization; e.g., profit, nonprofit, educational, small business;

statement: Two further listed items of basic information are the names and telephone numbers of technical and business personnel to be contacted for evaluation or negotiation purposes, and identification of proprietary data to be used only for evaluation purposes.
quote: (2) Names and telephone numbers of technical and business personnel to be contacted for evaluation or negotiation purposes; (3) Identification of proprietary data to be used only for evaluation purposes;

statement: Three further listed items of basic information are the names of other agencies or parties receiving the proposal or funding the proposed effort, the date of submission, and the signature of a person authorized to represent and contractually obligate the offeror.
quote: (4) Names of other Federal, State, or local agencies or parties receiving the proposal or funding the proposed effort; (5) Date of submission; and (6) Signature of a person authorized to represent and contractually obligate the offeror.

statement: One listed element of the technical information is a concise title and abstract of approximately 200 words of the proposed effort.
quote: (b) Technical information including— (1) Concise title and abstract (approximately 200 words) of the proposed effort;

statement: One listed element of the technical information is a reasonably complete discussion of the objectives, method of approach and extent of effort, nature and extent of anticipated results, and the manner in which the work will help support accomplishment of the agency's mission.
quote: (2) A reasonably complete discussion stating the objectives of the effort or activity, the method of approach and extent of effort to be employed, the nature and extent of the anticipated results, and the manner in which the work will help to support accomplishment of the agency's mission;

statement: Two further listed elements of the technical information are names and biographical information on the offeror's key personnel, including alternates, and the type of support needed from the agency.
quote: (3) Names and biographical information on the offeror's key personnel who would be involved, including alternates; and (4) Type of support needed from the agency; e.g., Government property or personnel resources.

statement: One listed element of the supporting information is the proposed price or total estimated cost for the effort in sufficient detail for meaningful evaluation.
quote: (c) Supporting information including— (1) Proposed price or total estimated cost for the effort in sufficient detail for meaningful evaluation;

statement: Three further listed elements of the supporting information are the period for which the proposal is valid, for which a 6-month minimum is suggested, the type of contract preferred, and the proposed duration of effort.
quote: (2) Period of time for which the proposal is valid (a 6-month minimum is suggested); (3) Type of contract preferred; (4) Proposed duration of effort;

statement: If the offeror wishes to restrict data in an unsolicited proposal that it does not want disclosed to the public or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes, the title page must be marked with a prescribed legend.
quote: An unsolicited proposal may include data that the offeror does not want disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes. If the offeror wishes to restrict the data, the title page must be marked with the following legend:

statement: The prescribed title page legend says the marked data shall not be disclosed outside the Government and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed, in whole or in part, for any purpose other than to evaluate the proposal.
quote: Use and Disclosure of Data This proposal includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed—in whole or in part—for any purpose other than to evaluate this proposal.

statement: The prescribed legend also says that if a contract is awarded to the offeror as a result of or in connection with the submission of the data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent provided in the resulting contract.
quote: However, if a contract is awarded to this offeror as a result of—or in connection with—the submission of these data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent provided in the resulting contract.

statement: The prescribed legend also says that the restriction does not limit the Government's right to use information contained in the data if it is obtained from another source without restriction.
quote: This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use information contained in these data if they are obtained from another source without restriction.

statement: The offeror shall also mark each sheet of data it wishes to restrict with a prescribed sheet legend that refers to the restriction on the title page.
quote: (b) The offeror shall also mark each sheet of data it wishes to restrict with the following legend: Use or disclosure of data contained on this sheet is subject to the restriction on the title page of this proposal.

statement: The agency point of contact shall return to the offeror any unsolicited proposal marked with a legend different from the prescribed title page legend.
quote: The agency point of contact shall return to the offeror any unsolicited proposal marked with a legend different from that provided in paragraph (a) of this section.

statement: The auditor is responsible for, among other listed duties, submitting information and advice to the requesting activity, based on analysis of the contractor's financial and accounting records or other related data, on the acceptability of the contractor's incurred and estimated costs.
quote: The auditor is responsible for— (1) Submitting information and advice to the requesting activity, based on the auditor's analysis of the contractor's financial and accounting records or other related data as to the acceptability of the contractor's incurred and estimated costs;

statement: Normally, for contractors other than educational institutions and nonprofit organizations, the Defense Contract Audit Agency is the responsible Government audit agency, although another agency may desire cognizance of a particular contractor.
quote: Normally, for contractors other than educational institutions and nonprofit organizations, the Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) is the responsible Government audit agency. However, there may be instances where an agency other than DCAA desires cognizance of a particular contractor.

statement: As provided in agency procedures or interagency agreements, contracting officers may request audit services directly from the responsible audit agency cited in the Directory of Federal Contract Audit Offices.
quote: As provided in agency procedures or interagency agreements, contracting officers may request audit services directly from the responsible audit agency cited in the Directory of Federal Contract Audit Offices.

statement: The audit request should include a suspense date and should identify any information needed by the contracting officer.
quote: The audit request should include a suspense date and should identify any information needed by the contracting officer.

statement: An offeror that was notified of exclusion from the competition before award but failed to submit a timely request is not entitled to a debriefing, although untimely debriefing requests may be accommodated.
quote: (3) An offeror that was notified of exclusion from the competition (see 15.505(a)), but failed to submit a timely request, is not entitled to a debriefing. (4) (i) Untimely debriefing requests may be accommodated.

statement: One listed minimum item of the debriefing information is reasonable responses to relevant questions about whether the source selection procedures in the solicitation, applicable regulations, and other applicable authorities were followed.
quote: (6) Reasonable responses to relevant questions about whether source selection procedures contained in the solicitation, applicable regulations, and other applicable authorities were followed.

statement: One listed item the debriefing shall not reveal is privileged or confidential manufacturing processes and techniques.
quote: (2) Privileged or confidential manufacturing processes and techniques;

statement: The contracting officer shall make every effort to debrief the unsuccessful offeror as soon as practicable, but may refuse the request for a debriefing if, for compelling reasons, it is not in the best interests of the Government to conduct a debriefing at that time.
quote: The contracting officer shall make every effort to debrief the unsuccessful offeror as soon as practicable, but may refuse the request for a debriefing if, for compelling reasons, it is not in the best interests of the Government to conduct a debriefing at that time.

statement: If the contracting officer delays the debriefing, it shall be provided no later than the time postaward debriefings are provided, and it shall include the information that a postaward debriefing includes at a minimum.
quote: If the contracting officer delays the debriefing, it shall be provided no later than the time postaward debriefings are provided under 15.506. In that event, the contracting officer shall include the information at 15.506(d) in the debriefing.

statement: Two further listed elements of the supporting information are a brief description of the organization, previous experience, relevant past performance and facilities to be used, and other statements, if applicable, about organizational conflicts of interest, security clearances, and environmental impacts.
quote: (5) Brief description of the organization, previous experience, relevant past performance, and facilities to be used; (6) Other statements, if applicable, about organizational conflicts of interest, security clearances, and environmental impacts; and

statement: One further listed element of the supporting information is the names and telephone numbers of agency technical or other agency points of contact already contacted regarding the proposal.
quote: (7) The names and telephone numbers of agency technical or other agency points of contact already contacted regarding the proposal.

statement: One further listed minimum item of a preaward debriefing is reasonable responses to relevant questions about whether the source selection procedures in the solicitation, applicable regulations, and other applicable authorities were followed in the process of eliminating the offeror from the competition.
quote: (3) Reasonable responses to relevant questions about whether source selection procedures contained in the solicitation, applicable regulations, and other applicable authorities were followed in the process of eliminating the offeror from the competition.

statement: In no event shall an offeror's cost breakdown, profit, overhead rates, trade secrets, manufacturing processes and techniques, or other confidential business information be disclosed to any other offeror.
quote: In no event shall an offeror's cost breakdown, profit, overhead rates, trade secrets, manufacturing processes and techniques, or other confidential business information be disclosed to any other offeror.

statement: Even where only the total contract price is furnished in the postaward notice, the items, quantities, and any stated unit prices of each award shall be made publicly available upon request.
quote: If the number of items or other factors makes listing any stated unit prices impracticable at that time, only the total contract price need be furnished in the notice. However, the items, quantities, and any stated unit prices of each award shall be made publicly available, upon request

statement: Upon request, the contracting officer shall furnish the postaward notice information to unsuccessful offerors in solicitations using simplified acquisition procedures.
quote: (2) Upon request, the contracting officer shall furnish the information described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section to unsuccessful offerors in solicitations using simplified acquisition procedures in part 13.

statement: The agency point of contact shall place a prescribed cover sheet on the proposal or clearly mark it with the prescribed notice, unless the offeror clearly states in writing that no restrictions are imposed on the disclosure or use of the data contained in the proposal.
quote: The agency point of contact shall place a cover sheet on the proposal or clearly mark it as follows, unless the offeror clearly states in writing that no restrictions are imposed on the disclosure or use of the data contained in the proposal:

statement: The prescribed cover sheet notice tells all Government personnel to exercise extreme care to ensure that the information in the proposal is not disclosed to an individual who has not been authorized access to such data.
quote: Unsolicited Proposal—Use of Data Limited All Government personnel must exercise extreme care to ensure that the information in this proposal is not disclosed to an individual who has not been authorized access to such data in accordance with FAR 3.104,

statement: The prescribed cover sheet notice also says the information in the proposal is not to be duplicated, used, or disclosed in whole or in part for any purpose other than evaluation of the proposal without the written permission of the offeror.
quote: and is not duplicated, used, or disclosed in whole or in part for any purpose other than evaluation of the proposal, without the written permission of the offeror.

statement: Agencies are told not to use the cover sheet notice to justify withholding of a record, or to improperly deny the public access to a record, where the Freedom of Information Act imposes an obligation.
quote: However, do not use this notice to justify withholding of a record, or to improperly deny the public access to a record, where an obligation is imposed by the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552).

statement: The agency point of contact has listed duties when an agency receives an unsolicited proposal without any restrictive legend from an educational or nonprofit organization or institution and an evaluation outside the Government is necessary.
quote: When an agency receives an unsolicited proposal without any restrictive legend from an educational or nonprofit organization or institution, and an evaluation outside the Government is necessary, the agency point of contact shall—

statement: One listed duty in that case is to attach a cover sheet clearly marked with the cover sheet notice.
quote: (1) Attach a cover sheet clearly marked with the legend in paragraph (d) of this section;

statement: Another listed duty in that case is to require any non-Government evaluator to agree in writing that data in the proposal will not be disclosed to others outside the Government.
quote: (3) Require any non-Government evaluator to agree in writing that data in the proposal will not be disclosed to others outside the Government.

statement: If an unsolicited proposal is received with the restrictive legend, the modified cover sheet shall also be used and permission shall be obtained from the offeror before release of the proposal for evaluation by non-Government personnel.
quote: (g) If the proposal is received with the restrictive legend (see paragraph (a) of this section), the modified cover sheet shall also be used and permission shall be obtained from the offeror before release of the proposal for evaluation by non-Government personnel.

statement: Further requirements apply when an agency receives an unsolicited proposal, with or without a restrictive legend, from other than an educational or nonprofit organization or institution and evaluation by Government personnel outside the agency or by experts outside of the Government is necessary.
quote: (h) When an agency receives an unsolicited proposal with or without a restrictive legend from other than an educational or nonprofit organization or institution, and evaluation by Government personnel outside the agency or by experts outside of the Government is necessary,

statement: In that case written permission must be obtained from the offeror before release of the proposal for evaluation.
quote: written permission must be obtained from the offeror before release of the proposal for evaluation.

statement: One listed duty of the agency point of contact in that case is to obtain a written agreement from any non-Government evaluator stating that data in the proposal will not be disclosed to persons outside the Government.
quote: (2) Obtain a written agreement from any non-Government evaluator stating that data in the proposal will not be disclosed to persons outside the Government.

statement: The responsible audit agency may decline requests for services on a case-by-case basis if its resources are inadequate to accomplish the tasks, and declinations shall be in writing.
quote: (b) The responsible audit agency may decline requests for services on a case-by-case basis, if resources of the audit agency are inadequate to accomplish the tasks. Declinations shall be in writing.

statement: One listed item of information that agencies must make available is instructions for identifying and marking proprietary information so that it is protected and restrictive legends conform to the section on limited use of data.
quote: (7) Instructions for identifying and marking proprietary information so that it is protected and restrictive legends conform to 15.609.

statement: Where an agency other than the Defense Contract Audit Agency desires cognizance of a particular contractor, the two agencies shall agree on the most efficient and economical approach to meet contract audit requirements.
quote: However, there may be instances where an agency other than DCAA desires cognizance of a particular contractor. In those instances, the two agencies shall agree on the most efficient and economical approach to meet contract audit requirements.

statement: One listed condition is that the agency would realize no, or minimal, value from a proposal that exceeds the minimum technical or performance requirements.
quote: (2) The agency would realize no, or minimal, value from a proposal that exceeds the minimum technical or performance requirements;

statement: One listed condition is that the agency believes the technical proposals will require no, or minimal, subjective judgment by the source selection authority as to the desirability of one offeror's proposal versus a competing proposal.
quote: (3) The agency believes the technical proposals will require no, or minimal, subjective judgment by the source selection authority as to the desirability of one offeror's proposal versus a competing proposal;

statement: One listed condition is that the agency determined that the lowest price reflects the total cost, including operation and support, of the products or services being acquired.
quote: (5) The agency determined that the lowest price reflects the total cost, including operation and support, of the product(s) or service(s) being acquired;

statement: If the contracting officer documents the file as the cross-referenced paragraph provides, past performance need not be an evaluation factor in lowest price technically acceptable source selections.
quote: If the contracting officer documents the file pursuant to 15.304(c)(3)(iii), past performance need not be an evaluation factor in lowest price technically acceptable source selections.

statement: If the contracting officer elects to consider past performance as an evaluation factor in a lowest price technically acceptable source selection, it is evaluated under the proposal evaluation section, but the comparative assessment in a cross-referenced paragraph does not apply.
quote: If the contracting officer elects to consider past performance as an evaluation factor, it shall be evaluated in accordance with 15.305. However, the comparative assessment in 15.305(a)(2)(i) does not apply.

statement: Information provided to a potential offeror in response to its request must not be disclosed if doing so would reveal the potential offeror's confidential business strategy and the information is protected under the cross-referenced provisions.
quote: Information provided to a potential offeror in response to its request must not be disclosed if doing so would reveal the potential offeror's confidential business strategy, and is protected under 3.104 or subpart 24.2.

statement: The duty to amend the solicitation for a proposal that departs from the stated requirements applies provided it can be done without revealing to the other offerors the alternate solution proposed or any other information entitled to protection.
quote: provided this can be done without revealing to the other offerors the alternate solution proposed or any other information that is entitled to protection

statement: A proposal, modification or revision received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is late.

statement: Restructuring costs associated with external restructuring activities that are allocated to DoD contracts and are less than $2.5 million are not subject to the audit, review, and determination requirements of paragraph (c)(4) of the cost principle.
quote: if restructuring costs associated with external restructuring activities allocated to DoD contracts are less than $2.5 million, the costs shall not be subject to the audit, review, and determination requirements of paragraph (c)(4) of this subsection;

quote: (20) Segment closing means that a segment has (i) been sold or ownership has been otherwise transferred, (ii) discontinued operations, or (iii) discontinued doing or actively seeking Government business under contracts subject to this Standard.

quote: If a segment is closed, if there is a pension plan termination, or if there is a curtailment of benefits, the contractor shall determine the difference between the actuarial accrued liability for the segment and the market value of the assets allocated to the segment
note: The same sentence adds that this applies irrespective of whether or not the pension plan is terminated.

statement: The difference between the market value of the assets and the actuarial accrued liability for the segment represents an adjustment of previously-determined pension costs.
quote: The difference between the market value of the assets and the actuarial accrued liability for the segment represents an adjustment of previously-determined pension costs.

quote: Predecessor CAGE code: ________ (or mark “Unknown”).

quote: If there is a pension plan termination, the actuarial accrued liability shall be measured as the amount paid to irrevocably settle all benefit obligations or paid to the Pension Benefit Guarantee Corporation.

quote: Plan improvements mandated by law or collective bargaining agreement are not subject to this phase-in.

quote: The numerator of such fraction shall be the sum of the pension plan costs allocated to all contracts and subcontracts (including Foreign Military Sales) subject to this Standard during a period of years representative of the Government's participation in the pension plan.
