quote: The denominator of such fraction shall be the total pension costs assigned to cost accounting periods during those same years.

statement: Concerns and entities are affiliates of each other when one controls or has the power to control the other, or a third party or parties controls or has the power to control both, whether or not control is exercised.
quote: Concerns and entities are affiliates of each other when one controls or has the power to control the other, or a third party or parties controls or has the power to control both. It does not matter whether control is exercised, so long as the power to control exists.

statement: Negative control includes, but is not limited to, instances where a minority shareholder can, under the concern's charter, by-laws or shareholder's agreement, prevent a quorum or otherwise block action by the board of directors or shareholders.
quote: Negative control includes, but is not limited to, instances where a minority shareholder has the ability, under the concern's charter, by-laws, or shareholder's agreement, to prevent a quorum or otherwise block action by the board of directors or shareholders.

statement: SBA will not find that a minority shareholder has negative control where the shareholder has the authority to block action by the board of directors or shareholders regarding the extraordinary circumstances that the rule then lists.
quote: However, SBA will not find that a minority shareholder has negative control where such minority shareholder has the authority to block action by the board of directors or shareholders regarding the following extraordinary circumstances:

statement: The listed extraordinary circumstances include adding a new equity stakeholder or increasing an equity stakeholder's investment, dissolution of the company, sale of the company or all of its assets, and the merger of the company.
quote: (i) Adding a new equity stakeholder or increasing the investment amount of an equity stakeholder; (ii) Dissolution of the company; (iii) Sale of the company or all assets of the company; (iv) The merger of the company;
note: The list continues with bankruptcy, amendment of governance documents to remove the blocking authority, and other extraordinary actions crafted solely to protect minority investment.

statement: In determining whether affiliation exists, SBA considers the totality of the circumstances and may find affiliation even though no single factor is sufficient to constitute affiliation.
quote: In determining whether affiliation exists, SBA will consider the totality of the circumstances, and may find affiliation even though no single factor is sufficient to constitute affiliation.

statement: In determining the size of the concern at issue, SBA counts the receipts, employees or other measure of size of that concern and of all its domestic and foreign affiliates, whether or not the affiliates are organized for profit.
quote: In determining the concern's size, SBA counts the receipts, employees, or other measure of size of the concern whose size is at issue and all of its domestic and foreign affiliates, regardless of whether the affiliates are organized for profit.

statement: A person that owns, or has the power to control, 50 percent or more of a concern's voting stock, or a block of voting stock that is large compared to other outstanding blocks, controls or has the power to control the concern.
quote: A person (including any individual, concern or other entity) that owns, or has the power to control, 50 percent or more of a concern's voting stock, or a block of voting stock which is large compared to other outstanding blocks of voting stock, controls or has the power to control the concern.

statement: SBA presumes that each such person controls or has the power to control the concern whose size is at issue where the minority holdings are equal or approximately equal in size and their aggregate is large as compared with any other stock holding.
quote: such minority holdings are equal or approximately equal in size, and the aggregate of these minority holdings is large as compared with any other stock holding, SBA presumes that each such person controls or has the power to control the concern whose size is at issue.

statement: The presumption that each such person controls the concern whose size is at issue may be rebutted by a showing that such control or power to control does not in fact exist.
quote: SBA presumes that each such person controls or has the power to control the concern whose size is at issue. This presumption may be rebutted by a showing that such control or power to control does not in fact exist.

statement: If a concern's voting stock is widely held and no single block is large compared with all other stock holdings, the concern's Board of Directors and CEO or President are deemed to have the power to control the concern in the absence of evidence to the contrary.
quote: If a concern's voting stock is widely held and no single block of stock is large as compared with all other stock holdings, the concern's Board of Directors and CEO or President will be deemed to have the power to control the concern in the absence of evidence to the contrary.

statement: SBA considers stock options, convertible securities and agreements to merge, including agreements in principle, to have a present effect on the power to control a concern, and it treats the rights granted as though they have been exercised.
quote: SBA considers stock options, convertible securities, and agreements to merge (including agreements in principle) to have a present effect on the power to control a concern. SBA treats such options, convertible securities, and agreements as though the rights granted have been exercised.
note: The quote begins after the opening words In determining size.

statement: Agreements to open or continue negotiations towards the possibility of a merger or a sale of stock at some later date are not agreements in principle and are not given present effect.
quote: Agreements to open or continue negotiations towards the possibility of a merger or a sale of stock at some later date are not considered “agreements in principle” and are thus not given present effect.

statement: Items that are subject to conditions precedent which are incapable of fulfillment, speculative, conjectural or unenforceable under state or Federal law, or where the probability of the transaction or of the exercise of the rights occurring is shown to be extremely remote, are not given present effect.
quote: that are subject to conditions precedent which are incapable of fulfillment, speculative, conjectural, or unenforceable under state or Federal law, or where the probability of the transaction (or exercise of the rights) occurring is shown to be extremely remote, are not given present effect.
note: The quote begins mid-sentence; the subject of the sentence is options, convertible securities, and agreements.

statement: SBA will not give present effect to an individual's, concern's or other entity's ability to divest all or part of its ownership interest in order to avoid a finding of affiliation.
quote: SBA will not give present effect to individuals', concerns' or other entities' ability to divest all or part of their ownership interest in order to avoid a finding of affiliation.

statement: Affiliation arises where one or more officers, directors, managing members or partners who control the board of directors or management of one concern also control the board of directors or management of one or more other concerns.
quote: Affiliation arises where one or more officers, directors, managing members, or partners who control the board of directors and/or management of one concern also control the board of directors or management of one or more other concerns.
note: The quote reads and/or; the statement uses or.

statement: Affiliation may arise among two or more persons with an identity of interest.
quote: Affiliation may arise among two or more persons with an identity of interest.

quote: If a concern has acquired an affiliate or been acquired as an affiliate during the applicable period of measurement or before the date on which it self-certified as small, the annual receipts used in determining size status includes the receipts of the acquired or acquiring concern.

quote: the annual receipts used in determining size status includes the receipts of the acquired or acquiring concern. This aggregation applies for the entire period of measurement, not just the period after the affiliation arose.

statement: If a concern has sold a segregable division to another business concern during the applicable period of measurement or before the date on which it self-certified as small, the annual receipts used in determining size status continue to include the receipts of the division that was sold.
quote: if a concern has sold a segregable division to another business concern during the applicable period of measurement or before the date on which it self-certified as small, the annual receipts used in determining size status will continue to include the receipts of the division that was sold.

quote: If a concern has acquired an affiliate or been acquired as an affiliate during the applicable period of measurement or before the date on which it self-certified as small, the employees counted in determining size status include the employees of the acquired or acquiring concern.

quote: The employees of a former affiliate are not counted if affiliation ceased before the date used for determining size. This exclusion of employees of a former affiliate applies during the entire period of measurement, rather than only for the period after which affiliation ceased.

statement: If a concern has sold a segregable division to another business concern during the applicable period of measurement or before the date on which it self-certified as small, the employees used in determining size status continue to include the employees of the division that was sold.

quote: Contracting officers shall— (a) Ensure that the requirements of 1.602-1(b) have been met, and that sufficient funds are available for obligation;

statement: The duty to designate a COR is to be carried out in writing and in accordance with agency procedures on all contracts and orders other than firm-fixed-price ones, and on firm-fixed-price ones as appropriate, unless the contracting officer retains and executes the COR duties.
quote: in writing and in accordance with agency procedures, a contracting officer's representative (COR) on all contracts and orders other than those that are firm-fixed price, and for firm-fixed-price contracts and orders as appropriate, unless the contracting officer retains and executes the COR duties.
note: The list item opens with the words Designate and authorize, which CL-OPM-0100 carries; this quote starts after them to stay within 300 characters.

statement: A COR shall be a Government employee, unless otherwise authorized in agency regulations.
quote: A COR— (1) Shall be a Government employee, unless otherwise authorized in agency regulations;

statement: One listed attribute of a COR is that the COR has no authority to make any commitments or changes that affect price, quality, quantity, delivery, or other terms and conditions of the contract, nor to direct the contractor or its subcontractors to operate in conflict with the contract terms and conditions.
quote: (5) Has no authority to make any commitments or changes that affect price, quality, quantity, delivery, or other terms and conditions of the contract nor in any way direct the contractor or its subcontractors to operate in conflict with the contract terms and conditions;

statement: One listed attribute of a COR is that the COR shall be designated in writing, with copies furnished to the contractor and the contract administration office, specifying the extent of the COR's authority and identifying the limitations on it.
quote: (7) Shall be designated in writing, with copies furnished to the contractor and the contract administration office— (i) Specifying the extent of the COR's authority to act on behalf of the contracting officer; (ii) Identifying the limitations on the COR's authority;

statement: Two listed statements in the written designation of a COR are that the authority is not redelegable and that the COR may be personally liable for unauthorized acts.
quote: (iv) Stating the authority is not redelegable; and (v) Stating that the COR may be personally liable for unauthorized acts.

statement: An unauthorized commitment is an agreement that is not binding solely because the Government representative who made it lacked the authority to enter into that agreement on behalf of the Government.
quote: Unauthorized commitment, as used in this subsection, means an agreement that is not binding solely because the Government representative who made it lacked the authority to enter into that agreement on behalf of the Government.

statement: Subject to the limitations in paragraph (c) of the subsection, the head of the contracting activity, unless the agency designates a higher level official, may ratify an unauthorized commitment.
quote: Subject to the limitations in paragraph (c) of this subsection, the head of the contracting activity, unless a higher level official is designated by the agency, may ratify an unauthorized commitment.

statement: The authority to ratify may be delegated in accordance with agency procedures, but in no case below the level of chief of the contracting office.
quote: The ratification authority in subparagraph (b)(2) of this subsection may be delegated in accordance with agency procedures, but in no case shall the authority be delegated below the level of chief of the contracting office.

statement: The authority to ratify may be exercised only when listed conditions are met, the first being that supplies or services have been provided to and accepted by the Government, or the Government otherwise has obtained or will obtain a benefit resulting from performance of the unauthorized commitment.
quote: The authority in subparagraph (b)(2) of this subsection may be exercised only when— (1) Supplies or services have been provided to and accepted by the Government, or the Government otherwise has obtained or will obtain a benefit resulting from performance of the unauthorized commitment;

statement: Two listed conditions for ratification are that the ratifying official has the authority to enter into a contractual commitment and that the resulting contract would otherwise have been proper if made by an appropriate contracting officer.
quote: (2) The ratifying official has the authority to enter into a contractual commitment; (3) The resulting contract would otherwise have been proper if made by an appropriate contracting officer;

statement: Two listed conditions for ratification are that the contracting officer reviewing the unauthorized commitment determines the price to be fair and reasonable, and that the contracting officer recommends payment and legal counsel concurs in the recommendation, unless agency procedures expressly do not require such concurrence.
quote: (4) The contracting officer reviewing the unauthorized commitment determines the price to be fair and reasonable; (5) The contracting officer recommends payment and legal counsel concurs in the recommendation, unless agency procedures expressly do not require such concurrence;

statement: Two listed conditions for ratification are that funds are available and were available at the time the unauthorized commitment was made, and that the ratification is in accordance with any other limitations prescribed under agency procedures.
quote: (6) Funds are available and were available at the time the unauthorized commitment was made; and (7) The ratification is in accordance with any other limitations prescribed under agency procedures.

statement: Cases that are not ratifiable under this subsection may be subject to resolution as recommended by the Government Accountability Office under its claim procedure, or as authorized by FAR Subpart 50.1.
quote: Cases that are not ratifiable under this subsection may be subject to resolution as recommended by the Government Accountability Office under its claim procedure (GAO Policy and Procedures Manual for Guidance of Federal Agencies, Title 4, Chapter 2), or as authorized by FAR Subpart 50.1.

statement: Contracting officers shall be appointed in writing on an SF 1402, Certificate of Appointment, which shall state any limitations on the scope of authority to be exercised, other than limitations contained in applicable law or regulation.
quote: Contracting officers shall be appointed in writing on an SF 1402, Certificate of Appointment, which shall state any limitations on the scope of authority to be exercised, other than limitations contained in applicable law or regulation.

statement: Appointing officials shall maintain files containing copies of all appointments that have not been terminated.
quote: Appointing officials shall maintain files containing copies of all appointments that have not been terminated.

statement: The COR shall maintain a file for each assigned contract, which must include, at a minimum, a copy of the contracting officer's letter of designation and other documents describing the COR's duties and responsibilities.
quote: The COR shall maintain a file for each assigned contract. The file must include, at a minimum— (a) A copy of the contracting officer's letter of designation and other documents describing the COR's duties and responsibilities;

statement: Two further listed items in the COR file are a copy of the contract administration functions delegated to a contract administration office which may not be delegated to the COR, and documentation of COR actions taken in accordance with the delegation of authority.
quote: (b) A copy of the contract administration functions delegated to a contract administration office which may not be delegated to the COR (see 1.602-2(d)(4)); and (c) Documentation of COR actions taken in accordance with the delegation of authority.

statement: Unless precluded by law, executive order, or regulation, deviations from the FAR may be granted as specified in the subpart when necessary to meet the specific needs and requirements of each agency.
quote: Unless precluded by law, executive order, or regulation, deviations from the FAR may be granted as specified in this subpart when necessary to meet the specific needs and requirements of each agency.

statement: Deviations are not authorized with respect to 30.201-3 and 30.201-4 or the requirements of the Cost Accounting Standards Board rules and regulations in 48 CFR chapter 99, and the FAR refers readers to 30.201-5 for waivers pertaining to Cost Accounting Standards.
quote: Deviations are not authorized with respect to 30.201-3 and 30.201-4, or the requirements of the Cost Accounting Standards Board (CASB) rules and regulations (48 CFR chapter 99). Refer to 30.201-5 for instructions concerning waivers pertaining to Cost Accounting Standards.

statement: Individual deviations affect only one contract action and, unless 1.405(e) is applicable, may be authorized by the agency head, and the contracting officer must document the justification and agency approval in the contract file.
quote: Individual deviations affect only one contract action, and, unless 1.405(e) is applicable, may be authorized by the agency head. The contracting officer must document the justification and agency approval in the contract file.

statement: Class deviations affect more than one contract action.
quote: Class deviations affect more than one contract action.

statement: For civilian agencies except NASA, class deviations may be authorized by agency heads or their designees, unless 1.405(e) is applicable, and that authority shall not be delegated below the head of a contracting activity.
quote: (a) For civilian agencies except NASA, class deviations may be authorized by agency heads or their designees, unless 1.405(e) is applicable. Delegation of this authority shall not be made below the head of a contracting activity.

statement: For DoD, class deviations shall be controlled, processed, and approved in accordance with the Defense FAR Supplement.
quote: (b) For DOD, class deviations shall be controlled, processed, and approved in accordance with the Defense FAR Supplement.

statement: Each D&F shall set forth enough facts and circumstances to clearly and convincingly justify the specific determination made and, as a minimum, shall include the listed information in the prescribed agency format.
quote: Each D&F shall set forth enough facts and circumstances to clearly and convincingly justify the specific determination made. As a minimum, each D&F shall include, in the prescribed agency format, the following information:

statement: Three listed items in a D&F are the identification of the agency and contracting activity and of the document as a Determination and Findings, the nature or description of the action being approved, and the citation of the statute or regulation on which the D&F is based.
quote: (a) Identification of the agency and of the contracting activity and specific identifications of the document as a Determination and Findings. (b) Nature and/or description of the action being approved. (c) Citation of the appropriate statute and/or regulation upon which the D&F is based.

statement: One listed item in a D&F is findings that detail the particular circumstances, facts, or reasoning essential to support the determination, with necessary supporting documentation obtained from appropriate requirements and technical personnel.
quote: (d) Findings that detail the particular circumstances, facts, or reasoning essential to support the determination. Necessary supporting documentation shall be obtained from appropriate requirements and technical personnel.

statement: Three further listed items in a D&F are a determination based on the findings that the proposed action is justified under the applicable statute or regulation, an expiration date if required, and the signature of the official authorized to sign and the date signed.
quote: (e) A determination, based on the findings, that the proposed action is justified under the applicable statute or regulation. (f) Expiration date of the D&F, if required (see 1.706(b)). (g) The signature of the official authorized to sign the D&F (see 1.706) and the date signed.

statement: When a D&F is required, it shall be signed by the appropriate official in accordance with agency regulations, and authority to sign or delegate signature authority for the various D&Fs is as shown in the applicable FAR part.
quote: When a D&F is required, it shall be signed by the appropriate official in accordance with agency regulations. Authority to sign or delegate signature authority for the various D&F's is as shown in the applicable FAR part.

statement: Cognizant Government or contractor personnel may request the contracting officer to arrange for orientation, but it is up to the contracting officer to decide whether a postaward orientation in any form is necessary.
quote: While cognizant Government or contractor personnel may request the contracting officer to arrange for orientation, it is up to the contracting officer to decide whether a postaward orientation in any form is necessary.

statement: When deciding whether postaward orientation is necessary and what form it shall take, the contracting officer shall consider, as a minimum, listed factors, the first being the nature and extent of the preaward survey and any other prior discussions with the contractor.
quote: When deciding whether postaward orientation is necessary and, if so, what form it shall take, the contracting officer shall consider, as a minimum, the— (a) Nature and extent of the preaward survey and any other prior discussions with the contractor;

statement: One listed factor for the contracting officer to consider is complex financing arrangements, such as progress payments, advance payments, or guaranteed loans.
quote: (k) Safety precautions required for hazardous materials or operations; and (l) Complex financing arrangements, such as progress payments, advance payments, or guaranteed loans.

statement: The chairperson of a postaward conference shall conduct the meeting and, unless a contract change is contemplated, shall emphasize that it is not the purpose of the meeting to change the contract.
quote: The chairperson of the conference shall conduct the meeting. Unless a contract change is contemplated, the chairperson shall emphasize that it is not the purpose of the meeting to change the contract.

statement: At a postaward conference the contracting officer may make commitments or give directions within the scope of the contracting officer's authority and shall put in writing and sign any commitment or direction, whether or not it changes the contract.
quote: The contracting officer may make commitments or give directions within the scope of the contracting officer's authority and shall put in writing and sign any commitment or direction, whether or not it changes the contract.

statement: Any change to the contract that results from a postaward conference shall be made only by a contract modification referencing the applicable terms of the contract, and participants without authority to bind the Government shall not take action that in any way alters the contract.
quote: Any change to the contract that results from the postaward conference shall be made only by a contract modification referencing the applicable terms of the contract. Participants without authority to bind the Government shall not take action that in any way alters the contract.

statement: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared at least annually and at the time the work under a contract or order is completed.
quote: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared at least annually and at the time the work under a contract or order is completed.

statement: Except as provided in paragraphs (e), (f), and (h) of the section, agencies shall prepare evaluations of contractor performance for each contract that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and for each order that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold.
quote: Except as provided in paragraphs (e), (f), and (h) of this section, agencies shall prepare evaluations of contractor performance for each contract (as defined in FAR part 2) that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and for each order that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold.

statement: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared for each construction contract of $900,000 or more, and for each construction contract terminated for default regardless of contract value.
quote: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared for each construction contract of $900,000 or more, and for each construction contract terminated for default regardless of contract value.

statement: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared for each architect-engineer services contract of $45,000 or more, and for each architect-engineer services contract that is terminated for default regardless of contract value.
quote: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared for each architect-engineer services contract of $45,000 or more, and for each architect-engineer services contract that is terminated for default regardless of contract value.

statement: Past performance evaluations shall include an assessment of the contractor's performance against, and efforts to achieve, the goals identified in the small business subcontracting plan when the contract includes the clause at 52.219-9.
quote: (g) Past performance evaluations shall include an assessment of the contractor's— (1) Performance against, and efforts to achieve, the goals identified in the small business subcontracting plan when the contract includes the clause at 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan; and

statement: One listed item that a past performance evaluation shall assess is reduced or untimely payments made to small business subcontractors that the contracting officer determines to be unjustified.
quote: (2) Reduced or untimely payments (as defined in 19.701), made to small business subcontractors, determined by the contracting officer to be unjustified.

statement: The contracting officer shall consider and evaluate a contractor's written explanation for a reduced or an untimely payment when determining whether the reduced or untimely payment is justified.
quote: The contracting officer shall— (i) Consider and evaluate a contractor's written explanation for a reduced or an untimely payment when determining whether the reduced or untimely payment is justified; and

statement: One listed duty of the contracting officer is to determine that a history of unjustified reduced or untimely payments has occurred when the contractor has reported three or more occasions of unjustified reduced or untimely payments under a single contract within a 12-month period.
quote: (ii) Determine that a history of unjustified reduced or untimely payments has occurred when the contractor has reported three or more occasions of unjustified reduced or untimely payments under a single contract within a 12-month period

statement: Contractors shall be afforded up to 14 calendar days from the date of notification of availability of the past performance evaluation to submit comments, rebutting statements, or additional information.
quote: Contractors shall be afforded up to 14 calendar days from the date of notification of availability of the past performance evaluation to submit comments, rebutting statements, or additional information.

statement: Agencies shall provide for review at a level above the contracting officer to consider disagreements between the parties regarding the evaluation, and the ultimate conclusion on the performance evaluation is a decision of the contracting agency.
quote: Agencies shall provide for review at a level above the contracting officer to consider disagreements between the parties regarding the evaluation. The ultimate conclusion on the performance evaluation is a decision of the contracting agency.

statement: Past performance evaluations, including any contractor-submitted information, become available for source selection officials not later than 14 days after the date on which the contractor is notified of the evaluation's availability for comment.
quote: These evaluations, including any contractor-submitted information (with indication whether agency review is pending), become available for source selection officials not later than 14 days after the date on which the contractor is notified of the evaluation's availability for comment.

statement: Agencies shall use the past performance information in CPARS that is within three years of the completion of performance of the evaluated contract or order, or within six years for construction and architect-engineer contracts.
quote: Agencies shall use the past performance information in CPARS that is within three years (six for construction and architect-engineer contracts) of the completion of performance of the evaluated contract or order

statement: The Government will maintain surveillance of contractor performance as necessary to protect its interests, and when the contracting office retains a contract for administration the contracting officer administering the contract shall determine the extent of surveillance.
quote: The Government will maintain surveillance of contractor performance as necessary to protect its interests. When the contracting office retains a contract for administration, the contracting officer administering the contract shall determine the extent of surveillance.

statement: The contract administration office determines the extent of production surveillance on the basis of the criticality assigned by the contracting officer to the supplies or services and consideration of a list of factors.
quote: The contract administration office determines the extent of production surveillance on the basis of (1) the criticality (degree of importance to the Government) assigned by the contracting officer (see 42.1105) to the supplies or services and (2) consideration of the following factors:

statement: The factors the contract administration office considers for the extent of production surveillance include contract requirements for reporting production progress and performance, the contract performance schedule and the contractor's production plan.
quote: (2) consideration of the following factors: (i) Contract requirements for reporting production progress and performance. (ii) The contract performance schedule. (iii) The contractor's production plan.

statement: The list of production surveillance factors in the section continues with the contractor's history of contract performance, the contractor's experience with the contract supplies or services, the contractor's financial capability and any supplementary written instructions from the contracting office.
quote: (iv) The contractor's history of contract performance. (v) The contractor's experience with the contract supplies or services. (vi) The contractor's financial capability. (vii) Any supplementary written instructions from the contracting office.

statement: Contracts at or below the simplified acquisition threshold should not normally require production surveillance.
quote: (b) Contracts at or below the simplified acquisition threshold should not normally require production surveillance.

statement: Contracting officers shall assign a criticality designator to each contract in the space for designating the contract administration office, with listed criteria.
quote: Contracting officers shall assign a criticality designator to each contract in the space for designating the contract administration office, as follows:

statement: Criticality designator A covers critical contracts, including DX-rated contracts, contracts citing the authority for unusual and compelling urgency, and contracts for major systems.
quote: Criterion A Critical contracts, including DX-rated contracts (see subpart 11.6), contracts citing the authority in 6.302-2 (unusual and compelling urgency), and contracts for major systems.

statement: One listed pair of designators is B, for contracts other than those designated A for items needed to maintain a Government or contractor production or repair line, to preclude out-of-stock conditions or to meet user needs for nonstock items, and C, for all contracts other than those designated A or B.
quote: B Contracts (other than those designated “A”) for items needed to maintain a Government or contractor production or repair line, to preclude out-of-stock conditions or to meet user needs for nonstock items. C All contracts other than those designated “A” or “B.”

statement: When information on contract performance status is needed, contracting officers may require contractors to submit production progress reports.
quote: When information on contract performance status is needed, contracting officers may require contractors to submit production progress reports (see 42.1107(a)).

statement: Reporting requirements shall be limited to that information essential to Government needs and shall take maximum advantage of data output generated by contractor management systems.
quote: Reporting requirements shall be limited to that information essential to Government needs and shall take maximum advantage of data output generated by contractor management systems.

statement: The contract administration office may at any time initiate a report to advise the contracting officer, and the inventory manager if one is designated in the contract, of any potential or actual delay in performance.
quote: The contract administration office may at any time initiate a report to advise the contracting officer (and the inventory manager, if one is designated in the contract) of any potential or actual delay in performance.

statement: Advice of any potential or actual delay in performance shall be in writing, be provided in sufficient time for the contracting officer to take necessary action, and provide a definite recommendation, if action is appropriate.
quote: of any potential or actual delay in performance. This advice shall (1) be in writing, (2) be provided in sufficient time for the contracting officer to take necessary action, and (3) provide a definite recommendation, if action is appropriate.

statement: The contracting officer should reject supplies or services not conforming in all respects to contract requirements.
quote: The contracting officer should reject supplies or services not conforming in all respects to contract requirements (see 46.102).

statement: The contracting officer ordinarily must give the contractor an opportunity to correct or replace nonconforming supplies or services when this can be accomplished within the required delivery schedule.
quote: The contracting officer ordinarily must give the contractor an opportunity to correct or replace nonconforming supplies or services when this can be accomplished within the required delivery schedule.

statement: Unless the contract specifies otherwise, correction or replacement must be without additional cost to the Government.
quote: Unless the contract specifies otherwise (as may be the case in some cost-reimbursement contracts), correction or replacement must be without additional cost to the Government.

statement: In situations not covered by the correct-or-replace paragraph, the contracting officer ordinarily must reject supplies or services when the nonconformance is critical or major or the supplies or services are otherwise incomplete.
quote: In situations not covered by paragraph (b) of this section, the contracting officer ordinarily must reject supplies or services when the nonconformance is critical or major or the supplies or services are otherwise incomplete.

statement: The contracting officer may determine, in circumstances such as reasons of economy or urgency, that acceptance or conditional acceptance of supplies or services is in the best interest of the Government.
quote: However, there may be circumstances (e.g., reasons of economy or urgency) when the contracting officer determines acceptance or conditional acceptance of supplies or services is in the best interest of the Government.

statement: Before making a decision to accept, the contracting officer must obtain the concurrence of the activity responsible for the technical requirements of the contract and, where health factors are involved, of the responsible health official of the agency concerned.
quote: Before making a decision to accept, the contracting officer must, obtain the concurrence of the activity responsible for the technical requirements of the contract and, where health factors are involved, of the responsible health official of the agency concerned.

statement: If the nonconformance is minor, the cognizant contract administration office may make the determination to accept or reject, except where this authority is withheld by the contracting office of the contracting activity.
quote: If the nonconformance is minor, the cognizant contract administration office may make the determination to accept or reject, except where this authority is withheld by the contracting office of the contracting activity.

statement: To assist in making a determination, the contract administration office may establish a joint contractor-contract administrative office review group, and acceptance of supplies and services with critical or major nonconformances is outside the scope of the review group.
quote: To assist in making this determination, the contract administration office may establish a joint contractor-contract administrative office review group. Acceptance of supplies and services with critical or major nonconformances is outside the scope of the review group.

statement: When supplies or services are accepted with critical or major nonconformances as authorized in the acceptance paragraph, the contracting officer must modify the contract to provide for an equitable price reduction or other consideration.
quote: When supplies or services are accepted with critical or major nonconformances as authorized in paragraph (c) of this section, the contracting officer must modify the contract to provide for an equitable price reduction or other consideration.

statement: In the case of conditional acceptance, amounts withheld from payments generally should be at least sufficient to cover the estimated cost and related profit to correct deficiencies and complete unfinished work.
quote: In the case of conditional acceptance, amounts withheld from payments generally should be at least sufficient to cover the estimated cost and related profit to correct deficiencies and complete unfinished work.

statement: Notices of rejection must include the reasons for rejection and be furnished promptly to the contractor.
quote: Notices of rejection must include the reasons for rejection and be furnished promptly to the contractor.

statement: The notice of rejection must be in writing if the supplies or services have been rejected at a place other than the contractor's plant, if the contractor persists in offering nonconforming supplies or services for acceptance, or if delivery or performance was late without excusable cause.
quote: The notice must, be in writing if— (1) The supplies or services have been rejected at a place other than the contractor's plant; (2) The contractor persists in offering nonconforming supplies or services for acceptance; or (3) Delivery or performance was late without excusable cause.

statement: The contracting officer shall provide disposition instructions for counterfeit or suspect counterfeit items in accordance with agency policy, and agency policy may require the contracting officer to direct the contractor to retain such items for investigative or evidentiary purposes.
quote: The contracting officer shall provide disposition instructions for counterfeit or suspect counterfeit items in accordance with agency policy. Agency policy may require the contracting officer to direct the contractor to retain such items for investigative or evidentiary purposes.

statement: Except as provided in the exclusions paragraph, the contracting officer shall insert the reporting nonconforming items clause in solicitations and contracts in the listed cases.
quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.246-26, Reporting Nonconforming Items, in solicitations and contracts—as follows:

statement: One listed case for inserting the clause is an acquisition that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and is by, or for, the Department of Defense of electronic parts or end items, components, parts, or materials containing electronic parts, whether or not covered in the preceding listed case.
quote: for an acquisition that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and is by, or for, the Department of Defense of electronic parts or end items, components, parts, or materials containing electronic parts, whether or not covered in paragraph (a)(1) of this section;

statement: The contracting officer shall not insert the reporting nonconforming items clause when acquiring commercial products and commercial services using part 12 procedures, which is one of two listed exclusions.
quote: The contracting officer shall not insert the clause at 52.246-26, Reporting Nonconforming Items, in solicitations and contracts when acquiring— (1) Commercial products and commercial services using part 12 procedures; or

statement: If required by agency policy, the contracting officer may modify the clause, but only to change the responsibility for the contractor to submit reports to the agency rather than to the Government-Industry Data Exchange Program.
quote: If required by agency policy, the contracting officer may modify paragraph (b)(4) of the clause at 52.246-26, but only to change the responsibility for the contractor to submit reports to the agency rather than to Government-Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP),

statement: Where the contracting officer modifies the clause to change the responsibility for submitting reports, the agency instead of the contractor submits reports to the Government-Industry Data Exchange Program within the mandatory 60 days.
quote: but only to change the responsibility for the contractor to submit reports to the agency rather than to Government-Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP), so that the agency instead of the contractor submits reports to GIDEP within the mandatory 60 days.

statement: Contractors shall perform all contracts, so far as practicable, without using overtime, particularly as a regular employment practice, except when lower overall costs to the Government will result or when it is necessary to meet urgent program needs.
quote: Contractors shall perform all contracts, so far as practicable, without using overtime, particularly as a regular employment practice, except when lower overall costs to the Government will result or when it is necessary to meet urgent program needs.

statement: Approval of the use of overtime may be granted by an agency approving official after determining in writing that overtime is necessary to meet essential delivery or performance schedules, which is one of the listed purposes.
quote: Approval of the use of overtime may be granted by an agency approving official after determining in writing that overtime is necessary to— (1) Meet essential delivery or performance schedules;

statement: A biennial anniversary date is listed for a multiple year contract if the contract is not subject to annual appropriations and its proposed term exceeds 2 years, unless otherwise advised by the Wage and Hour Division.
quote: (2) Biennial anniversary date if the contract is not subject to annual appropriations and its proposed term exceeds 2 years—unless otherwise advised by the Wage and Hour Division.

statement: Approval by the designated official of the use and total dollar amount of overtime is required before an amount is included in the overtime premiums clause.
quote: Approval by the designated official of use and total dollar amount of overtime is required before inclusion of an amount in paragraph (a) of the clause at 52.222-2, Payment for Overtime Premiums.

statement: Contracting officer approval of payment of overtime premiums is required for time-and-materials and labor-hour contracts.
quote: Contracting officer approval of payment of overtime premiums is required for time-and-materials and labor-hour contracts

statement: No approvals are required for paying overtime premiums under other types of contracts.
quote: No approvals are required for paying overtime premiums under other types of contracts.

statement: The contracting officer shall include the overtime premiums clause in solicitations and contracts when a cost-reimbursement contract is contemplated and the contract amount is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold, unless an exception stated in the same sentence applies.
quote: The contracting officer shall include the clause at 52.222-2, Payment for Overtime Premiums, in solicitations and contracts when a cost-reimbursement contract is contemplated and the contract amount is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold; unless

statement: The overtime premiums clause is not required when a cost-reimbursement contract for operation of vessels is contemplated or a cost-plus-incentive-fee contract is contemplated that will provide a swing from the target fee of at least plus or minus 3 percent and a contractor's share of at least 10 percent.
quote: unless (a) a cost-reimbursement contract for operation of vessels is contemplated, or (b) a cost-plus-incentive-fee contract that will provide a swing from the target fee of at least plus or minus 3 percent and a contractor's share of at least 10 percent is contemplated.

statement: Certain contracts contain a clause specifying that no laborer or mechanic doing any part of the work shall be required or permitted to work more than 40 hours in any workweek unless paid for all such overtime hours at not less than one and one-half times the basic rate of pay.
quote: that certain contracts contain a clause specifying that no laborer or mechanic doing any part of the work contemplated by the contract shall be required or permitted to work more than 40 hours in any workweek unless paid for all such overtime hours at not less than 11⁄2 times the basic rate of pay.

statement: When an overtime computation discloses underpayments, the responsible contractor or subcontractor must pay the affected employee any unpaid wages and pay liquidated damages to the Government.
quote: When an overtime computation discloses underpayments, the responsible contractor or subcontractor must pay the affected employee any unpaid wages and pay liquidated damages to the Government.

statement: Liquidated damages must be assessed at the rate specified in the cited regulation per affected employee for each calendar day on which the employer required or permitted the employee to work in excess of the standard workweek of 40 hours without paying overtime wages required by the statute.
quote: must assess liquidated damages at the rate specified at 29 CFR 5.5(b)(2) per affected employee for each calendar day on which the employer required or permitted the employee to work in excess of the standard workweek of 40 hours without paying overtime wages required by the statute.

statement: The contracting officer inserts the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards clause in solicitations and contracts, including basic ordering agreements, when the contract may require or involve the employment of laborers or mechanics.
quote: Insert the clause at 52.222-4, Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards—Overtime Compensation, in solicitations and contracts (including, for this purpose, basic ordering agreements) when the contract may require or involve the employment of laborers or mechanics.

statement: One listed group of cases in which the clause is not included covers solicitations and contracts valued at or below $200,000, for commercial products and commercial services, and for transportation or the transmission of intelligence.
quote: However, do not include the clause in solicitations and contracts— (a) Valued at or below $200,000; (b) For commercial products and commercial services; (c) For transportation or the transmission of intelligence;

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Service Contract Labor Standards clause in solicitations and contracts, except as provided in the listed exceptions paragraph, if the contract is subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute and meets a listed condition, one of which is that the contract is over $2,500.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.222-41, Service Contract Labor Standards, in solicitations and contracts (except as provided in paragraph (a)(2) of this section) if the contract is subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute and is— (i) Over $2,500;

statement: A contract subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute meets the listed condition either by being over $2,500 or by being for an indefinite dollar amount where the contracting officer does not know in advance that the contract amount will be $2,500 or less.
quote: if the contract is subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute and is— (i) Over $2,500; or (ii) For an indefinite dollar amount and the contracting officer does not know in advance that the contract amount will be $2,500 or less.

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Statement of Equivalent Rates for Federal Hires clause in solicitations and contracts if the contract amount is expected to be over $2,500 and the Service Contract Labor Standards statute is applicable.
quote: (b) The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.222-42, Statement of Equivalent Rates for Federal Hires, in solicitations and contracts if the contract amount is expected to be over $2,500 and the Service Contract Labor Standards statute is applicable.

statement: The contracting officer shall obtain wage determinations for each new service solicitation and contract in excess of $2,500, which is one of the listed service contracts.
quote: The contracting officer shall obtain wage determinations for the following service contracts: (a) Each new solicitation and contract in excess of $2,500.

statement: Item (b) of the list in the section on obtaining wage determinations is each contract modification which brings the contract above $2,500 and either extends the existing contract pursuant to an option clause or otherwise or changes the scope of the contract whereby labor requirements are affected significantly.
quote: (b) Each contract modification which brings the contract above $2,500 and— (1) Extends the existing contract pursuant to an option clause or otherwise; or (2) Changes the scope of the contract whereby labor requirements are affected significantly.

statement: One listed service contract for which the contracting officer shall obtain wage determinations is each multiple year contract in excess of $2,500, upon the annual anniversary date if the contract is subject to annual appropriations.
quote: (c) Each multiple year contract in excess of $2,500 upon— (1) Annual anniversary date if the contract is subject to annual appropriations

statement: One listed exclusion from inserting the clause is the acquisition of medical devices that are subject to the Food and Drug Administration reporting requirements.
quote: (2) Medical devices that are subject to the Food and Drug Administration reporting requirements at 21 CFR 803.

statement: One listed duty of contracting officers is to designate and authorize, in writing and in accordance with agency procedures, a COR, within the scope that the same list item sets out.
quote: (d) Designate and authorize, in writing and in accordance with agency procedures, a contracting officer's representative (COR)
note: The scope and the exception in the same list item are carried by CL-OPM-0004.

statement: One listed attribute of a COR is that the COR may not be delegated responsibility to perform functions that have been delegated to a contract administration office, but may be assigned some duties by the contracting officer.
quote: (4) May not be delegated responsibility to perform functions that have been delegated under 42.202 to a contract administration office, but may be assigned some duties at 42.302 by the contracting officer;

statement: Ratification means the act of approving an unauthorized commitment by an official who has the authority to do so.
quote: Ratification, as used in this subsection, means the act of approving an unauthorized commitment by an official who has the authority to do so.

statement: Agencies should take positive action to preclude, to the maximum extent possible, the need for ratification actions.
quote: Agencies should take positive action to preclude, to the maximum extent possible, the need for ratification actions.

statement: Although the section provides ratification procedures for cases where ratification of an unauthorized commitment is necessary, those procedures may not be used in a manner that encourages such commitments being made by Government personnel.
quote: Although procedures are provided in this section for use in those cases where the ratification of an unauthorized commitment is necessary, these procedures may not be used in a manner that encourages such commitments being made by Government personnel.

statement: Agencies should process unauthorized commitments using the ratification authority of the subsection instead of referring such actions to the Government Accountability Office for resolution.
quote: Agencies should process unauthorized commitments using the ratification authority of this subsection instead of referring such actions to the Government Accountability Office for resolution.

statement: Unauthorized commitments that would involve claims subject to resolution under the Contract Disputes chapter of title 41 of the United States Code should be processed in accordance with FAR subpart 33.2, Disputes and Appeals.
quote: Unauthorized commitments that would involve claims subject to resolution under 41 U.S.C. chapter 71, Contract Disputes, should be processed in accordance with subpart 33.2, Disputes and Appeals.

statement: One listed limitation on authorization of class deviations by agency officials is that an agency official who may authorize one shall, before doing so, consult with the chairperson of the Civilian Agency Acquisition Council, unless the official determines that urgency precludes such consultation.
quote: (1) An agency official who may authorize a class deviation, before doing so, shall consult with the chairperson of the Civilian Agency Acquisition Council (CAA Council), unless that agency official determines that urgency precludes such consultation.

statement: For NASA, class deviations shall be controlled and approved by the Assistant Administrator for Procurement.
quote: (c) For NASA, class deviations shall be controlled and approved by the Assistant Administrator for Procurement.

statement: For civilian agencies other than NASA, a request for a deviation required to comply with a treaty or an executive agreement that is not authorized by the treaty and executive agreement paragraphs of the section shall be processed through the FAR Secretariat to the Civilian Agency Acquisition Council.
quote: (e) For civilian agencies other than NASA, if a deviation required to comply with a treaty or an executive agreement is not authorized by paragraph (b) or (c) of this section, then the request for deviation shall be processed through the FAR Secretariat to the Civilian Agency Acquisition Council.

statement: Maximum benefits of a postaward orientation will be realized when it is conducted promptly after award.
quote: (d) Maximum benefits will be realized when orientation is conducted promptly after award.

statement: A postaward orientation is not a substitute for the contractor's fully understanding the work requirements at the time offers are submitted, nor is it to be used to alter the final agreement arrived at in any negotiations leading to contract award.
quote: However, it is not a substitute for the contractor's fully understanding the work requirements at the time offers are submitted, nor is it to be used to alter the final agreement arrived at in any negotiations leading to contract award.

statement: Agencies shall not evaluate performance for contracts awarded under FAR subpart 8.7.
quote: (h) Agencies shall not evaluate performance for contracts awarded under Subpart 8.7.

statement: Agencies shall prepare and submit all past performance evaluations electronically in CPARS.
quote: Agencies shall prepare and submit all past performance evaluations electronically in CPARS

statement: Past performance evaluations for classified contracts and special access programs shall not be reported in CPARS, but will be reported as stated in the subpart and in accordance with agency procedures.
quote: Past performance evaluations for classified contracts and special access programs shall not be reported in CPARS, but will be reported as stated in this subpart and in accordance with agency procedures.

statement: Three listed payment or nonpayment situations that are not considered unjustified are a contract dispute on performance, a partial payment made for amounts not in dispute, and a payment reduced due to past overpayments.
quote: The following payment or nonpayment situations are not considered to be unjustified: (A) There is a contract dispute on performance. (B) A partial payment is made for amounts not in dispute. (C) A payment is reduced due to past overpayments.

statement: Two further listed situations that are not considered unjustified are an administrative mistake and late performance by the subcontractor that leads to later payment by the prime contractor.
quote: (D) There is an administrative mistake. (E) Late performance by the subcontractor leads to later payment by the prime contractor.

statement: After the contracting officer determines the liquidated damages and the contractor makes appropriate payments, any remaining assessments are disbursed in accordance with agency procedures.
quote: After the contracting officer determines the liquidated damages and the contractor makes appropriate payments, disburse any remaining assessments in accordance with agency procedures.

statement: One listed case for inserting the reporting nonconforming items clause is an acquisition by any agency, including the Department of Defense, of any items that are subject to higher-level quality standards in accordance with the higher-level contract quality requirement clause.
quote: (1) For an acquisition by any agency, including the Department of Defense, of— (i) Any items that are subject to higher-level quality standards in accordance with the clause at 52.246-11, Higher-Level Contract Quality Requirement;

statement: The first listed case for inserting the reporting nonconforming items clause also covers any items that the contracting officer, in consultation with the requiring activity, determines to be critical items for which use of the clause is appropriate.
quote: (ii) Any items that the contracting officer, in consultation with the requiring activity determines to be critical items for which use of the clause is appropriate;

statement: A further listed case for inserting the reporting nonconforming items clause is the acquisition of services, if the contractor will furnish, as part of the service, any items that meet the criteria specified in the first two listed cases.
quote: or (3) For the acquisition of services, if the contractor will furnish, as part of the service, any items that meet the criteria specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (a)(2) of this section.

statement: Two further listed purposes of approved overtime are to make up for delays beyond the control and without the fault or negligence of the contractor and to eliminate foreseeable extended production bottlenecks that cannot be eliminated in any other way.
quote: (2) Make up for delays beyond the control and without the fault or negligence of the contractor; or (3) Eliminate foreseeable extended production bottlenecks that cannot be eliminated in any other way.

statement: Promptness in giving the notice of rejection is essential because, if timely nature of rejection is not furnished, acceptance may in certain cases be implied as a matter of law.
quote: Promptness in giving this notice is essential because, if timely nature of rejection is not furnished, acceptance may in certain cases be implied as a matter of law.

statement: Except for the exempt contracts, for DoD cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts of $50 million or more, the earned value management system must comply with the EIA-748 guidelines.
quote: For cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts valued at $50 million or more, the clause at 252.234-7999, Earned Value Management System, requires
note: Codified DFARS 234.201(1)(i) (S-0010) still says $20,000,000. Effective date is the memo's signature date; it says effective immediately. The (j) exemptions (contracts primarily for software, or awarded to nontraditional defense contractors) apply; the HCA may waive only the nontraditional-contractor exemption (pp. 6-7). Rev 1 supersedes 2026-O0011 of 2025-12-18, not stored, so whether these values started then is unconfirmed.

statement: Except for the exempt contracts, for DoD cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts of $100 million or more, the contractor must have an earned value management system the cognizant agency has determined compliant.
quote: For cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts valued at $100 million or more, the clause at 252.234-7999, Earned Value Management System, requires the contractor to have an earned value management system
note: Codified DFARS 234.201(1)(ii) (S-0010) still says $50,000,000. The (j) exemptions (contracts primarily for software, or awarded to nontraditional defense contractors) apply; the HCA may waive only the nontraditional-contractor exemption (pp. 6-7). Rev 1 supersedes 2026-O0011 of 2025-12-18, not stored, so whether these values started then is unconfirmed.

statement: DoD does not apply the earned value management system requirement to contracts primarily for software or to contracts awarded to nontraditional defense contractors.
quote: Do not apply this subpart to contracts— (i) Primarily for software, including those using a software acquisition pathway in accordance with DoD Instruction 5000.87, Operation of the Software Acquisition Pathway; or (ii) Awarded to nontraditional defense contractors.
note: The waiver of the nontraditional-contractor exemption is (j)(2); see CL-PRG-0004. Codified DFARS 234.201 (S-0010) has no such exemption.

statement: The head of the contracting activity may waive only the DoD earned value management exemption for nontraditional defense contractors, by written determination that applying the requirement is in DoD's best interest; the authority may be delegated no lower than the chief of the contracting office.
quote: The head of the contracting activity may waive the exemption relating to nontraditional defense contractors by written determination
note: The software exemption in (j)(1)(i) has no waiver. Codified DFARS 234.201 (S-0010) has no such exemption or waiver.

statement: The contractor must use an earned value management system that complies with the ANSI/EIA-748 earned value management system guidelines.
quote: An Earned Value Management System (EVMS) that complies with the EVMS guidelines in the American National Standards Institute/Electronic Industries Alliance Standard 748, Earned Value Management Systems (ANSI/EIA-748)

statement: Management procedures must provide for generating timely, reliable, and verifiable information for the Contract Performance Report and Integrated Master Schedule.
quote: Management procedures that provide for generation of timely, reliable, and verifiable information for the Contract Performance Report (CPR) and the Integrated Master Schedule (IMS)

statement: For a contract valued at $50 million or more, the contractor must use an earned value management system determined acceptable by the Cognizant Federal Agency.
quote: If this contract has a value of $50 million or more, the Contractor shall use an EVMS that has been determined to be acceptable by the Cognizant Federal Agency (CFA).

statement: The section opened for this topic is the guide's organization guideline on defining the work breakdown structure, labelled in the source as an EIA standard guideline.
quote: GUIDELINE 1: DEFINE THE WORK BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE EVMS Category: Organization EIA Standard Guideline: 2.1a
note: The printed source is page text from the DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide, so no codified or RFO citation is recorded for it.

statement: The guideline requires the contractor to define the authorized work elements for the program, and records that a product-oriented work breakdown structure tailored for effective internal management control is commonly used for that purpose.
quote: Define the authorized work elements for the program. A product-oriented work breakdown structure, tailored for effective internal management control, is commonly used in this process.

statement: The work breakdown structure is a product-oriented, hierarchical breakdown of the program requirements that includes all program elements, such as hardware, software, services, data or facilities.
quote: The WBS is a product-oriented, hierarchical breakdown of the program requirements. The WBS includes all program elements (e.g., hardware, software, services, data, or facilities)

statement: The work breakdown structure must also include all subcontracted work scope.
quote: The WBS must also include all subcontracted work scope.

statement: The contractor must extend the contract work breakdown structure to a level needed for effective internal management control, and this level should not be an arbitrary level established across the program.
quote: In all cases, the contractor must extend the contract WBS to a level needed for effective internal management control. This should not be an arbitrary level established across the program.

statement: Cost collection requirements, such as cost and software data reporting, may require a different reporting structure than the work breakdown structure used in the earned value management system for program management.
quote: Cost collection requirements, such as Cost and Software Data Reporting (CSDR), may require a different reporting structure other than the WBS used in the Earned Value Management System (EVMS)

statement: A single product-oriented work breakdown structure is used for a given contract and extends to the level necessary for management action, comprising all contract work scope including subcontracted and intercompany scope.
quote: A single product-oriented WBS is used for a given contract and extends to the level necessary for management action. The WBS comprises all contract work scope, including subcontracted and intercompany scope, to levels needed for effective internal management control.

statement: The section opened for this topic is the guide's organization guideline on defining the program organizational breakdown structure, labelled in the source as an EIA standard guideline.
quote: GUIDELINE 2: DEFINE PROGRAM ORGANIZATIONAL BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE EVMS Category: Organization EIA Standard Guideline: 2.1b
note: The printed source is page text from the DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide, so no codified or RFO citation is recorded for it.

statement: The guideline requires the contractor to identify the program organizational structure, including the major subcontractors, responsible for accomplishing the authorized work, and to define the organizational elements where work will be planned and controlled.
quote: Identify the program organizational structure, including the major subcontractors, responsible for accomplishing the authorized work and define the organizational elements where work will be planned and controlled.

statement: The hierarchical alpha-numeric unique coding of the organization structure results in the organizational breakdown structure.
quote: The hierarchical alpha-numeric unique coding of the organization structure results in the Organizational Breakdown Structure (OBS).

statement: When designating the internal organization responsible for managing the program, the contractor must assign a program manager with sufficient authority and responsibility to ensure performance of the authorized work.
quote: When designating the internal organization responsible for managing the program efforts, the contractor must assign a program manager with sufficient authority and responsibility to ensure the performance of the authorized work.

statement: The manager assigned to subcontractor work must have full responsibility for the authorized work.
quote: The manager assigned to subcontractor work must have full responsibility for the authorized work.

statement: A single organizational structure exists that contains all organizational elements defined by the organizational breakdown structure, including major subcontractors and inter-company work, as necessary to execute the contract.
quote: A single organizational structure exists that contains all of the organizational elements as defined by the OBS, including major subcontractors and inter-company work, necessary to execute the contract.

statement: The organizational breakdown structure is defined with uniquely defined nomenclature.
quote: The OBS is defined with uniquely defined nomenclature

statement: The section opened for this topic is the guide's organization guideline on integrating the work breakdown structure and the organizational structure, labelled in the source as an EIA standard guideline.
quote: GUIDELINE 3: INTEGRATE WBS AND OBS TO CREATE CONTROL ACCOUNTS EVMS Category: Organization EIA Standard Guideline: 2.1c
note: The printed source is page text from the DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide, so no codified or RFO citation is recorded for it.

statement: The guideline requires the contractor to integrate the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure to identify management control points where responsibility is assigned to specific work scope.
quote: Integrate the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure to identify management control points where responsibility is assigned to specific work scope.

statement: The intersection of the lowest level work breakdown structure element and the organizational breakdown structure is the point at which control accounts are established.
quote: The intersection of the lowest level WBS element and the OBS is the point at which control account(s) are established.

statement: Control accounts should not be arbitrarily established at a single work breakdown structure level across the program.
quote: Control Accounts should not be arbitrarily established at a single WBS level across the program.

statement: Each control account has a corresponding control account manager, who is responsible for ensuring the accomplishment of work in the control account and is the focal point of management control.
quote: Each control account has a corresponding Control Account Manager (CAM), who is responsible for ensuring the accomplishment of work in the control account and is the focal point of management control.

statement: For management control purposes there may be one or more responsible organizations supporting a single work breakdown structure element, or multiple control accounts within one organizational element, driven by scope and exit criteria.
quote: For management control purposes, there may be one or more responsible organizations supporting a single WBS or multiple control accounts within one OBS element driven by scope and exit criteria

statement: For scope that cannot practically be identified to a control account, it is permissible to establish a summary level planning package above the control account level with an assigned manager.
quote: For scope that cannot practically be identified to a control account, it is permissible to establish a Summary Level Planning Package (SLPP) above the control account level with the assignment of an SLPP manager

statement: Each control account is assigned to a single organizational element directly responsible for the work identifiable to a single element of the work breakdown structure.
quote: Each control account is assigned to a single organizational element directly responsible for the work identifiable to a single element of the WBS.

statement: The section opened for this topic is the guide's organization guideline on integrating subsidiary management processes, labelled in the source as an EIA standard guideline.
quote: GUIDELINE 4: INTEGRATE SUBSIDIARY MANAGEMENT PROCESSES EVMS Category: Organization EIA Standard Guideline: 2.1d
note: The printed source is page text from the DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide, so no codified or RFO citation is recorded for it.

statement: The guideline requires the contractor to provide for the integration of the scheduling, budgeting, work authorization and cost accumulation processes with each other and, as appropriate, with the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure.
quote: Provide for the integration of the scheduling, budgeting, work authorization, and cost accumulation processes with each other and, as appropriate, the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure

statement: Integrating planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization and cost accumulation management processes provides the capability for establishing the performance measurement baseline, identifying work progress and collecting actual costs.
quote: The integration of planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization, and cost accumulation management processes provides the capability for establishing the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB), identifying work progress, and collecting actual costs

statement: Through coding structures that use unique identifiers and common data elements, or a simple mapping method, the contractor's planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization and cost accumulation processes are integrated.
quote: Through coding structures that use unique identifiers (UIDs) and common data elements or a simple mapping method, the contractor’s planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization, and cost accumulation processes are integrated.

statement: The earned value system must integrate subcontractor data.
quote: The system must integrate subcontractor data.

statement: The planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization and cost accumulation subsystems are integrated via a common and unique coding structure for all levels of the contract work breakdown structure and the organizational structure.
quote: The planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization, and cost accumulation subsystems are integrated via a common and unique coding structure for all levels of the Contract Work Breakdown Structure (CWBS) and the organizational structure.

statement: The fifth earned value guideline directs the contractor to identify in the schedule the physical products, milestones, technical performance goals, or other objective indicators used to measure progress.
quote: Identify, in the schedule, the physical products, milestones, technical performance goals, or other objective indicators that will be used to measure progress.

statement: The guideline ensures that program schedules establish and maintain a relationship between technical achievement and progress statusing, providing objective performance data that accurately reflects the progress of the work.
quote: To ensure program schedule(s) establish and maintain a relationship between technical achievement and progress statusing and provide objective performance data that accurately reflects the progress of the work.

statement: Interim measures are defined as the detailed schedule is established to ensure performance is measured as objectively as possible.
quote: Interim measures are defined as the detailed schedule is established to ensure performance is measured as objectively as possible.

statement: Identifying objective criteria linked to technical progress indicators ensures that performance assessments reflect the true technical performance of the program.
quote: Identifying objective criteria, linked to technical progress indicators, ensures performance assessments reflect the true technical performance of the program.

statement: Objective program milestones aligned with the accomplishment of technical requirements and goals are determined in advance, documented, and used to plan and measure progress.
